title: Revisiting the urban past virtually to enhance well-being for older adults
abstract: As development progresses, urban landmarks may be lost to history, resulting in the disconnection and isolation of older adults from their contemporary city. Huang and colleagues virtually reconstructed immersive past urban scenes from Hong Kong to understand the physiological and psychological effects and support mental health for aging populations.

title: Reversible Sn4+/Sn0 anode for high-energy-density flow batteries
abstract: Aqueous batteries offer a relatively safe, energy-dense means to store electrochemical energy. Tin is a promising anode material, due to its potential four-electron redox-active states and lack of dendrite formation. However, the irreversible electrochemical behaviour of the Sn4+/Sn2+ couple have limited high-capacity anode development. Here we achieve the reversible Sn4+/Sn2+ conversion, enabling a Sn4+/Sn0 anode for high-energy-density flow batteries. We accomplish this by adding iodide to highly soluble SnCl4 solutions at ratios that form SnCl62- and SnI62- intermediate complexes. SnI62- reduces reorganization energy during the electrochemical reaction of Sn4+/Sn2+, ensuring reversibility. SnCl62- imparts anolyte solubility. The redox peak potential difference decreased from 978 mV (Cl-) to 97 mV (I-), with a substantial decrease to the electron transfer impedance decrease. Coupled with Br-/Br2, the assembled full battery showed 89% energy efficiency at 40 mA cm-2, 227 Ah l-1 anolyte capacity and 205 Wh l-1 anolyte energy density. Based on these studies, we developed a kilowatt-scale stack that can operate stably for over 1,000 h.

title: Unanticipated intermediates during isopenicillin N synthase catalysis identified by time-resolved X-ray free-electron laser studies
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Biosynthesis of penicillin and cephalosporin antibiotics involves the oxidation of the tripeptide δ-(
                    l
                    -α-aminoadipoyl)-
                    l
                    -cysteinyl-
                    d
                    -valine (ACV) to give the conformationally strained bicyclic penicillin ring system, as catalysed by the Fe(II)-dependent oxidase isopenicillin N synthase (IPNS). The structures of the precursors for the sequential β-lactam and thiazolidine ring forming steps in IPNS have remained elusive. Here we studied the reaction of anaerobic IPNS:Fe(II):ACV microcrystals with O
                    2
                    using time-resolved serial femtosecond crystallography and X-ray emission spectroscopy. High-resolution structures reveal that ACV cysteinyl oxidation produces a thioaldehyde that unexpectedly does not coordinate the iron centre. The use of deuterium-labelled ACV enabled the observation of a monocyclic β-lactam with restoration of the Fe–S bond. Together with mutagenesis, spectroscopic and computational studies, the results support Fe(IV)-mediated penicillin formation involving active-site water molecules. These findings provide structural insight into IPNS catalysis, inform on the wider Fe(II) oxygenase superfamily and highlight the power of X-ray free-electron laser methods for resolving transient enzymatic intermediates.

title: Energy efficiency and sustainability of desalination
abstract: Energy efficiency and environmental impacts are key aspects of desalination operations. This Review discusses the efficiency and impacts of membrane-based desalination approaches and identifies areas for further development.

title: Urban memory and mental health
abstract: To what extent does the memory of historic urban spaces benefit the mental health of lifelong residents? A new experimental study used multimodal psychophysiological measurements and revealed that urban memory could significantly improve mental health in older lifelong residents. This News & Views discusses the methodology and findings of this study to stimulate further research and practice on this critical and timely topic.

title: Limited agricultural gains but high flood risk from global wetland reclamation
abstract: As food demand increases, global wetlands are being reclaimed as croplands; however, these reclaimed croplands are not only less productive, but also face substantially higher flood exposure. This dual vulnerability highlights the urgency of balancing food security with wetland conservation.

title: Engineering biocomputability in living and material systems
abstract: Circuitry is increasingly being engineered into both living systems and biomaterials. This Review highlights shared biocomputational design principles across synthetic, nucleic acid and protein platforms, then explores how their convergence may enable truly living materials.

title: A global view of urban land subsidence and its changing trajectories
abstract: Urban land subsidence poses a widespread but poorly quantified threat to cities worldwide. This study generates 40-m-resolution land subsidence maps and trend estimates for 465 cities with populations above one million.

title: The spatial reach of mobility interactions in urban systems
abstract: Human mobility interactions describe how movements across locations collectively generate citywide spatial organization. This study introduces the spatial range exponent (ρ) to measure this organization and shows how it can be used to compare cities, track mobility reorganization during disruptions and connect urban mobility structure to public health outcomes.

title: Global patterns and temporal dynamics of urban subsidence
abstract: High-resolution satellite observations were analyzed to monitor subsidence across 465 cities worldwide. Urban subsidence was found to be widespread, with the most severe sinking occurring in Southern North America, Southeast Asia and West-Central Asia. Hotspots in Southeast and East Asia included a combination of accelerating and decelerating subsidence dynamics.

title: Flexibility technologies in clean energy systems
abstract: The transition to clean energy systems is increasing the need to balance variable supply and demand across timescales and sectors. This Review describes different technologies that can enable flexibility in energy systems and assesses trends in their global deployment.

abstract: The miniaturization of capacitors for advanced electronics requires dielectrics that balance high permittivity, low loss and stable temperature response. Now, a hierarchical machine learning approach is developed for the design of such materials. The resulting Bi–Ge co-substituted tungsten bronze ceramic exhibits balanced dielectric properties, enabling a substantial volume reduction of chip capacitors.

title: Atomic-scale spin sensing of a 2D d-wave altermagnet via helical tunneling
abstract: Altermagnets simultaneously possess momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting and zero net magnetization (1-6). Their defining crystalline symmetry connects opposite-spin sublattices in real space and imposes alternating spin polarization on the symmetry-related electronic states in momentum space (1-3). Identifying such an order and its associated spin response therefore calls for atomic-scale spin-sensitive measurements in both real and momentum space, an experimental milestone yet to be achieved. Here we show that the helical edge modes of the higher-order topological insulator α-Bi4Br4 can serve as a spin-selective scanning tunnelling microscopy probe of the two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetic order in the surface layer of KV2Se2O. Atomically registered mapping reveals the spatial relationship between the two V sublattices and a density-wave lattice modulation, as well as real-space patterns consistent with the checkerboard antiferromagnetic order. Field-dependent spectroscopy further finds opposite energy shifts of the unidirectional quasiparticle excitations extending along two orthogonal crystal axes and a predominantly out-of-plane magnetic response. In momentum space, spin-sensitive quasiparticle interference imaging reveals a bias-reversing d-wave anisotropy between the symmetry-paired X and Y valleys. These results provide converging evidence for two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetism on the surface of KV2Se2O and demonstrate helical-edge-mode tunnelling as a route for atomic-scale spin sensing in quantum materials.

title: Selective, Catalytic Oxidation of Polyethylene Surfaces
abstract: Polyethylene (PE) accounts for more than a quarter of all plastic produced, owing to its exceptional material properties and scalable production.1 However, pristine PE lacks critical properties, such as adhesion, that are needed for many additional commercial applications.2 Selective post-polymerization functionalization of PE can impart properties that are absent in the pristine polymer, but global functionalization in a uniform medium perturbs bulk properties.3–5 Here, we demonstrate catalytic functionalization of solid PE at a solid–liquid interface. The resulting materials possess enhanced surface properties while maintaining bulk properties, such as melting temperature or tensile strength. The method selectively converts methylene units to ketones with just 0.001 mol% iron catalyst below 80 °C with inexpensive oxidants. PE functionalized at the solid–liquid interface adheres to polar surfaces up to 90-fold more strongly than does pristine PE and up to 4-fold more strongly than does PE functionalized in a uniform medium at a comparable level. We demonstrate that the surface ketones can be modified to enhance adhesive strength further and that the augmented surface properties persist for longer than they do after other unselective functionalizations. Thus, selective C–H bond functionalization at the solid–liquid interface produces materials inaccessible by bulk functionalization methods or by traditional surface oxidations.

title: Sexual dimorphism in epidermal stem cell dynamics
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The epidermis is a stratified epithelium comprising proliferative basal cells and differentiated suprabasal cells that are continuously renewed throughout life. Conflicting theories have been proposed regarding the heterogeneity of the basal cell layer, with some studies proposing that all proliferative cells have self-renewal potential during homeostasis
                    1–5
                    . Meanwhile, others posit a model in which stem cell differentiation occurs through an intermediate transit-amplifying-like progenitor state with strictly limited proliferative potential
                    6–10
                    . Here, to determine the heterogeneity and pattern of cell fate, we performed intravital time-lapse imaging to track the fate of lineage-labelled cells in the skin interfollicular epidermis. Results from quantitative analyses of clonal dynamics support a two-compartment model of epidermal homeostasis, whereby basal cells are organized in a stem cell–transit-amplifying cell hierarchy. Critical to these conclusions was the discovery of sexual dimorphism in epidermal fate, with female mice showing a highly synchronized pattern of cell division, differentiation and delamination that contributes to accelerated wound healing. Single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling and clonal analyses of castrated mice revealed that male sex hormones promote stem cell differentiation and delamination. In summary, our study provides insight into the functional identity of the stem cell population and identifies sex-specific differences in the regulation of epidermal stem cells and transit-amplifying cell fate.

title: Interhemispheric monsoon dynamics over the past 450,000 years
abstract: The global monsoon system provides freshwater to much of Earth's biota, including its human population1. The Milankovitch theory predicts changes in Earth's solar insolation over geologic time, and these variations are expected to result in changes to the global monsoon2. Internal climate forcings, such as ice cover and sea surface temperatures, may also affect the system. However, few records of monsoon variability in the Southern Hemisphere over glacial-interglacial cycles exist to test our understanding of the factors that drive variations in the global monsoon. Here we show that monsoons in both the Southern and Northern Hemispheres vary with Milankovitch forcing, and with internal boundary conditions over the past 450,000 years. We present a record of South American Summer Monsoon (SASM) variability, based on speleothem oxygen-isotope data from the Amazon Basin. South American Summer Monsoon variability and that of a major Northern Hemisphere monsoon-that is, the Asian monsoon3,4-have been strikingly out of phase. However, we observe occasional synchronous behaviour in regions impacted by both monsoons. We identify a synchronicity threshold that is exceeded during ten events, including during glacial terminations. Comparison with palaeoclimatic forcing factors during these intervals indicates that greenhouse gas concentrations, cross-equatorial thermal gradients and sea surface temperatures in both the Atlantic and Pacific probably influence these events. This record demonstrates that the global monsoon can reorganize itself, especially during intervals of rapidly changing planetary boundary conditions.

title: The Molecular Logic of Platelet-Activating Factor (PAF)
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Platelet-activating factor (PAF) is a well-known if enigmatic lipid signal with important roles in inflammatory responses, allergic reactions, autoimmune diseases, and thrombotic cascades. Several lines of evidence suggest that our current model of PAF’s molecular mechanism is inadequate. This report describes a recontextualized model for PAF. The revised model embeds PAF in a plasmalogen-based molecular mechanism in which activation is a spontaneous chemical reaction triggered by environmental conditions that liberates a PAF receptor (PAF-R) agonist from a membrane-bound phospholipid. The active ligand subsequently undergoes a thermodynamically driven spontaneous rearrangement into an inactive isomer, a feature that controls response lifetime. The revised model is a molecule-autonomous set of transformations that create a response with spatial and temporal control. More generally the revised model’s congruence with a similar model for RORγt supports a picture in which plasmalogens form a part of the immune system that is separate from the cell-based innate and adaptive immune systems.

title: A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology
                    1,2
                    . Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism-like phenotypes
                    1,3,4
                    . However, the full landscape of microexons is not known, and the impact of genetic variation on these exons has not been systematically investigated. Here, through extensive transcriptome profiling, we detect hundreds of new microexons, including many with neuronal subtype-specific splicing patterns, and others that activate nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. Using machine learning, we define a sequence code predictive of neuronally spliced microexons and use this to identify critical regulatory elements surrounding the expanded microexon repertoire. This code further reveals genomic variants predicted to alter microexon splicing in individuals affected by autism, with rare variants having the strongest estimated impact. These variants are mostly detected in idiopathic individuals and are associated with autism status. They also converge on synaptic and other autism-linked genes, as well as genes not previously linked to autism. Our results collectively define an expanded repertoire of microexons, delineate their regulatory code, and pinpoint variants predicted to affect their splicing, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders.

title: Educational intervention can rewire village social networks
abstract: Social networks shape behaviour, affect information dissemination and undergird collective action. And they can be exploited in the design of interventions in these domains1-7. Although social networks obey fundamental principles, such as the degree distribution8,9, they can nevertheless evolve as ties form and break. Here, through a randomized controlled trial involving a total of 8,331 people in 110 remote Honduran villages, we evaluate the secondary effects of a 22-month public-health intervention1 on pre-existing social-network structure. We used a design in which a varying fraction of village households received the intervention, and villages in which no one received the intervention were used as the primary reference group. In 'low-dosage' villages (in which 5-30% of households received the intervention), people who received the intervention tended to sever ties with untreated individuals to whom they previously went for health advice. Conversely, in high-dosage villages (50-100%), treated individuals increased their ties. These average changes are explained mainly by tie dynamics; that is, treated-treated pairs persist and form new links, whereas treated-untreated ties dissolve. A mediation analysis indicates that absorption of health information increases the likelihood of tie formation and persistence. The rewiring patterns generally lasted for three years after the intervention ceased. Moreover, although the intervention delivered health information, it reshaped friendship and financial ties, not just health-advice connections. In aggregate, the introduction of a new information regime acted as a kind of social institution, rewiring individuals' connections even though the overall degree distribution of village-wide networks remained relatively stable.

title: Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning
abstract: Decision-makers rely on weather forecasts to plant crops, manage wildfires, allocate water and energy and prepare for weather extremes1-3. Today, such forecasts enjoy unprecedented accuracy as far as 2 weeks thanks to steady advances in physics-based dynamical models and data-driven artificial intelligence models4-10. However, model skill drops precipitously at subseasonal timescales (2-6 weeks ahead) due to compounding errors, systemic model biases and the chaotic nature of the atmosphere11-15. To counter this degradation, we introduce probabilistic bias correction, a machine learning framework that substantially reduces systematic error by learning to correct historical probabilistic forecasts. When applied to the leading dynamical and artificial intelligence models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), probabilistic bias correction doubles the modest subseasonal skill of the AI Forecasting System16 and improves the skill of the operationally debiased dynamical model17 for 91% of pressure, 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets. We designed probabilistic bias correction for operational deployment, and, in the 2025 real-time forecasting competition of ECMWF18, its global forecasts were the best for all weather variables and lead times, outperforming the dynamical models from six operational forecasting centres, an international dynamical multimodel ensemble, the AI Forecasting System of ECMWF and the forecasting systems of 34 teams worldwide. These probabilistic skill gains translate into more accurate prediction of extreme events and have the potential to improve agricultural planning, energy management and disaster preparedness in vulnerable communities19.

title: Jurassic flightless bird reveals early ecological diversity of avialans
abstract: The origin and early diversification of birds remain highly debated in vertebrate evolution. Although estimates of the evolutionary timescales suggest a Jurassic period radiation1,2, a profound scarcity of fossils from this period has hampered how the distinctive bird bauplan was assembled3-5. Selection for powered flight has been viewed as the primary driver of early avialan skeletal modifications3,6,7, attesting to the independent occurrences of aerodynamic features among paravian lineages8. Here we report on the discovery of a Late Jurassic avialan, Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, gen. et sp. nov., from the Zhenghe Fauna of southeastern China9. As one of the earliest diverging avialans, Y. yangyuanensis exhibits a striking mosaic of features, combining a mixture of avialan- and troodontid-like cranial characters, paired with derived postcranial traits and a deinonychosaur-like hyperextensible second pedal digit. Phylogenetically informed analyses show that Y. yangyuanensis possesses markedly short forelimbs-a condition present widely among non-avialan theropods. These findings provide strong evidence for a terrestrial, flightless lifestyle of Y. yangyuanensis. Our study demonstrates that evolution works intensively as exemplified by the occurrence of several, divergent ecological pathways being exploited in the initial diversification of birds.

title: Photonic half-semimetals with dual semimetal-insulator topology
abstract: Topological wave systems have largely evolved along two distinct paradigms: gapless topological semimetals and gapped topological insulators. While topological semimetals support bulk transport, they generally lack intrinsic selectivity among propagation channels; topological insulators enable robust transport but confine it to narrow interfaces, limiting spatial utilization. Here, we theoretically demonstrate and experimentally realize time-reversal-invariant spin-valley photonic half-semimetals (HSMs), which exhibit a dual semimetal-insulator topology within a single bulk band structure. In HSMs, the bandgap closes selectively in spin-valley space: for a given spin (valley), one valley (spin) is semimetallic while the other remains insulating. This coexistence of spin- and valley-resolved gapless and gapped band structures makes HSMs fundamentally distinct from both conventional semimetals and insulators. As a defining bulk phenomenon, an HSM functions as a spin-valley-locked beam splitter, intrinsically enabling valley-selective spin routing. Moreover, when four complementary HSMs are assembled into a periodic superlattice, the same dual topology enables reciprocal spin-valley-resolved multilane helical transport with 100% spatial utilization. These results establish HSMs as a platform for selective bulk wave control and multichannel topological transport beyond conventional topological phases.

title: Unified structural origin of functionality in spiral skyrmions revealed by 3D electron tomography
abstract: Ferroelectric skyrmions exhibit a range of emergent phenomena, including collective dynamics, negative capacitance, and a strong electric-field-induced second-harmonic generation response. However, three-dimensional (3D) atomic-scale configurations of skyrmions are unclarified yet, making the relationship between the physical functionalities and their underlying structural origin remains elusive. Here, using atomic-scale electron tomography, we experimentally resolve the 3D structure of polar skyrmion for the first time in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattice. On the basis of large-data image acquisition with more than 95,000 3D coordinates of atoms, we visualize that the core of the skyrmions exhibit an upward spiraling morphology. By quantitatively analyzing the ferroelectric polarization and lattice distortion, we uncover an unconventional decoupling between the two at the skyrmion wall, where the polarization is suppressed, accompanied by a local enhancement of tetragonality exceeding 5% at the center of the wall. This increased tetragonality modifies the local free-energy landscape, enhancing the negative-capacitance response and field sensitivity at the skyrmion wall. The polar skyrmion wall hosts a concentration of emergent physical properties, thereby providing a unified structural origin for the functionalities and physical behaviors of skyrmions. This work establishes a real space basis for understanding the physical properties of polar skyrmions.

title: Asymmetric Elongation of Uranyl within a Silver Nanocluster
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Confinement within nanoscale cavities can profoundly alter molecular structure and electronic properties, but this strategy has never been applied to inherently linear and symmetric uranyl cations (UO22+). Here, we report the first example of uranyl encapsulation within a self-assembled silver nanocluster, [UO2F5@Ag21(CCBut)14](BF4)3F (CCBut = 3,3-dimethyl-1-butynyl), abbreviated as UO2F5@Ag21. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals asymmetric elongation of the axial O ≡ U≡O bonds from the ideal symmetric value of 1.77 Å to 1.788(9) and 1.837(9) Å, respectively. Raman and IR spectroscopy show extreme redshifts of both symmetric and asymmetric stretching vibrations (ν1 down to 765 cm–1). Transient absorption spectroscopy further reveals an excited-state quenching process of the (UO2F5)3– guest driven by unique confinement. High-energy-resolved fluorescence detected X-ray absorption near edge structure (HERFD-XANES) at the U M4 edge demonstrates re-engineered 5f electronic states, with a shifted and broadened 5fσ* feature indicating reduced U≡O covalency. This work establishes nanoconfinement as a powerful new route to reshape the electronic structure and property of actinide-based materials.

title: Chemical Bonding Rules for Stacking-Sequence Stability in Bismuth Oxychloride Intergrowths and Their Consequences for Band Structure
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal oxyhalides are versatile materials, exhibiting properties relevant to photocatalysis, solid-state battery systems, ferromagnetism, multiferroics, and nonlinear optics. Here, mixed-metal oxyhalide intergrowths, layered materials formed by intercalating SrBi3O4Cl3 and Bi2GdO4Cl blocks along the c direction within a crystal, are reported. They are synthesized through a flux-based approach in which the SrBi3O4Cl3-to-Bi2GdO4Cl ratio can be precisely controlled. Despite the structural and compositional flexibility of such intergrowths, there is no general framework for predicting which local structural arrangements are preferred. Density functional theory combined with Bader charge analysis shows that preferred stacking sequences are those that minimize charge disproportionation across distinct chlorine environments, consistent with Pauling’s fifth rule, and we support this bonding-based framework through computational cation substitution that shifts the ionic-covalent balance of the metal–chloride bonding. With the preferred stacking arrangement established, this same system further reveals that intergrowth layering and Sr/Bi site occupancy modulate the interaction between the Bi3+ lone pair and anion p orbitals. Density functional theory calculations reveal that intergrowth formation destabilizes the O-2p orbitals, raising the valence band maximum for visible-light absorption, with the lone-pair interaction and layering-driven internal electrostatic field acting as competing effects on the resulting band gap. Significantly, this experimental-computational study establishes a transferable, bonding-based framework for stacking-sequence stability in layered oxyhalide intergrowths, while also clarifying how the same structural levers used to control stability can be tuned to engineer band structure.

title: Robust quasi-bound states in the continuum in bilayer terahertz metasurface with S4 point-group symmetry
abstract: Metasurface-based bound states in the continuum (BICs) enable exceptional spatiotemporal control of light and substantially enhance light–matter interactions, making them highly attractive for applications in sensing, nonlinear optics, and integrated photonics. However, conventional BICs in single-layer metasurfaces rely on in-plane symmetry and are highly susceptible to structural perturbations, offering limited design flexibility and constraining both their robustness and functional diversity. title: Deciphering Critical Transition for AKI Deterioration by STIfuse: Fusing Dynamic and Static Representations
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening condition with notably high in-hospital mortality, characterized by a three-phase progression: a relatively stable state (without imminent life threat), a critical pre-deterioration state (the time window which may be identified and in which timely intervention could prevent upcoming irreversible deterioration), and a deteriorated state (severe conditions such as death or rescue events). Accurate early prediction of AKI deterioration and deciphering the critical transition remain challenging because of complex, high-dimensional, noisy, and incomplete clinical data, as well as limited mechanistic understanding of disease progression. To solve this problem, we propose STIfuse (Spatiotemporal Information fusion), a unique dual-view framework that integrates deep learning (DL) and spatiotemporal information transformation (STI) based on Takens’ embedding theorem and critical slowing down (CSD) theory. The DL backbone encodes multi-dimensional static representations to capture structural dependencies, while the STI branch transforms high-dimensional spatial information into a low-dimensional dynamic representation. These views are fused by a multivariate Gaussian distribution: the means capture statistical levels for diagnosis, and the covariances reflect collective physiological fluctuations for early deterioration prediction. An optimal-transport-distance-based contrastive loss is employed to learn discriminative dynamic features between ˈcriticalˈ and ˈstableˈ states. Pretrained on the MIMIC-IV dataset and validated on five external cohorts (including MIMIC-III (with two independent cohorts), eICU, HiRID, and NWICU), STIfuse demonstrated superior performance in predicting 72-hour deterioration. Further analysis of single-cell multi-omics data study uncovered inflammatory cascades linking comorbidities to AKI. STIfuse provides an interpretable, robust and scalable framework for early warning of AKI deterioration prediction, highlighting its potential in utility and scalability for clinical foundation models.

title: Suppressing carbonate formation in alkaline CO 2 electrolysis
abstract: A dual-function porous layer suppresses carbonate formation by restricting electrolyte convection, enabling alkaline CO 2 electrolysis for 500 h with 80% C 2 -product selectivity at 2.30 V and the lowest energy cost reported to date.

title: Cross-Interface Diffusion-Driven Exsolution of Praseodymium Oxide Nanoparticles for Enabling Electrolysis at Industrially Relevant Temperatures in Protonic Ceramic Cells
abstract: Protonic ceramic electrolysis cells (PCECs) can unlock direct electrification of catalytic processes towards intensification and operation at intermediate temperatures (400-650 oC). A primary challenge however is the development of the...

title: Electrochemical energy conversion beyond Earth
abstract: Terrestrial electrochemical design implicitly relies on Earth-bound physics, such as gravity and natural convection. Beyond Earth, where these conditions no longer apply, we argue that designing with architecture, co-integrating electrochemical, thermal, and mechanical functions into a single structure, emerges as a primary physical variable rather than a downstream choice. Furthermore, additive manufacturing enables rapid structural iteration, allowing electrochemical energy conversion devices to be tailored to the strict operational demands of both space environments and resource-limited terrestrial applications.

title: Multiplexed live imaging deciphers nuclear force-driven chromatin dynamics and embryo development
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mechanical forces transmitted to the nucleus regulate chromatin organization and gene expression to guide cell fate transitions. However, how the forces dynamically reshape the genome in living systems remains unclear. Here, inspired by the visualization of perinuclear chromatin detachment under low tension, we develop a genetically encoded fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based nuclear tension sensor (NuTS) that directly quantifies forces transmitted into the nucleus through LINC complex proteins SUN1/2 and their effect on chromatin reorganization. NuTS enables high spatiotemporal mapping of forces across the nuclear envelope. Combined imaging of NuTS and lamina-associated domains (LADs) reveals that force fluctuations are coupled to LADs repositioning, and that a force of approximately 6 pN on SUN2 is required to maintain perinuclear chromatin anchoring. A drop below this threshold triggers lamin A phosphorylation at Ser22, which precedes and drives perinuclear chromatin dissociation and LAD reorganization by about 10 min. LINC-complex force transmission critically regulates cell migration and is essential for embryonic notochord development in vitro and in vivo. Our study establishes a mechanochemical framework linking nuclear forces to chromatin organization and function.

title: Catalytic Asymmetric 1,6-Diene Cyclization via Designed Carbocationic 5- and 6- exo Pathways
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Catalytic asymmetric electrophilic alkene functionalization provides a powerful strategy for the construction of complex chiral molecules. Despite significant progress in this field, the asymmetric functionalization of alkenes promoted by an electrophilic carbon species via an exo-cyclization mode remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a solution to this challenge: alkenes can undergo designed 5-exo- and 6-exo-carbocationic cyclizations to generate optically pure, complex chiral compounds with high enantio- and diastereoselectivities. In this approach, for 1,6-dienes bearing bulky sulfonamide or quaternary carbon linkers, one double bond of the substrate interacts with an external electrophile, such as a trifluoromethylthio, arylthio, alkylthio, or chlorine species, generating an electrophilic carbon species that promotes the transformation of 1,6-dienes under chiral indane-based chalcogenide catalysis. Notably, the reaction can be terminated by intramolecular nucleophiles via cis-addition or can be captured by various intermolecular nucleophiles. A diverse array of optically pure polycyclic and monocyclic compounds can be obtained, including 5-5-6 tricyclic N-heterocycles and pentasubstituted chiral cyclohexanes. The same strategy can also be efficiently applied to 6-endo cyclizations, leading to the formation of 6-6-6 tricyclic and monocyclic N-heterocycles. The resulting products can be readily converted to various other valuable compounds, further demonstrating the utility of this methodology. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to rationalize the observed selectivities, revealing that the preferential transition-state conformations lower the activation barriers for the desired cyclization pathways. This work offers a versatile platform for the synthesis of enantioenriched chiral scaffolds prevalent in bioactive molecules and pharmaceuticals, significantly expanding the scope of polyene cyclization chemistry.

title: Kinetic Programming of Heteromolecular Contacts in Boron- and Nitrogen-Containing π-Systems via External and Internal Cross-Seeding
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We establish a kinetic strategy for controlling the supramolecular copolymerization of boron- and nitrogen-containing π-electron systems by exploiting intramolecular hydrogen bonding in cystine-based dimeric diamides. Two dimeric diamides bearing solubilizing alkyl chains, DBB and DNN, were designed and synthesized by functionalization with planarized triarylborane (PTAB) and planarized triarylamine (PTAA) units, respectively. In low-polarity solvents, both molecules form one-dimensional nanostructures upon ultrasonication. Intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the two diamide units within the cystine framework suppresses spontaneous nucleation and generates metastable monomeric states, thereby providing a kinetic window for seeded supramolecular polymerization. Despite a difference of more than 10 kJ mol–1 between their Gibbs free energy changes for homopolymerization, external cross-seeding with preformed DBB seeds initiates the supramolecular polymerization of metastable DNN monomers. The resulting supramolecular copolymers exhibit long-lived emission arising from spatially confined interactions between the PTAB and PTAA units. The extent of heteromolecular contact formation can be modulated by switching between external and internal cross-seeding protocols. In the internal cross-seeding process, DBB assemblies are generated in situ in the presence of DNN monomers, enabling their incorporation during supramolecular growth and producing coassemblies with an enhanced contribution of heteromolecular excited-state interactions. These results demonstrate that kinetic control over nucleation and elongation enables pathway-dependent regulation of heteromolecular contacts in equimolar binary supramolecular polymers with markedly different homopolymerization propensities.

title: Group Theory-Guided Orbital Symmetry Engineering of cis -Quinacridone: From Symmetry-Forbidden to Dipole-Allowed Transitions for Efficient Narrowband Emissions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Although group theory is widely used to analyze symmetry and electronic transition selection rules in condensed matter physics and coordination chemistry, its use as a predictive design tool for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) remains largely unexplored. This is particularly important for highly symmetric emitters, where orbital-symmetry constraints can render the lowest-energy transition symmetry-forbidden. Herein, guided by quantum-chemical and group-theoretical analyses, we revisit the long-known cis- and trans-quinacridone isomers and reveal that the lowest-energy transition of cis-quinacridone (cis-QA) is symmetry-forbidden, resulting in a negligible transition dipole moment and intrinsically weak emission. We address this limitation through a group theory-guided orbital-symmetry engineering strategy based on carbonyl-to-imine transformation of the cis-QA skeleton. This targeted structural modification reorganizes the frontier orbital symmetry, converting the lowest-energy transition from symmetry-forbidden to dipole-allowed, while preserving the rigid, highly symmetric molecular framework and suppressing excited-state structural relaxation and vibronic coupling. The resulting cis-I2A2 derivatives exhibit high photoluminescence quantum yields (ΦPL) of 70–99% and narrow emission bandwidths with full-widths at half-maximum (fwhm’s) of 20–32 nm. An OLED based on cis-I2A2-3 delivers narrowband yellow electroluminescence with an emission maximum at 550 nm, a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 32.4%, and substantially mitigated efficiency roll-off relative to conventional cis-quinacridone emitters. This work establishes orbital-symmetry engineering as a rational strategy for decoupling orbital symmetry from overall molecular symmetry, providing a general approach to transforming intrinsically weak luminophores into efficient narrowband emitters.

title: Unlocking the Tertiary Nitrogen Effect in 3D Anisotropic Covalent Organic Frameworks to Achieve Record Iodine Capture under Industrial Conditions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Using porous adsorbents to achieve efficient capture of radioactive iodine from nuclear waste under industrial conditions remains a formidable challenge, since most adsorbents just exhibit a low iodine uptake under such conditions. We herein show two 3D [8 + 4]-assembled covalent organic frameworks (COFs, ECUT-COF-99 and ECUT-COF-100) for this challenging target. The two COFs feature a minimal-transitivity [3 4] flu-derived net, which allows anisotropic isoreticular expansion through a general sequential derived-net approach. ECUT-COF-100 was found to give an ultrahigh iodine uptake of 1.51 g/g under simulated industrial conditions (150 °C and 150 ppmv I2), 5.2-fold that of ECUT-COF-99 (0.29 g/g). Such performance also far exceeds all established organic adsorbents for this use. Mechanism studies reveal that nonaromatic tertiary nitrogen atoms allow for strong charge transfer from the lone-pair electrons of tertiary nitrogen to I2, leading to the formation of ionic iodides (I3– and I5–) and the N·+ radical cation and then fixing of ionic iodides by Coulomb interactions. This work not only provides a promising adsorbent with record iodine uptake for radioactive iodine capture from nuclear waste but also highlights a new insight into the tertiary nitrogen effect in 3D COFs for efficient iodine capture.

title: From active site dynamics to durable Ir-based aerogel: operando insights and flash calcination strategy for the oxygen evolution reaction in proton exchange membrane water electrolyser
abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) represents a cornerstone towards low-carbon energy transition. However, its deployment at large scale remains limited by two major challenges: (i) the scarcity of Ir-based...

title: Imaging of Electrochemically Programmed Single-Molecule Reactions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Single-molecule reactions reveal intrinsic heterogeneity that is obscured in ensemble measurements. However, most existing approaches rely on extreme dilution, ultrasmall solution volumes, or physical confinement to keep individual events sufficiently sparse. Here, we introduce electrochemically programmed single-molecule reactions (PSMR), a pulse-regulated strategy that shifts single-molecule electrochemistry from passive observation to active control. It converts continuous interfacial reactions to a sequence of short, repeatable reaction trials. By tailoring the pulse waveform, PSMR controls the driving force and duration of each reaction trial, thereby regulating the probability of single-molecule reactions, while the relaxation interval between pulses allows the interface to recover before the next trial. This coordinated control enables single-molecule reactions to be actively regulated under conventional solution volumes and reaction concentrations. By coupling individual reaction events to single-photon emission through electrogenerated chemiluminescence (ECL), we can directly count and image the reactions. The ultrashort reaction windows and relaxation periods suppress diffusion-layer buildup, thereby preserving sensitivity to local reaction kinetics, even at high overpotentials. Using this approach, individual Au nanoparticles were imaged over a broad potential range, and particles as small as 5 nm were distinguished from the substrate background. Sparse photon events were accumulated over repeated trials and further analyzed using localization- and fluctuation-based algorithms, enabling super-resolution mapping of reaction activity beyond the optical diffraction limit. PSMR therefore provides a framework for actively regulating, quantitatively imaging, and spatially mapping single-molecule electrochemical reactions at nanointerfaces, opening new opportunities for mechanistic studies and rational design across molecular electrochemistry, electrocatalysis, and energy conversion.

title: Clickable Photolabile Linkers for Convenient Immobilization and Light-Controlled Release of Substrates from Solid Support
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photolabile linkers (PLLs) enable spatiotemporal control over substrate release but often suffer from slow photorelease kinetics, low quantum yields, or limited functionalization options. Here, we report a family of heterobifunctional PLLs based on (3-hydroxy-5-alkoxynaphthalen-2-yl)methyl (NQMP) chromophores that combine rapid, high-yielding photochemical cleavage with orthogonal conjugation chemistries for efficient substrate immobilization and light-triggered release. Six heterobifunctional NQMP-based linkers bearing terminal acetylene, cyclooctyne, amine, carboxyl, allyl, and biotin groups were synthesized and employed for the immobilization of fluorescent dyes, acetylsalicylic acid, biotin, avidin, and doxorubicin on silica microspheres and mesoporous silica nanoparticles. Mild UV-A irradiation resulted in efficient release of the attached payloads while preserving the integrity of the solid support. Mesoporous silica nanoparticles provide high loading capacity and are suitable for light-controlled drug delivery. The modular design, excellent photochemical efficiency, orthogonal conjugation chemistries, and compatibility with diverse substrates make NQMP-based PLLs versatile tools for reversible surface functionalization, controlled cargo release, affinity capture, and photoresponsive drug delivery applications.

title: Reactivity and Selectivity of Photocatalytic Nitrate Reduction Reaction to Ammonia: Pt, Pd, Ir, and Rh Single Atoms on p-Type TiO2 Nanotubes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We present a systematic study of noble metal (Pt, Pd, Ir, and Rh) single-atom cocatalysts decorated on p-type and quantum-confined TiO2 nanotubes for photocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia. All single-atom cocatalysts were prepared through a reactive deposition using different metal precursors, resulting in a single-atom oxidation state (δ+) of δ ≈ 2. At a similar loading concentration (0.2–0.3 at%) and in the absence of any sacrificial agent, Pd single atoms exhibit the highest element-specific activity for ammonia production, while Pt single atoms display a prominent photocatalytic activity with a strong tendency of nitrite reduction toward ammonia. Rh single atoms achieve the highest ammonia selectivity, whereas Ir single atoms predominantly produce nitrite due to inhibited subsequent reduction. Comparisons with single atoms deposited on conventional TiO2 (P25) and with nanoparticles supported on the nanotubes reveal that both the semiconductor properties (quantum confinement effect and p-type conductivity) and the speciation of the cocatalyst (single atom) can significantly enhance activity and selectivity. These findings aid in establishing design principles for different single-atom catalysts toward efficient and selective photocatalytic nitrogen valorization.

title: Redox-Induced Polymeric Micelle-to-Coacervate Transition for Enhanced Endosomal Escape, Prolonged Drug Retention, and Improved Sequential Drug Delivery
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polymeric micelles (PMs) and coacervate microdroplets (CMs) are both promising delivery vehicles, yet each suffers from distinct limitations. The delivery efficiency of PMs is often hindered by factors, such as limited endosome escape and uncontrolled drug release. On the other hand, CMs are prone to coalescence and aging, which hamper long-term storage and systemic injection. Here, by employing an intracellular morphological transition strategy, these drawbacks can be efficiently addressed without compromising their inherent advantages. The system exists as nanosized PMs during storage and circulation. Upon internalization by the tumor cells, the highly reductive intracellular environment induces the detachment of the poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) shell and results in in situ formation of CMs. The formed CMs can effectively escape from endosomes by disrupting the endosomal membrane, facilitating the release of drugs into the cytoplasm. Furthermore, the CMs can serve as drug reservoirs, protecting the cargo from burst release and degradation, thus significantly prolonging the retention time and improving systemic delivery efficacy. Notably, the CMs can also sequester free drugs from the surrounding environment, enhancing sequential therapy by increasing the intratumoral accumulation of the temporally staggered agents. Thus, this micelle-to-coacervate transformable platform illuminates new possibilities for both types of drug-delivery systems.

title: On-Surface Synthesis of a Low Bandgap Cyclopenta[ c , d ]azulene-Based Polymer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nonbenzenoid topologies offer a compelling strategy to tailor the electronic properties of low-dimensional carbon materials. Here, we report the on-surface synthesis of a nonalternant polymer incorporating a [7–5–5] cyclopenta[c,d]azulene (CPA) motif on Au(111) via thermally induced Ullmann coupling. Bond-resolved scanning tunneling microscopy confirms the robustness of the [7–5–5] framework. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy, together with dI/dV mapping supported by density functional theory calculations, reveals a remarkable narrow polymeric bandgap of 1.5 eV. The electronic structure is governed by the intramolecular charge transfer from the heptagonal ring to the adjacent fused pentagonal rings, resulting in a pronounced dipole moment despite being composed exclusively of carbon and hydrogen. Aromaticity analyses indicate the coexistence of locally aromatic and slightly antiaromatic regions, highlighting the intrinsic electronic frustration associated with the nonalternant topology. These findings demonstrate how the controlled incorporation of [7–5–5] motifs enables the rational bandgap engineering in carbon-based polymers and expands the scope of nonbenzenoid design in on-surface synthesis.

title: Direct Detection of the Calcium–Sodium–Calcium Metal Triad in Thermostable α-Amylases from Bacillus sp. Bacteria in Aqueous Solution by 23Na Quadrupole-Central-Transition NMR Spectroscopy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report that the Na+ ion within the calcium–sodium–calcium (Ca–Na–Ca) metal triad in two thermostable bacterial α-amylases (ca. 58 kDa) can be directly detected by 23Na (I = 3/2) quadrupole-central-transition (QCT) NMR spectroscopy in aqueous solution. We show that 23Na QCT NMR signals from hyperthermostable Bacillus licheniformis α-amylase (BLA) and its mesophilic homologue, Bacillus amyloliquefaciens α-amylase (BAA), exhibit remarkable subppm spectral resolution, which is unprecedented in NMR studies of quadrupolar nuclei in proteins. Using this new 23Na QCT NMR methodology, we examine the pH-dependent unfolding, melting temperatures (Tm), long-term thermal inactivation profiles, and chemical denaturing of BAA and BLA. We also use 23Na QCT NMR to monitor EDTA titration experiments, which yielded the apparent binding constants of the Na+ ion to BAA and BLA to be (0.3 ± 0.1) × 109 and (0.6 ± 0.1) × 109 M–1, respectively. Because the Ca–Na–Ca metal triad is located in the vicinity of the active cleft, the subppm spectral resolution of 23Na QCT NMR makes it possible to detect subtle changes of the enzyme structure caused by the presence of inhibitors such as acarbose and quercetin. This work represents the first time that Na+ ions tightly bound to an enzyme are directly observed by 23Na QCT NMR in aqueous solution. This new 23Na QCT NMR approach can potentially be extended to detection of other metal ions with quadrupolar nuclei such as K+, Mg2+, and Zn2+ in metalloenzymes in their native aqueous environment.

title: Multifunctional π–π conjugated molecular bridges for perovskite solar cells
abstract: A π–π co-assembled SAM formed by Me-4PACz and CDA optimizes NiO x /perovskite heterojunction. Interfacial dipole tunes band alignment, suppresses non-radiative recombination, accelerates hole extraction, yielding PSCs with 26.94% PCE.

title: Multicomponent Nanocrystal Superlattice Structure Prediction from First-Principles Validated against Two Decades of Experiments
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Predicting nanocrystal (nanoparticle) assembly into ordered arrays (superlattices) is a grand challenge in materials chemistry that has largely resisted first-principles theories. Here, we extend MOLT-CF, a classical density functional theory, to multicomponent nanocrystal systems and subject it to a rigorous validation by comparing against nearly 300 experiments spanning two decades of literature. We use MOLT-CF to predict stability and phase diagrams for binary superlattices of nanocrystals with linear hydrocarbon ligands, as well as many other fine structural details, for example, lattice constants, packing fractions, ligand structure, and, in the case of (cubic) perovskite nanocrystals, orientation. Significant discrepancies from experiments are noted only for the Li3Bi and Cu3Au superlattices. In the former, we predict that this lattice is stabilized by particle fractionalization, which is supported by a reexamination of experimental data in the literature. In the case of Cu3Au (for which MOLT-CF predicts thermodynamic instability against phase separation into single-component lattices), we propose two alternative candidate structures that reconcile theory with experimental observations. These results establish MOLT-CF as a rigorous platform for the computational design of next-generation functional nanoparticle materials.

title: Electrolyte design toward stable layered oxide cathodes of sodium-ion batteries
abstract: This review analyzes layered oxide cathode degradation in sodium-ion batteries from an electrolyte perspective, proposes electrolyte design principles, summarizes traditional and emerging electrolyte systems, and outlines future perspectives.

title: Redox Properties of the Copper Centers in Particulate Methane Monooxygenase
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Particulate methane monooxygenase (pMMO) and its homolog ammonia monooxygenase (AMO), central enzymes in the global carbon and nitrogen cycles, contain three highly conserved mononuclear copper centers, denoted CuB, CuC, and CuD. While these sites have been well characterized structurally and spectroscopically, with recent studies identifying CuD as the active site, their reduction potentials have not been measured. This knowledge gap has hindered efforts to determine how the two electrons and two protons required for substrate oxidation are sourced and delivered. Here, we have elucidated the redox properties of each copper center in pMMO/AMO by protein film voltammetry using samples with copper occupancies known from cryoelectron microscopy (cryoEM) structures. The reduction potential of the CuB site, −72 to −139 mV, is significantly lower than the ∼400 mV measured for the CuD site, with consistent values determined for pMMOs and AMO from different species. Mutation of a residue in the second sphere of CuB, Glu35, alters the redox potential and impairs cell growth and pMMO activity, indicating that redox chemistry at CuB might be functionally relevant. Finally, a Pourbaix diagram constructed for the CuBII/I and CuDII/I half-reactions suggests that a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process occurs at the CuD site but not at the CuB site. Thermochemical analysis of this proposed PCET process is compatible with electron delivery by a quinol reductant. These results provide new context for future investigations of the pMMO and AMO reaction mechanisms.

title: Wave coarsening drives time crystallization in mechatronic metamaterials
abstract: When metals are magnetized1, emulsions phase separate2, or galaxies cluster3, domain walls and patterns form and irremediably coarsen over time. This coarsening is universally driven by diffusive relaxation towards equilibrium. Here we discover a vibrational counterpart-wave coarsening-in active elastic media4-13: vibrations emerge and spontaneously grow in wavelength, period and amplitude, before a globally synchronized state called a time crystal14-17 forms. We observe wave coarsening in one- and two-dimensional mechatronic metamaterials and capture its dynamical scaling. We further arrest the process by breaking momentum conservation and reveal a far-from-equilibrium nonlinear analogue to chiral topological edge modes18-24. Our results open new questions about the transient physics of systems with non-potential interactions15,25-28 and suggest an organizing principle for nonlinear waves in acoustics29,30, optomechanics31,32, living matter6,33 and soft robotics9.

title: Hemispheric asymmetry in predicted range shifts of anti-tropical fish under future climate change
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anti-tropically distributed species have long intrigued biogeographers. However, how they will respond to future climate change remains a key unresolved question, particularly for marine species given an expected hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming. Here, using species distribution models for 172 anti-tropical marine fishes, we predict that northern hemispheric lineages will experience significantly higher range contractions, in agreement with the hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming. Our predictions show that suitable habitat will be reduced at a similar rate both within and outside marine protected areas, leading protection efficacy (the proportion of the total suitable habitat protected) to remain at current levels, irrespective of the scenario and period considered, and the level of protection efficacy to remain significantly higher in the Southern Hemisphere. These results highlight the need for accounting for hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming when designing future conservation strategies.

title: On predictability of slip, rupture geometry, and speed of the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay, Myanmar, earthquake
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The 2025 M7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions.

title: Downside-risk pre-positioning for resilient scheduling of an off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system under extreme weather
abstract: An off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system (DOEH-IES) provides a practical carrier for onsite offshore wind utilization and multi-energy coordination. However, under typhoon conditions, coupled wind-wave effects and platform motion reduce the available power of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs), introducing a time-varying downside risk that conventional scheduling methods often fail to mitigate proactively. To address this issue, a downside-risk pre-positioning framework is developed for the DOEH-IES that converts physical FOWT power reductions into actionable scheduling decisions. First, a wind power correction model for FOWTs is established by considering wave, floating-platform motion, and air density variation. A dynamically asymmetric envelope is then constructed to extract the time-varying downside exposure during a typhoon and further develop a downside risk indicator. Subsequently, driven by the risk indicator, BESS capacity is reserved in advance of the onset of high-risk periods. Case studies based on typhoon reanalysis data from the South China Sea show that the proposed dynamic asymmetric envelope achieves risk-oriented boundary characterization without increasing weekly average envelope conservatism, with a pre-typhoon average envelope width of 2.69 MW and a maximum downside deviation of 150 MW during peak disturbance. Relative to the comparison case without risk-informed pre-positioning, the proposed framework eliminates electrical load shedding and reserve insufficiency, increases pre-disturbance available stored energy by 72.5%, and reduces natural gas consumption by 15.0% with only a 2.09% cost increase. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can effectively translate the risk into pre-positioning actions, safeguarding supply and equipment continuity.

title: Luminal geometry and coiled coil length determine submembrane localization of type II transmembrane Golgi proteins
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: We previously showed that transmembrane proteins laterally partition within Golgi cisternae: trafficking components (e.g., GPP130, a type II transmembrane protein) are enriched at the cisternal rim, whereas Golgi enzymes localize to the cisternal interior. However, the underlying mechanism was unclear. We found that the luminal juxtamembrane coiled coil of GPP130 is necessary and sufficient for rim localization, with coiled coil length, rather than sequence identity, determining partitioning. When retargeted to the ER, GPP130 preferentially localized to ER sheet rims and was partially excluded from the nuclear envelope, an exclusion reduced upon nuclear envelope expansion. Cryo-electron tomography revealed that the intraluminal widths of Golgi cisternal interiors, some ER sheets, and the nuclear envelope are smaller than the predicted coiled coil length. Two additional type II Golgi transmembrane proteins with long luminal juxtamembrane coiled coils similarly localized to cisternal rims. These findings identify intraluminal width as a mechanism governing the lateral partitioning of type II transmembrane proteins with long luminal coiled coils.

title: Fatty acid metabolism controls plasma membrane cholesterol accessibility via ATGL-dependent phospholipid remodeling
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Accessible cholesterol, the pool of membrane cholesterol with high chemical activity, regulates vital processes including vertebrate development and pathogen evasion. The mechanisms that govern plasma membrane (PM) cholesterol accessibility are incompletely understood. Using a genome-wide screen we find that acetyl-CoA carboxylase alpha (ACC1) loss causes a ~10-fold increase in PM accessible cholesterol in cells and a male mouse model. We demonstrate that reduced fatty acyl-CoA levels, achieved by targeting metabolic enzymes including ACC1, fatty acid synthase (FASN) or acyl-CoA synthetases long chain (ACSL1, 3 and 4), results in the activation of adipose triacylglycerol lipase (ATGL). ATGL activation elevates polyunsaturated diacylglycerols even in triacylglycerol-deficient backgrounds, suggesting that ATGL acts independently of triacylglycerol hydrolysis. These diacylglycerol species are utilized to generate polyunsaturated phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine, which raises PM fluidity and cholesterol accessibility. Conversely, ATGL inhibition rigidifies the PM, reducing PM accessible cholesterol. Increased PM fluidity impairs cholesterol transport, triggering SREBP2 activation. This study reveals a surprising link between fatty acid metabolism and cholesterol homeostasis, demonstrating how ATGL-dependent lipid remodeling tunes membrane fluidity to regulate intracellular cholesterol signaling.

title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals inter-household networks of gut-colonising ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in two rural Malawian districts
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Infection with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli (ESBL-Ec) is a global health concern that disproportionately affects sub-Saharan Africa. Gut mucosal colonisation is thought to precede invasive infection. Understanding ESBL-Ec colonisation and transmission across communities is therefore essential. Here, we investigate the genomic epidemiology and spatial structure of 159 gut-colonising ESBL-Ec isolates from the faeces of 211 people in two rural Malawian villages using longitudinal sampling (2023–24), whole-genome sequencing and household mapping. Colonisation prevalence rose from 34.1% (95% CI: 27.8–41.0) to 54.2% (95% CI: 46.0–62.3) over one year. Isolates belonged to 33 sequence types (STs), most commonly ST38 and ST131, harbouring 46 distinct antimicrobial resistance gene types. Fifteen strains were identified in ≥3 households that were typically separated by short geographic distances (

title: Bridging deterministic and stochastic scheduling: Learning risk-aware forecast adjustments for PV-BESS operation
abstract: The participation of hybrid photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) installations in electricity markets requires modeling multi-temporal forecast uncertainty via temporal trajectories and integrating this information into bidding optimization frameworks. Most state-of-the-art approaches rely on stochastic or robust optimization methods, which are computationally intensive and offer limited interpretability to decision-makers. Consequently, deterministic optimization approaches remain the industry standard in practical market applications. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a novel learning-to-optimize framework that combines a deterministic mixed-integer linear programming formulation with a context-aware artificial neural network policy trained through reinforcement learning. The policy operates as a learned cost function approximation , translating probabilistic forecast metrics into time-dependent multiplicative forecast adjustment parameters. This approach preserves the simplicity and industry acceptance of deterministic optimization while effectively embedding information related to forecast uncertainty and risk-awareness into the day-ahead bidding and scheduling process for hybrid PV-BESS systems. For a real-world electric vehicle charging station case study in Portugal, equipped with 375 kWp of PV generation and a 1.258 MWh BESS, the proposed learning-to-optimize framework substantially outperforms the deterministic baseline. Specifically, it captures 39.27% and 27.26% of the maximum theoretical cost-saving potential achievable under perfect forecasts during autumn and summer peak periods, respectively. At the intraday level, the learned policy effectively mitigates systematic forecast errors, reducing the cumulative daily negative imbalance volume by 48.22% under standard operating conditions. Moreover, the framework maintains a robust operational safety margin, reducing imbalance exposure by 10.02% during large unforeseen PV generation drops caused by clouds.

title: Fever enhances host bacterial defence while limiting mitochondrial damage
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Infection triggers the fever response, but the response’s effect on antimicrobial peptide (AMP) function remains unknown. We discovered that human AMP LL-37 antibacterial activity is temperature-dependent and were curious as to why. Its temperature dependence is not an accident, as AMPs from other animals with different body temperatures have distinct temperature sensitivities. We find that AMP temperature sensitivities are tuned to animals’ body temperatures, and that for animals able to raise their body temperature, this is used to increase the AMP’s antibacterial efficacy. This effect reflects a balance between optimizing antibacterial killing while minimizing mitochondrial damage. In contrast, cold-blooded animals that are unable to raise their body temperature use a different strategy to avoid mitochondrial damage. Together, this study suggests that fever is beneficial for antimicrobial defense by raising AMP activity towards bacteria while reducing mitochondrial damage when pathogens are absent.

title: Theory-guided lightweight decomposition for efficient and robust day-ahead electrical load forecasting
abstract: Accurate electrical load forecasting is important for operational planning and dispatch in modern power systems, yet existing models often face a trade-off among predictive accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness to imperfect exogenous inputs. To address this challenge, we propose a Theory-guided Lightweight Efficient Decomposition (TgLED) framework with a Structured Temporal–Exogenous Mixer (STEM) for day-ahead electrical load forecasting. TgLED transforms raw load data into a normalized load-ratio series and decomposes it into a transferable dimensionless trend and a local fluctuation component. The trend captures stable structural patterns through domain knowledge, whereas the fluctuation is learned by STEM, a lightweight dual-path architecture that separately models temporal inertia and exogenous drivers using efficient feedforward operations. Four-fold cross-validation on hourly load and weather data from 12 districts in Beijing shows that TgLED achieves an average MSE of 0.056, reducing the error by 9.8% compared with the previous theory-guided baseline TgDLF. Compared with recently proposed lightweight time-series forecasting baselines, TgLED achieves evident superiority in forecasting performance. On the same RTX 4090 platform, TgLED reduces the training time from 768.66 s to 6.85 s and the inference time from 19.25 s to 1.91 s, indicating its practical value for frequent retraining and multi-district day-ahead forecasting. Additional noise-injection experiments on weather inputs show slower performance degradation, indicating stronger robustness to exogenous-input uncertainty and weather forecast errors. These results demonstrate that TgLED provides an efficient and interpretable approach to electrical load forecasting under limited computational budgets and imperfect exogenous information.

title: The claustrum contributes to working memory maintenance in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Working memory (WM) enables the temporary maintenance and manipulation of sensory information to guide behavior, yet the neural circuits supporting this process remain incompletely defined. The claustrum is a highly interconnected brain structure positioned to integrate distributed cortical activity, but its contribution to WM has remained unclear. Here, we combined microendoscopic calcium imaging, chemogenetic and optogenetic manipulations in mice performing sensory-guided WM tasks to examine the role of the claustrum in WM. Claustrum neurons exhibited cue-evoked activity that persisted across delay periods and evolved dynamically over time, with population states retaining information about cue identity on single trials. Reducing claustrum excitability during encoding, delay maintenance, or target comparison similarly impaired WM performance across sensory modalities, without affecting sensory processing, motor output, arousal or inhibitory control. Together, these findings reveal an important causal contribution of the claustrum to WM maintenance.

title: Regulation of PDH via cysteine oxidation on DLAT
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex is a key regulator of metabolism, controlling flux from glycolysis into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. PDH is often dysregulated in metabolic diseases and cancer. We discover here that in addition to its well characterized regulation by phosphorylation, PDH activity is also regulated via inhibitory oxidation of three cysteines of the DLAT subunit - Cys488, Cys586 and Cys618. Oxidation of these cysteines increases under oxidative stress, and is highly prevalent in mouse and human tissues. This mechanism enables cells to efficiently fight oxidative stress. Under oxidative stress, cells execute a metabolic shift, blocking glycolytic flux into the TCA cycle to shunt glycolytic carbons toward the pentose phosphate pathway. This generates NADPH which cells use to detoxify H2O2 and to reduce oxidized cysteines. We find that DLAT oxidation is required for cells to mount an effective antioxidant response. Mutations preventing DLAT oxidation render PDH resistant to oxidative inhibition, impair NADPH generation, reduce peroxide detoxification, and sensitize cells to oxidative damage and death. DLAT oxidation also drives a Warburg-like metabolic phenotype of increased glucose uptake, elevated lactate secretion, and reduced TCA cycle activity. Thus DLAT oxidation is a redox-sensing mechanism that regulates PDH activity and central carbon metabolism.

title: Dual-time-scale predictive hierarchical electro-thermal coordination for thermal-load reshaping in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles
abstract: Unlike passenger electric vehicles, heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles operate for long periods under high-load conditions. The continuous heat rejection of the engine-generator set through the engine high-temperature coolant loop makes fan/pump power directly interact with the direct-current (DC) bus power balance and generator–battery power split. Therefore, cooling power scheduling is part of energy management, rather than only a thermal-protection task. This paper proposes a dual-time-scale predictive hierarchical electro-thermal coordination strategy, termed DTP-HETC, for thermal-load reshaping in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles. A shared-encoder dual-head bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) predictor is used to capture short-horizon traction fluctuations and long-horizon engine-loop thermal evolution. The predicted thermal risk is quantified as thermal debt and converted into thermal buffer intensity B T k , which further adapts the thermal-load-shaping weights and the control-grid resolution of dynamic programming-based model predictive control (DP-MPC). By using this information, DTP-HETC advances part of the cooling effort from boundary-triggered response to thermal-risk formation intervals, smoothing cooling-induced DC-bus disturbances and coordinating fan/pump power with generator–battery power allocation. Simulation and hardware-in-the-loop tests on a 220-ton series hybrid mining truck show that, under sustained heavy-load uphill operation, DTP-HETC reduces equivalent fuel consumption by 12.16% and lowers peak engine-loop coolant temperature by 2.53 °C compared with a rule-based baseline. The mean execution time is 33.7 ms, confirming controller-level real-time feasibility. These results indicate that DTP-HETC provides an effective thermal-load reshaping approach for improving energy efficiency and thermal reliability in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles.

title: Shifting balance between habitat and climate in boreal biodiversity patterns across space, time and taxa
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Climate and habitat are key drivers of biodiversity patterns. However, how they independently and jointly affect species distribution across space, time, and taxa remains poorly understood. Here, we evaluate the relative importance of habitat and climate variables underpinning occurrence and abundance patterns of 503 terrestrial animal species over 20 years and a ~ 1100 km latitudinal gradient in Finland. Habitat composition is the main explanatory variable of biodiversity patterns, with varying importance and uncertainty across taxa, regions, and years, and with effects being partially correlated for many species. Specifically, habitat dominate in importance for butterflies, birds, and small mammals, while both habitat and climate explain the patterns of large mammals and moths. Additionally, patterns between biogeographical regions and years are mainly explained by climate, while habitat explains most variation within regions and years. Further differences emerge among functional groups, as body size, pace of life and specialization modulate the relative importance of habitat and climate. Our findings emphasize that land use is a major force in shaping terrestrial biodiversity, while highlighting its tight connection with climate. Considering functional, spatial, and temporal contexts is thus essential for building effective conservation strategies for biodiversity under global change.

title: Small viruses reveal bidirectional evolution between HK97-fold viruses and encapsulins via procapsids
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The HK97-fold is an ancient, conserved protein structure that assembles protein shells, forming the capsids of Duplodnaviria viruses and prokaryotic biochemical compartments called encapsulsins. It has been proposed that encapsulins evolved from HK97-fold viruses. But the higher complexity of viral capsids represents a biophysical paradox in the evolution of HK97-fold protein shells. To resolve this problem, we hypothesize the existence of simpler HK97-fold viral capsids associated with smaller genomes than those of known HK97-fold viruses. Such small viral genomes are searched in environmental metagenomes across public databases, including IMG/M and MGnify. Using hidden Markov models and protein language models, we identify and characterize small viral genomes encoding HK97-fold proteins that exhibit molecular similarities to encapsulins yet lack portal and tail genes. The phylogenetic analyses of HK97-fold proteins reveal independent mixed groups of viruses and encapsulins, and structural analyses identify similarities between encapsulins and procapsids, the immature state of viral capsids. The observations support a bidirectional evolution between encapsulins and HK97-fold viruses enabled by the viral procapsid state. Using biophysical and genomic arguments, we introduce an evolutionary model of HK97-fold protein shells, predicting that they emerged as lower-symmetry biochemical compartments and that HK97-fold viral capsids may retain biochemical functions.

title: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
