abstract: Although cerebellum is neuropathologically affected in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementia (ADRD), the cell type-specific genomic and epigenomic changes remain poorly understood. Here, we present single-nucleus multiome (RNA-seq and ATAC-seq) analysis of 103,861 nuclei isolated from both the cerebellum and frontal cortex of diseased individuals and cognitively healthy controls. We identify 431,834 significant peak-to-gene linkages across cell subtypes, revealing cis-regulatory elements linked to cell type-specific and disease-associated transcriptomic and regulatory network changes. Differential trajectory analysis pinpoints disease-associated genes in cerebellar granule cells, such as STMN1 and CLU. Integrating epigenomic, genetic, and three-dimensional genome data, we pinpoint two likely causal variants linked to SEZ6L2 in Purkinje cells and KANSL1 in granule cells. Through CRISPR interference in patient-derived cerebellar organoids, we show that silencing the variant-containing regulatory elements suppresses SEZ6L2 and KANSL1 expression, which perturbs neurodegeneration-associated gene programs. This cell type-specific regulatory landscape provides genomic and epigenomic insights into the pathological role of the cerebellum in AD/ADRD.

title: EphrinA4/EphA4 controls blood pressure via arterial sympathetic innervation in male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The autonomic sympathetic nervous system innervates peripheral resistance arteries, thereby controlling arterial diameter and modulating blood supply to organs and arterial tone. Despite its fundamental role in blood flow regulation and cardiovascular adaptation to challenging situations, how sympathetic arterial innervation develops remains poorly understood.We here show that sympathetic arterial innervation is regulated by the axonal guidance molecule EphrinA4 in arterial Smooth Muscle Cells (SMCs), which repels sympathetic axons via the EphA4 receptor. Using the EphA4flox-THCRE mouse, we specifically inactivated EphA4 in sympathetic axons, inducing a loss of repulsion and increased sympathetic innervation of peripheral arteries throughout life. Functional consequences included a significant increase in arterial tone, including resistivity and vasoconstriction, associated with elevated systemic arterial blood pressure at rest and a marked increase during acute stress. These findings identify a pathway that negatively regulates sympathetic arterial innervation and could contribute to elevated systemic blood pressure in male mice.

title: Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-myocarditis) is a rare but frequently fatal immune-related adverse event. A comprehensive understanding of the cellular and molecular determinants driving ICI-myocarditis is essential for improving diagnostic precision and developing targeted interventions. We delineate the immune landscape of ICI-myocarditis via scRNA-seq, flow cytometry, Olink proteomics, and multiplex cytokine profiling. We demonstrate that high levels of baseline ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells are linked to the proinflammatory features of monocytes and in vitro experiments confirm the existence of circulating ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells with a high potential to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, supporting their pathogenic potential for cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity. Notably, intercellular crosstalk between these subsets is possibly mediated via the CCL2-CCR2 axis, and its blockade attenuated ICI-induced cardiac injury in vivo. Based on the inflammatory signature in ICI-myocarditis, we develop an 8-protein custom panel with promising performance in distinguishing ICI-myocarditis from other ICIs-treated controls. JAK-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes. Furthermore, JAK-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse models. In summary, this study implicates immune-pathogenic features of ICI-myocarditis and provides a possible basis for future therapies.

title: Replacing anaerobic fermentation with reverse β-oxidation enables growth-coupled evolution for enhanced fatty-alcohol production
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Engineering robust fermentation hosts remains a barrier to scalable biomanufacturing. In this work we replace canonical mixed-acid fermentation in Escherichia coli with a redox‑balanced reverse β‑oxidation (rBOX) pathway that produces medium‑chain fatty alcohols and is bioenergetically equivalent to ethanol fermentation. This synthetic fermentation restores anaerobic growth, tightly coupling fitness to product formation and enabling adaptive laboratory evolution that selects for mutations increasing rBOX flux. Evolved strains increase maximum productivity fourfold (110 ± 0.15 mg/L/hr) and titer more than threefold up to 4.0 ± 0.28 g/L compared to the unevolved strain. Proteomic analyses of evolved strains indicate differential expression of enzymes at key metabolic nodes and activation of latent genes with functions overlapping those of rBOX enzymes. These results establish redox-balanced growth coupling as a powerful tool for strain improvement and demonstrate rBOX as a practical synthetic fermentation pathway.

title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chiral amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceutical synthesis. (R)-3-([1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)-2-aminopropan-1-ol (ABP), a key chiral amine intermediate of the drug Entresto, has remained difficult to access via enzymatic asymmetric synthesis due to the inability of ω-transaminases to accommodate its bulky ketone precursor. Here, we engineer an ω-transaminase from Bacillus megaterium by integrating Funnel metadynamics, PathDetect-SOM, and path collective variables to reconstruct the free energy surface of substrate binding, pinpointing high-energy barrier regions of the binding process and the trade-off between tunnel accessibility and productive binding. Dynamic cross-correlation network analysis further identifies distal regulatory sites governing these bottleneck regions. Iterative experimental optimization yields the 13M variant, exhibiting catalytic activity 106 times that of the wild type with >99% enantiomeric excess, enabling the efficient enzymatic asymmetric synthesis of ABP. This integrated computational-experimental framework for resolving the tunnel-pocket binding trade-off offers a generalizable strategy for engineering ω-transaminases toward bulky substrates in green pharmaceutical synthesis.

title: Effects of time-restricted eating and supervised exercise on intrahepatic fat and cardiometabolic health in adults with obesity: the TEMPUS randomized controlled trial
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Lifestyle interventions targeting intrahepatic fat remain limited. We investigated whether 8-hour time-restricted eating (TRE), supervised exercise, or their combination reduced intrahepatic fat fraction (IHFF) more than usual care (UC; Mediterranean diet and physical activity education) and each other. This investigator-initiated, parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted in Granada, Spain. Participants were recruited from May 2023 to April 2024, and the trial was completed on 5 September 2025. Primary outcome assessors and statisticians were blinded to group allocation, whereas intervention personnel were not. All 187 randomized adults with obesity (50% women) were included in the primary intention-to-treat analysis: UC (n = 48), TRE (n = 46), Exercise (n = 47), and TRE+Exercise (n = 46). The primary outcome was change in IHFF measured by magnetic resonance imaging after 12 weeks. IHFF change did not differ with TRE (−0.4%; 95% CI, −2.0 to 1.2; P = 0.93), Exercise (−0.8%; −2.4 to 0.8; P = 0.54), or TRE+Exercise (−1.1%; −2.7 to 0.5; P = 0.28) compared with UC, nor among intervention groups. These findings do not support greater short-term IHFF reductions with TRE, exercise, or their combination than with UC or between intervention groups. Trial registration: NCT05897073.

title: Evolutionary remodeling of the ventral retina enables aerial vision in the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The emergence of evolutionary novelties remains a central challenge in biology, particularly for complex organs such as the vertebrate eye. Here, we use the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps to investigate adaptation to simultaneous aerial and aquatic vision. Single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics reveal that the ventral retina, which processes aerial light, is developmentally expanded and exhibits region-specific opsin expression. Ventral PR1 cones express opn1mw2 rather than the longer-wavelength-sensitive opn1lw paralogs expressed dorsally. Machine-learning predictions indicate that Opn1mw2 is red-shifted relative to Opn1mw1 but remains blue-shifted relative to dorsal Opn1lw pigments. Dorsal-ventral patterning markers further reveal an overrepresentation of ventral retinal identities. Comparative spatial profiling of developing and adult Anableps and killifish indicates dorsal displacement of the retinal boundary, producing a proportionally larger ventral domain. Thus, Anableps evolved aerial vision through developmental expansion of the ventral retina and regional reconfiguration of opsin expression within conserved cone subtypes.

title: Lesion penetration predicts tuberculosis treatment shortening through a validated translational tool to de-risk development
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anti-tuberculosis (TB) drugs must reach the disease site to be effective, but complex TB pathology limits drug distribution and efficacy, as bacteria in the necrotic center of lung cavities are difficult to access and kill. Our study generates the most comprehensive database of site-of-disease distribution for 24 drugs and drug candidates in a rabbit model of cavitary TB. We validate a lung lesion penetration model with clinical data and develop an integrated approach that combines microenvironment-specific pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Next, we simulate site-of-disease coverage of shortened regimens tested in major Phase 3 trials over the past decade, allowing direct comparisons with trial outcomes. We propose that regimens including at least two drugs achieving bactericidal concentrations in pulmonary cavities are more likely to meet primary clinical endpoints in patients with cavitary disease. Our translational platform constitutes a validated tool to support drug evaluation, smart regimen design, and de-risking of late-stage trials.

title: Evaluating the effects of population mobility on transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Changes to community mobility during the COVID-19 pandemic, together with unprecedented availability of surveillance and mobility data, provide a unique opportunity to quantify the effect of mobility on respiratory infection transmission. We present a renewal model that incorporates epidemiological mechanisms influencing SARS-CoV-2 transmission along with a non-mechanistic scaling process. We compare models with and without mobility using epidemic data from 122 countries and quantify the influence of mobility through reductions in non-mechanistic scaling. In several countries, this non-mechanistic process closely tracks mobility trends and varies substantially less when mobility is incorporated. This is especially evident in Western Europe and North America, but not in several countries of West Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Google and Facebook data produce similar findings, and parks is frequently assigned the lowest weight in the multi-location Google analysis. Mobility trends are strongly aligned with short-term transmission dynamics in many high-income settings, although between-country heterogeneity remains.

title: Citizens’ assemblies propose ambitious climate policy but impacts remain limited
abstract:
Abstract
                  Climate citizens’ assemblies convene randomly selected citizens who, after structured learning and deliberation, develop policy recommendations. Yet, whether they produce more ambitious recommendations and influence political decisions remains contested. Here we conduct a comparative, counterfactual assessment of 488 recommendations from five national and one state-level assembly in Western Europe, drawing on document analysis and expert interviews. The results show that citizens consistently proposed more ambitious climate measures than existing government policy. Recommendations sometimes influenced policy by adding momentum, enriching plans, breaking deadlocks or introducing novel ideas, but such influence was rare. Only the French assembly shows substantial policy impact, with one-third of its recommendations having influenced policy, due to strong power delegation, political leadership and resulting public pressure. In the other cases, policy impact was minimal or absent. These findings show that citizens’ assemblies can raise policy ambition, but translating recommendations into political decisions depends strongly on political conditions.

title: A methodology for long-term hourly electricity demand forecasting driven by GDP and invariant load profiles
abstract: Long-term electricity demand forecasting is necessary for grid and operations planning, as well as for the analysis and planning of energy transition strategies. However, accurate long-term load forecasting with high temporal resolution remains a challenge as most existing approaches focus on aggregated forecasts, which require accurate prediction of many other variables. This study proposes a parsimonious methodology that uses t-tests to verify the temporal invariance of historical load profiles and the correlation of load with gross domestic product (GDP) to arrive at a long-term hourly load forecast. Applying this methodology first to a controlled benchmark analysing Singapore’s isolated grid, and of multi-year historical data (2004–2022) reveals that its relative hourly load has remained statistically invariant, with an overall percentage deviation of 4.24% across seasonality indices. Utilizing these invariant historical load profiles, five-year-ahead total yearly forecasts were generated using GDP as a predictor, and the hourly loads were then forecasted using hourly seasonality index fractions. The maximum Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) across multiple experiments of six years ahead forecasts was only 6.87%. To systematically evaluate the generalizability and macroeconomic limitations of this top-down methodology beyond Singapore, the methodology was subsequently tested across six European countries. Results show that the methodology achieves high accuracy (MAPE < 8%) for economies with strong GDP-load correlations (Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Spain) but exhibits some performance degradation in decoupled economies where macroeconomic growth no longer drives electricity demand expansion linearly (Germany, UK). Additionally, invariant seasonality metrics were incorporated into a short-term forecasting model based on exponential smoothing (ES), demonstrating comparable or improved accuracy relative to existing machine learning-based methods. The findings show that parsimonious approaches can be effective in arriving at long-term, high resolution forecasts.

title: Genome-reduced Aridivitia evolved predation to thrive in Earth’s oligotrophic depths
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Deep soils represent one of Earth’s largest yet most enigmatic microbial habitats, where survival strategies under extreme oligotrophy remain poorly understood. Here, we report the Aridivitia group, a globally distributed bacterial lineage enriched in oligotrophic soils and thriving down to 22 m depth across sites in the United States and China. Despite its genome reduction (average size ~2.9 Mb), Aridivitia exhibits high metabolic flexibility in utilizing diverse carbon and energy sources. Cellular, genomic, and metatranscriptomic evidence, including small cell and genome sizes, host-associated metabolism, and the active expression of attachment- and attack-associated surface structures such as Tad pili and pore-forming toxins, indicate a predatory lifestyle in Aridivitia. Ancestral genome reconstruction reveals that Aridivitia originated as free-living mixotrophs, but subsequently lost the ability to fix carbon as they evolved a predatory lifestyle. Collectively, Aridivitia exemplifies a unique evolutionary strategy that reconciles genome reduction with functional versatility, expanding our understanding of microbial adaptation and evolution at the energetic limits of life.

title: Transport characteristics and formation mechanism of voltage inconsistency in 200-cell PEMFC stack: Numerical reconstruction and experimental investigation
abstract: Due to the difficulty in directly observing and resolving internal mass transport in multi-cell proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) stacks, current studies on stack voltage inconsistency remain largely confined to macroscopic performance analysis. Consequently, the mechanisms responsible for voltage inconsistency remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, this study develops a framework integrating offline pressure testing, pressure boundary extraction, and grouped numerical reconstruction to investigate internal transport processes and clarify the formation mechanism of voltage inconsistency in large-scale multi-cell stacks. In this framework, pressure data measured at different stack positions are used as boundary conditions to reconstruct the transport behavior of representative cells and analyze stack mass transport characteristics. The reconstructed results are then combined with sensitivity analysis of the experimental data to identify the dominant factors governing stack voltage nonuniformity. Finally, numerical simulations are performed to reproduce the development of low-voltage cells and further verify the proposed mechanism. The results show that the maximum oxygen concentration difference among cells at different stack positions is only 0.4 mol/m 3 , indicating that oxygen distribution differences alone are insufficient to cause significant performance variations. Correlation analysis further indicates that liquid water accumulation at the bottom of the stack is the dominant factor responsible for voltage reduction in the bottom cells. Water-rich simulations demonstrate that increased liquid-water loading in the bottom cells can obstruct oxygen transport and cause voltage decay. This study provides an effective numerical reconstruction method for resolving internal transport processes in multi-cell PEMFC stacks and offers guidance for improving stack cell-voltage consistency.

title: A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Wildfires in the Amazon have far-reaching climatic and ecological impacts, yet their predictability remains limited. Here we identify a large-scale atmospheric precursor of August–September Amazon wildfires: a June–July dipole mode of South Atlantic atmospheric rivers (ARs), characterized by suppressed AR activity in the north and enhanced activity in the south. This dipole is strongly linked to interannual variability in Amazon wildfire activity through land–atmosphere feedbacks associated with reduced precipitation and humidity, enhanced surface warming and solar radiation, and increased vegetation stress. We estimate that wildfire-related forest loss associated with this AR dipole mode accounts for approximately 26% of the observed interannual variability in total forest loss. Adding the South Atlantic AR dipole to predictors based on May–June sea surface temperature anomalies and June–July wildfire activity yields substantial predictive skill for August–September burned area (R² = 0.67). Climate model projections further indicate a future intensification of the South Atlantic AR dipole mode, implying increased wildfire-driven ecological degradation in the Amazon under continued warming.

title: Global expansion of compound drought–heatwave risk
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The increasing frequency of compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events poses a growing threat to water security, agriculture, and ecosystems. However, the evolution, expansion, and spatial reorganization of CDHW hotspots across global land regions remain largely unexplored. Here we track more than 2500 CDHW events using a three-dimensional connected-component (CC3D) labeling approach and show that CDHWs, often treated as spatially stationary extremes, exhibit systematic displacement over time. Larger and longer-lasting events tend to travel farther and faster, expanding the spatial footprint of compound heat and moisture stress. Most contiguous events persist for 6–12 days, displace by up to ~500 km, and reach peak daily spatial extents of 2–5 × 10⁵ km². Migration is strongest in the Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes and is predominantly eastward. We identify emerging hotspots of increasing CDHW migration potential across the European Plains, western North America, the Amazon, the West African Sahel, Central Asia, and northern Australia. These shifts are linked to evolving large-scale atmospheric circulation and are reinforced by downstream drying through reduced moisture transport and strengthened land–atmosphere coupling. Increasing CDHW migration potential over agricultural landscapes may expand exposure to compound heat and moisture stress, particularly in grazing-dependent regions vulnerable to pastureland-to-scrubland transitions.

title: Universal crystallization kinetics of solution-processed semiconductors
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Heterogeneous crystallization kinetics critically govern the morphology and performance of solution-processed semiconductors, yet morphology control is often achieved through trial-and-error optimization. Quantitative understanding of crystallization is essential for precise morphology control but is limited by the simultaneous occurrence of heterogeneous nucleation and crystal growth. Here, a time-defined induced nucleation strategy has been developed to initiate crystallization at specific stages of solution processing. Systematic variation of nucleation timing reveals three distinct morphological regimes, whose emergence is explained by the concentration-dependent critical cluster radius in bulk, interfacial, and cusp environments. On this basis, a quantitative, dimensionless model is developed for heterogeneous crystallization kinetics across diverse processing conditions. The model demonstrates universality across perovskite and organic semiconductors. In situ studies reveal identical growth kinetics for induced and spontaneous nuclei, validating its generality. The resulting morphology control enables tuning of crystallinity and charge transport in solution-processed transistors.

title: Vacancy-mediated ultrafast oxide-ion conduction in excess-oxygen Sillén oxybromides
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) require electrolytes with high oxide-ion conductivity at low temperatures (200–400 °C) to reduce costs. Here, we report that Bi1.9Te0.1LaO4.05Br exhibits oxide-ion conductivity of 0.01 S cm⁻¹ at 233 °C within the “Norby gap” in dry atmospheres. This performance exceeds that of leading proton conductors, such as BaZr0.8Y0.2O2.9 and BaZr0.4Ce0.4Y0.1Yb0.1O2.9, as well as representative oxide-ion conductors, including yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ), LaGaO3-based phases (LSGM), and Bi2V0.7Sb0.3O5.5. Bi1.9Te0.1LaO4.05Br also exhibits negligible chemical expansion and high chemical stability under oxidizing, reducing, and CO2-containing atmospheres. The high conductivity is associated with a layered Sillén structure composed of Bi-containing triple fluorite-like slabs and Br layers, together with oxygen vacancies that enable vacancy-mediated oxide-ion migration. Despite the presence of excess oxide ions, oxide-ion transport predominantly occurs via a vacancy mechanism, as revealed by ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, static density functional theory calculations, and neutron diffraction analyses. These findings establish a design principle for high-performance oxide-ion conductors based on vacancy-mediated oxide-ion transport in excess-oxygen Bi-containing Sillén oxyhalides.

title: Giant Baromagnetic Effect Induced by Spin Engineering in Mn3(Zn0.25Sn0.25Ga0.25Ge0.25)C
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Baromagnetic effect (BME), arising from pressure-induced spin reorientation, holds great potential for next-generation information technologies owing to its strong multifield coupling characteristics. However, the practical implementation of BME is hindered by the small magnetization change and the large driving pressure required in conventional materials. Guided by spin-polarized calculations, this work successfully obtains a giant BME material Mn3(Zn0.25Sn0.25Ga0.25Ge0.25)C, which exhibits a remarkable pressure-induced maximum magnetization change (|ΔMmax|) of 2.63 μB·f.u.–1 and an exceptionally large baromagnetic coefficient (BMC, d) of 15.0 μB·f.u.–1·GPa–1. Temperature-dependent neutron powder diffraction (NPD) measurements reveal a clear evolution from the nearly collinear antiferromagnetic (cAFM) configuration with k = (1/2, 1/2, 1/2) to the ferromagnetic (FM) configuration, indicating that the spins are highly susceptible to reorientation under external perturbations. First-principles calculations further clarify that pressure modulates the energy difference (ΔE) between the cAFM and FM configurations via the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, elucidating the microscopic origin of the giant BME. This demonstration establishes spin engineering, achieved through precise control of spin configurations via targeted element selection, as an effective strategy for realizing high-performance baromagnetic systems. It further provides clear guidance for designing materials with superior functional properties.

title: Thermodynamic decoupling of polymer pre-aggregation in sustainable solvents enables high-detectivity flexible organic photodiodes
abstract: Precise control of solution aggregation enables flexible organic photodiodes processed from sustainable solvents to combine high detectivity with strong mechanical durability. By slowing rapid nucleation and improving film formation, this approach reduces trap formation and structural defects, offering a practical route toward sustainably manufactured wearable optoelectronics.

title: Can weakly interlayer-coupled transition metal dichalcogenides open up a new prospect of two-dimensional family?
abstract: Weak interlayer coupling, originating from electron interactions of adjacent layers, can provide promising prospects for two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), which can be respectively evaluated by energy criteria qualitatively and by band-gap transformation and band-shifting ratios quantitatively. Weakly interlayer-coupled TMDCs will promote the development of all-2D processing-in-memory devices together with strongly interlayer-coupled ones.

title: Metal-organic pulsed laser deposition for complex oxide heterostructures
abstract: Point defects govern the properties of complex oxides, yet they are hard to control precisely. Lee et al. introduce metal-organic pulsed laser deposition (MOPLD), which tunes the cation stoichiometry of SrTiO3 films to within a 0.1% solubility limit. By selectively adjusting antisite and vacancy populations, MOPLD suppresses oxygen vacancies and boosts the low-temperature mobility of the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 electron gas, offering a general route to defect engineering in oxide heterostructures for quantum materials research.

title: A stochastic techno-economic framework for hydrogen-based maritime decarbonisation under market and policy uncertainty
abstract: Maritime decarbonisation pathways are subject to substantial uncertainty arising from volatile fuel markets and evolving regulatory frameworks. This study develops a stochastic techno-economic framework to evaluate the lifecycle cost competitiveness of hydrogen-based propulsion systems under combined market and policy uncertainty. The framework integrates Monte Carlo-based stochastic price uncertainty with scenario-conditioned policy uncertainty, capturing variability in key cost drivers including CAPEX, fuel price, CO 2 value, EU ETS, FuelEU Maritime, and IMO GFI mechanisms. Two hydrogen pathways, namely onboard hydrogen production using steam methane reforming with carbon capture (HPU) and green hydrogen bunkering (Green H 2), are assessed against a conventional oil-fuelled reference ship (RefShip) over the 2030–2050 period. Results show that HPU exhibits strong policy sensitivity and becomes increasingly competitive under supportive policy conditions, whereas Green H 2 competitiveness remains constrained by hydrogen fuel cost. The median net lifecycle cost ratio relative to RefShip, R , is in the range 0.24–0.68 for the hydrogen pathways. Excluding FuelEU Maritime and IMO GFI surplus-credit revenues increases the median gross cost ratio to R = 0.65–0.90 for HPU and approximately R = ~0.8 for Green H 2. While HPU retains only a small probability of exceeding RefShip costs under Conservative and Moderate policy scenarios, this probability becomes negligible under Optimistic and Policy-Optimal scenarios. Green H 2, however, maintains probability of being more expensive than RefShip across all policy scenarios due to the dominant contribution of hydrogen fuel expenditure. Threshold analysis demonstrates that both pathways remain economically favourable relative to RefShip at EUA prices below ~100 €/tCO 2 , hydrogen price below ~$5.8/kg H 2 , and CO 2 offloading costs below ~$300/tCO 2 . The results demonstrate the importance of stochastic assessment for capturing long-term investment risk and policy uncertainty, highlighting the value of the proposed framework for risk-informed maritime decarbonisation planning.

title: Transferable state-of-charge prediction across temperature domains for lithium-ion and semi-solid batteries
abstract: Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is essential for battery management systems (BMSs) in electric vehicles (EVs) and energy storage systems. The rapid innovation in battery technologies and the complexity of operating environments pose significant challenges to SOC estimation. This paper introduces an application-oriented TabPFN-based SOC estimation framework that adapts a pretrained tabular foundation model to sequential battery data for efficient SOC prediction. A sliding-window feature construction strategy is employed to transform historical current, voltage, and temperature measurements into structured tabular features and capture short-term temporal dependencies. The proposed framework was evaluated on both public and self-made datasets. Notably, the self-made datasets include not only traditional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) but also advanced semi-solid batteries (SSBs). The results suggest that the TabPFN-based framework has promising applicability for SOC estimation under the tested battery types, temperatures, and driving profiles. Experimental results show that, compared with selected baseline models, this approach achieves high prediction accuracy while reducing task-specific model training and hyperparameter-tuning efforts, suggesting its potential for practical SOC estimation.

title: Risk-aware cooperative planning of energy storage in multi-regional power systems under extreme weather: CVaR-based transfer pricing and contribution-based Nash bargaining
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable generation highlights the need for cross-regional resource sharing, especially during extreme-weather events that cause renewable droughts and supply shortages. However, regional differences in renewable profiles, load characteristics, flexibility resources, storage investment potential, and risk exposure make sustained cooperation difficult. System-level cost minimization can lead to uneven support obligations, risk burdens, and benefits among autonomous regions. This paper proposes a risk-aware cooperative energy storage planning framework for multi-regional power systems. The framework first introduces a physical planning model that jointly optimizes the siting and sizing of short- and long-duration energy storage, as well as cross-regional operations under both normal and extreme-weather scenarios. A risk-adjusted transfer-pricing rule combines a load-weighted conditional shadow-price signal with an average conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) allocation charge. The resulting recipient-side prices are used to value outward emergency support and determine contribution-based weights for asymmetric Nash bargaining, which allocates the cooperative surplus under individual-rationality and internal budget-balance constraints. A three-level C&CG–AOP–ADMM procedure is developed for distributed planning and exchange coordination, with exchange valuation and surplus allocation based on regional optimization outputs. Numerical studies on a four-region IEEE RTS-24 system show that cooperation reduces system physical cost by 29.14% and expected load shedding by 48.64% relative to independent regional planning, while the proposed allocation links regional surplus shares to recipient-valued support contributions and satisfies individual rationality and internal budget balance.

title: Environmental synergies and trade-offs in the rapid transition of China's electricity system
abstract: China's power sector is undergoing rapid decarbonisation while simultaneously expanding generation. Although the power sector's greenhouse gas (GHG) emission trajectories under various decarbonisation pathways have been extensively researched, other non-GHG environmental implications remain poorly investigated, particularly due to limited spatially resolved data to trace where the actual impact occurs globally. Therefore, this study employs a spatially explicit life cycle assessment method to evaluate the environmental synergies and trade-offs of China's power sector under two future scenarios in 2050. A comprehensive portfolio of provincial-level, technology-specific life cycle inventories for China's current and future power systems are compiled, incorporating country-specific supply chain processes for key materials. The results show substantial decreases in GHG Emissions, from 5.5 Gt CO 2 eq in 2020 to 3.2 and − 1.02 Gt CO 2 eq by 2050 under the two scenarios. Synergies are observed between GHG Emissions and Particulate Matter Formation, with the latter declining by 31–70% compared to 2020. However, these synergies are accompanied by significant environmental trade-offs, as Land Transformation, Freshwater Eutrophication and Mineral Resource Use increase significantly. Spatially, land and water related impacts are gradually concentrating in China, while mineral related impacts are increasingly spreading to other countries and regions. Provincial contributions to national total impacts are also significantly reshaped under future scenarios because different power system configurations redistribute the ultimate cause of environmental impacts. This study highlights the need for climate policies to balance climate targets with broader environmental considerations for sustainable decarbonisation and to coordinate tailored mitigation across technologies, provinces, and global supply chains to support a more equitable and just transition.

title: China’s dynamic layouts of carbon capture utilization and storage
abstract: Carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS) is pivotal to China's carbon neutrality goal by 2060. A national-scale dynamic source-sink matching optimization model is developed to explore CCUS deployment across 31 provinces and 16 sedimentary basins under eight integrated scenarios, which combine two emission pathways (Announced Pledges Scenario, APS; Stated Policies Scenario, STEPS) with four storage growth pathways (CS1–CS4). The model quantifies CO₂ capture from coal-fired power, gas-fired power, steel, cement, and chemical plants, and evaluates storage via enhanced oil recovery (EOR), enhanced gas recovery (EGR), enhanced water recovery (EWR), and enhanced coal bed methane (ECBM). Under the CE1-CS1 pathway cumulative CO₂ capture and storage reaches 11.1 billion tons by 2060 with the Ordos Basin storing 4.24 billion tons. Coal-fired power plants dominate capture contributions, while EWR and EGR emerge as predominant utilization modes. In STEPS, the CE2-CS1 pathway featuring slower emission decline but sustained storage growth yields a cumulative capture of 32.59 billion tons. Hebei, Shanxi, and Shandong collectively account for 26.5% of national capture, with the Ordos Basin storing 8.29 billion tons. Here, EGR and ECBM become the dominant storage strategies, reflecting higher residual emission and extended capture timelines. Economic analysis shows that the CE1-CS1 pathway generates benefits totaling 4849.5 billion yuan. Proximity between major emitters (e.g., Shanxi) and large storage basins (e.g., Ordos) is critical for cost-effective transport. The study highlights that coal-fired power remains the primary CCUS target, while EOR/EGR offer high-value utilization opportunities. These findings provide a data-driven framework for scaling CCUS in China and insights for global carbon management.

title: Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.

title: Tailoring Superhydrophobic Ultramicropores in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Humidity-Resistant Methane Purification
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Efficient purification of methane from raw natural gas under humid conditions remains challenging because water adsorption often degrades the separation performance and structural stability of porous adsorbents. Here we report a topology- and stacking-guided molecular design strategy that integrates ultramicropore engineering with pore-surface fluorination to construct superhydrophobic covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for humidity-resistant methane purification. Two isoreticular fluorinated COFs, TF-COF and NF-COF, were constructed by rationally controlling framework topology and interlayer stacking, generating well-defined ultramicropores for size-selective discrimination of C1–C3 hydrocarbons. Fluorination simultaneously enhances pore-wall hydrophobicity and strengthens host–guest interactions, creating a confined adsorption environment that promotes hydrocarbon recognition while effectively suppressing competitive water adsorption. As a result, NF-COF exhibits a propane uptake of 99.4 cm3 g–1 and an exceptional C3H8/CH4 IAST selectivity of 251.7 at 298 K. Dynamic breakthrough experiments further demonstrate efficient methane purification under both dry and highly humid conditions, with the separation performance fully retained at 97% relative humidity owing to its superhydrophobic surface. Theoretical calculations reveal that densely distributed fluorine atoms generate synergistic pore confinement and multiple C–H···F van der Waals interactions, simultaneously maximizing adsorption capacity and molecular discrimination. These findings establish fluorinated superhydrophobic COFs as a robust platform for energy-efficient natural gas upgrading under industrially relevant humid conditions.

title: Surface carbonation governs olivine reactivity for rapid CO2 mineralization
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ultramafic rocks are a global resource with vast potential for permanent CO2 mineralization. However, the origin of the striking reactivity difference between Ca- and Mg-bearing olivine remains poorly understood. Here we show that this difference arises not merely from the type of cation, but more fundamentally from how these cations modulate the oxygen reactivity. Nonbridging oxygens serve as the oxygen source for CO2 surface reactions, which in Ca-olivine reduce the Ca2+ dissolution barrier by 60% and accelerate ion release by six orders of magnitude. The calculated apparent dissolution rate constants reproduce the experimentally observed complete conversion of Ca-olivine within hours under 1 atm CO2. This multiscale framework reveals how surface reactions govern silicate carbonation and provides a predictive basis for modeling and engineering large-scale CO2 mineralization in both synthetic materials and basaltic reservoirs.

title: Spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe–La geminal atoms with spin and coordination modulation for acidic oxygen reduction
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Synergistic spin-state and local coordination engineering offers a promising strategy for enhancing the acidic oxygen reduction reaction performance of Fe–N–C electrocatalysts, yet the precise control and stabilization of active sites remain challenging. Here we report a Fe–La geminal-atom electrocatalyst (Fe1-La1/NC) with spontaneous ferromagnetic spin ordering for acidic oxygen reduction reaction. The catalyst achieves a half-wave potential of 0.92 V and a turnover frequency of 17.3e-site−1s−1, compared with commercial Pt/C (0.87 V, 9.9e-site−1s−1). A proton exchange membrane fuel cell equipped with Fe1-La1/NC cathode delivers a high current density of 56 mA cm−2 at 0.9ViR-free under H2-O2 condition, while maintaining stable operation for 100 h at 0.67 V with 86% performance retention. Operando studies and theoretical simulations reveal that La incorporation promotes a spin-polarized high-spin Fe 3 d configuration and room-temperature ferromagnetic ordering, while also regulating the local coordination/electronic structure and oxygen-intermediate adsorption. Moreover, La enables dynamic self-adaptive stabilization of Fe sites, which mitigates the conventional activity–stability trade-off. This finding provides an avenue to rationally design efficient and selective electrocatalysts.

title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes.

title: A swing-type solid-state host–guest system enabling spontaneous adsorption–desorption cycling
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Macrocycle-based solid-state adsorbents offer molecularly precise platforms for the selective capture of volatile organic molecules. However, regeneration of these materials commonly relies on thermal or solvent stimulation, limiting energy efficiency and the recovery of adsorbed molecules. Developing solid-state adsorption systems that enable reversible guest release under mild conditions remains challenging, particularly for structurally similar volatile molecules. Here we show a swing-type solid-state host–guest system based on a fluorinated pillar[5]arene that enables reversible adsorption–desorption cycling of volatile methylpyridines at ambient temperature without heat or solvent stimulation. Competitive binding of nonvolatile electron-deficient acceptors drives the transformation of volatile guest inclusion phases into charge-transfer phases, releasing the volatile guests and producing a visible chromic response. Re-exposure to excess volatile vapor reverses the phase transformation, with the direction and extent of switching influenced by the relative stability of the competing host–guest assemblies and further modulated by guest size and lattice accessibility. These findings highlight an appropriate degree of thermodynamic proximity between competing solid-state complexes as an important design consideration for reversible guest exchange. More broadly, this strategy provides a route to adaptive macrocycle-based adsorbents for low-energy, visually traceable adsorption–desorption processes.

title: Observation of dark magnons in a van der Waals antiferromagnet/ferromagnet interface
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Magnons, the quanta of spin waves, offer a promising platform for low-power information processing owing to their charge-free propagation. Dark magnon modes, which are intrinsically decoupled from electromagnetic fields, exhibit high robustness against environmental perturbations and enable stealth-like propagation, making them highly attractive for magnonic applications. However, the excitation and detection of dark magnons in antiferromagnets remain highly challenging. Here, we report the direct observation of a magnon dark mode in a van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr interfaced with a ferromagnetic insulator YIG. In CrSBr, the canted (spin-flop) phase is nearly bypassed and the spin-flip phase has two magnon branches, one of which, the dark mode, has nearly zero net dynamic magnetization. We demonstrate that the interfacial exchange interaction enables the experimental detection of the magnon dark mode, while its presence is confirmed by the observation of coherent magnon-magnon coupling between YIG and CrSBr magnons. Micromagnetic simulations and a theoretical model reveal that the dark mode in CrSBr at the heterostructure interface hybridizes with YIG magnons via interfacial exchange interaction. Our results provide a new route for detecting dark magnon modes in antiferromagnets and open up opportunities for stealth-like magnon transport and hybrid magnonic devices based on van der Waals heterostructures.

title: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Acting as frontline sensors during cardiovascular injury, endothelial cells respond to acute ischemia by releasing exosomes as angiocrine signals for intercellular communication and cardioprotection. However, these endogenous signals are poorly utilized because released exosomes distribute systemically and show limited exposure in injured myocardium. Here we develop a systemically administered nanosystem for relocalizing circulating endothelial exosomes towards the myocardium, increasing their local availability. The nanosystem captures circulating endothelial exosomes, mediates their transvascular relocalization and promotes delivery to cardiomyocytes in the ischemic myocardium, thereby enhancing the local availability of native angiocrine signals. In a murine model of acute cardiac ischemia using male mice, this strategy increases endothelial exosome exposure in myocardium, improves cardiomyocyte survival, and preserves cardiac function. This approach enhances the reception of native angiocrine signals at the injured myocardium, therefore converting the originally diffuse, short-lived response into a sustained, organ-specific therapeutic exposure.

title: Origami-inspired folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels for thermal insulation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nanofiber aerogels (NFAs) are promising thermal insulation materials for extreme environments; however, simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness, resilience, and low thermal conductivity remains a long-standing challenge in layered NFAs, where interlaminar instability often compromises structural reliability. Here we present an origami-inspired structural engineering strategy to construct folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels. A folded-interlocked origami skeleton, integrated with a tailored interlaminar structure, introduces geometric confinement and fiber-mediated interlaminar toughening. As a result, the aerogels exhibit high compressive strength (548.02 kPa at 80% strain) and a near-zero Poisson’s ratio. Importantly, the robust interlaminar network enhances resistance to delamination, allowing the aerogels to sustain tensile deformation up to approximately 40% strain before interlaminar failure. Meanwhile, interlaminar-guided heat-flow redistribution yields a low axial thermal conductivity of 0.035 W m−1 K−1 and pronounced anisotropic thermal insulation. This work provides an architectural strategy for designing folded-interlocked NFAs for thermal protection in aerospace and other harsh environments.

title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti-inflammatory, barrier-reparative, and microbiota-modulating effects. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides (NZEP) by integrating nanozymes with yeast-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization-inspired strategy. Among them, NZEPTA-Ce, with the highest degree of nanozyme-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. Oral administration of NZEPTA-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair. Furthermore, NZEPTA-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities.

title: From ancient practice to modern innovation solving the clay mineral puzzle in brickmaking
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Clay minerals are the most crucial constituents in brickmaking clays, yet the specific role of different clay minerals remain poorly understood due to their natural coexistence and formidable challenges of separation. Here, we design a kaolinite-illite-quartz-feldspar system through a multiple-stage purification strategy, enabling direct evaluation of two of the most critical clay minerals for brick making - kaolinite and illite. Precise tuning the initial clay mineral assemblage yields brick strengths up to 8.5 times the ASTM C62 Grade MW requirement, without upgrading existing production methods. Mineralogical mechanisms responsible for substantial strength enhancement are revealed. Extensive analyses of 60 brick formulations uncovered a breakdown of conventional linear relationships among different brick properties due to the temperature-dependent responses of kaolinite and illite; specific formation pathways of mullite and amorphous phases; and over-firing defects above 1200 °C due to K+-induced fluxing from illite. Notably, a previously unrecognized negative correlation between mullite and brick strength is identified, suggesting a need to reconsider the widely held assumption of mullite as a strengthening phase. This work not only presents insights for optimizing high-strength brick formulations but also opens avenues for investigating the intricate contributions of distinct starting components to key brick performance.

title: Spectral sensing at a glance
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Portable biosensors are revolutionizing the way we diagnose disease and ill-health. By varying a metasurface’s geometry continuously across a chip, a recent study by H. Kim et al. reports a new sensing strategy, which reads signals from individual camera images without the need for a spectrometer. This enables the label-free detection of biomarkers in a handheld format.

title: Signatures of bi-altermagnetism revealed by sublattice-specific circular dichroism in resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: An altermagnet is a recently identified class of magnets that exhibit a zero net magnetic moment but break symmetry under the combined operations of parity and time reversal. It typically consists of two magnetic sites of opposite spins related by rotation within the unit cell. Here, we use circular dichroism (CD) in resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to reveal symmetry signatures of a distinct form of altermagnetism, namely bi-altermagnetism, in the correlated insulator Fe2Mo3O8, which comprises two altermagnetic sublattices: one with alternating quasi-octahedral Fe environments and the other with alternating tetrahedral Fe environments. We experimentally revealed the emergence of CD in an achiral, zero-magnetization system, thereby probing mirror-symmetry breaking associated with altermagnetic order. Notably, the CD appeared at sublattice-specific excitations of the octahedral and tetrahedral sites, indicating symmetry breaking in both altermagnetic sublattices. Calculations based on a model with the bi-altermagnetic order along the c axis successfully reproduce the observed CD. Our findings support the realization of bi-altermagnetism in Fe2Mo3O8, and showcase the use of RIXS-CD as a probe of magnetic sublattices in systems with zero net magnetization.

title: High-performance p-type two-dimensional transistors enabled by weak disorder engineering
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-performance field effect transistors (FETs) demand efficient charge doping alongside superior charge transport, which has proven challenging for p-type two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors. Conventional substitutional impurity doping often induces severe lattice damage and deep-level acceptor states within 2D semiconductors, severely deteriorating carrier transport. Here, we demonstrate weak disorder engineering (WD)—a mild two-step procedure involving sulfur vacancy creation and subsequent oxygen passivation—to simultaneously achieve efficient hole doping and exceptional hole transport in 2D semiconductors (e.g., MoS2 and WS2, collectively denoted as MS2). First-principles calculations reveal that oxygen-passivated sulfur vacancies suppress deep trap states while preserving near-valence-edge occupied states (NVOS), rationalizing the simultaneous hole doping and high hole mobility. Photoelectron spectroscopy indicates the Fermi level (EF) of WD-MS2 is shifted by ~ 240 meV toward the valence band. Structural and Raman characterizations show that the mild process preserves the lattice integrity of 2D semiconductors and introduces compressive strain. Owing to NVOS‑induced efficient hole doping, suppressed deep‑trap states, preserved lattice integrity, and engineered compressive strain, the p‑type 2D WD‑MS2 FETs deliver high hole mobilities, high on/off ratios, and large current densities. Furthermore, high‑gain, low‑power 2D Complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) inverters are constructed by integrating p‑type WD-WS2 FETs.

title: Clasping folds enable superior elastic strength of graphene films
abstract: Two-dimensional graphene sheets show strong potential for use in fabrication of macroscopic films, as they have exceptional mechanical properties owing to their in-plane strength1-6. Improvements in the stacking order of flat two-dimensional sheets have led to corresponding improvements in the strength and toughness of such films7-11. In addition, modulation of the spatial conformation of individual units has enabled the development of benchmark materials with superior properties12,13; however, this has remained elusive in the case of two-dimensional sheets. Here we report a strategy for preparation of graphene films with a combination of high strength (2.9 GPa), toughness (84.5 MJ m-3) and elastic strain (5%). We attribute these performance gains to a fold-clasping lamellar structure achieved by modular assembly of surface-folded multilayer graphene oxide flakes. We identify a pull-to-push transition of force chain topology and propose a shear-lock stress transfer strategy in the fold-clasping lamellar graphene film that enables advances in mechanical properties. This work demonstrates the modular design of spatial conformation of two-dimensional flakes on a large scale and further improves the performance of macroscopic films for potential applications in lightweight structural components.

title: Two-Dimensional IR Spectroscopy as a Window into the Molecular Structure and Dynamics of Electrolytes and Ionic Liquids: A Review
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional infrared (2DIR) spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for probing the structure and picosecond dynamics of complex, condensed-phase systems at the molecular level. In electrolytes and ionic liquids, where physicochemical properties arise from the interplay between solvation and ionic interactions, 2DIR spectroscopy provides unique insights into intermolecular interactions and dynamical processes that are often inaccessible to conventional spectroscopies. This review highlights seminal and recent advances in understanding the behavior of these systems using 2DIR spectroscopy, with particular emphasis on spectral diffusion, vibrational relaxation, and chemical exchange dynamics. The review also describes how complementary information from the vibrational modes of solvents, salts, and external probes enables detailed characterization of ion–ion interactions, hydrogen-bonding networks, and solvation environments, providing a molecular framework of the structure and time evolution of these charged systems. Moreover, particular attention is given to the dynamics of distinct molecular moieties and to the role of specific anions, cations, and solvent environments in governing behavior on femtosecond to picosecond time scales. Finally, the review describes current challenges, including the limited availability of intrinsic vibrational reporters and experimental constraints, and key open questions in electrochemical and energy-relevant systems that remain despite an extensive number of studies in the area.

title: Intrinsic physicochemical activity at microplastic–water interfaces
abstract: Plastics have become an integral part of our modern society, largely because they are generally regarded as chemically inert under normal circumstances. However, plastics fragmented into microplastics (less than 5 mm in size) have recently raised significant public concerns, and have been detected widely across ecosystems and human tissues with increasing environmental and health risks1, 2, 3, 4–5. Here we show that commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity in water, manifested by the spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species that increases with interfacial hydrophobicity and strongly correlates with interfacial electrostatics. Ab initio calculations support these observations and reveal that hydroxide oxidation becomes energetically more favourable at increasingly hydrophobic microplastic–water interfaces through the combined effects of partial solvation and electrostatics. These interfacial properties and the resulting oxidative chemistry have direct implications for biomolecular adsorption, protein aggregation, and even cellular damage. Together, our findings challenge the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, identify a possibly overlooked mechanism for the detrimental effects of microplastics on health and the environment, and contribute to a fundamental understanding of the structure–activity relationship of interfacial water, which may inform the design of safer and more sustainable plastic materials. Commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity at water interfaces, manifested by spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species, challenging the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, with implications for human health and the environment.

title: Gate-induced layer sliding drives non-volatile switching of magnetism in tetralayer graphene
abstract: Layer stacking in two-dimensional materials can strongly impact electronic phases. In graphene, for instance, the metastable rhombohedral stacking arrangement hosts correlated and topological electronic phases, which are absent in conventional Bernal stacking. Here we use the sliding-induced first-order structural phase transition between Bernal and rhombohedral tetralayer graphene driven by gate voltages to manipulate the magnetic phase of the sample. Through transport measurement on marginally twisted double-bilayer graphene samples, we observe bistable switching between a Bernal-dominant state and a rhombohedral-Bernal mixed state across a wide space of the gate-voltage phase diagram. The structural phase transition induces a non-volatile switching between a non-magnetic and a ferromagnetic phase. We characterize the latter phase via low-temperature electric transport measurements and observe an anomalous Hall effect. The sign reversal of the anomalous Hall signal under opposite displacement fields suggests that the Hall signal may originate from domain boundaries between Bernal and rhombohedral regions. Our experiments showcase how gating-induced sliding phase transitions of two-dimensional materials can provide on-demand toggle switching between complex phases and offer insights on the effect of stacking domain boundaries on the global response of the system.

title: Cryogenic shock exfoliation for ultrahigh mobility rhombohedral graphite nanoelectronics
abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene offers a tunable platform for correlated electron physics, featuring field-effect control of magnetic, superconducting and topological phases. The promise of these materials has been held back by the limited abundance of rhombohedral stacking in natural graphite, which constrains both sample yield and useful area. Here we introduce cryogenic shock exfoliation to produce large-area rhombohedral graphene flakes. This exfoliation, combined with a low-pressure van der Waals assembly technique that preserves stacking order, enables highly uniform devices exceeding 1,300 μm2 in area with fabrication yields of ∼90%. Using scanning nanoSQUID-on-tip imaging, we demonstrate uniform spin magnetism over the full central 10 × 10 μm2 area of our devices. Transverse magnetic focusing reveals a disorder mean free path exceeding 200 μm at low temperatures. Within the flat surface bands of rhombohedral multilayer graphene, we observe a size-driven crossover from Poiseuille to porous electron flow in the intermediate-temperature regime of strong electron-electron hydrodynamics, providing a further signature of ultrahigh device quality. Our approach overcomes a key materials bottleneck in the fabrication of mesoscopic rhombohedral graphene devices, paving the way for incorporating strongly correlated phases into two-dimensional nanoelectronics.

title: Unlocking Quantum Confinement in Two-/Three-Dimensional Tin-Based Perovskites for High-Efficiency Photovoltaics
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional/three-dimensional (2D/3D) mixed tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free photovoltaic absorbers, but uncontrolled crystallization produces excessive low-n phases that impede charge extraction due to a quantum confinement effect. Here, we employ 1,4-benzenediammonium iodide (1,4-BDI2) as a multifunctional additive to regulate crystallization, phase distribution, and defects. The additive modulates precursor colloid assembly and retards low-dimensional crystal growth, yielding dense films dominated by highly oriented three-dimensional perovskites with suppressed n = 1 and reduced n = 2 phases. Meanwhile, 1,4-BD2+ cations and unincorporated organic ligands accumulate at grain boundaries to form a passivating complex that passivates deep-trap states and forms favorable interfacial energy-level alignment to promote charge transfer. Consequently, inverted tin perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.94% and an open-circuit voltage of 0.91 V, together with improved operational and storage stability. This work establishes an integrated molecular strategy for phase regulation and defect passivation in efficient lead-free photovoltaics.

title: Carbon Monoxide Oxidation Enables Energy-Efficient Hydrogen Peroxide and Carbonate Coproduction from CO-Rich Flue Gas and Air
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The electrochemical carbon monoxide oxidation reaction (COOR) is an attractive anodic alternative to the oxygen evolution reaction, offering a route to lower the energy demand of electrosynthesis while utilizing abundant industrial waste gas. However, COOR has rarely been implemented in practical paired electrolysis systems because of modest device-level performance, reliance on purified CO feedstocks, and operational instability. Here, we establish a COOR∥two-electron oxygen reduction reaction paired electrolysis platform for H2O2 and CO32– coproduction using simulated CO-rich steelmaking flue gas. The system sustains bias-free operation for >140 h. Under high-current-density operation, in situ surface analysis revealed that interfacial carbonate accumulation causes anodic passivation and current decay. Pulsed electrolysis was introduced to alleviate such carbonate buildup and stabilized operation at 100 mA cm–2. Techno-economic analysis estimated an H2O2 minimum selling price of $0.71 kg–1. Together, these results establish COOR as a practical strategy for energy-efficient electrosynthesis using industrial waste gas.

title: Catalytic transfer of carbon atoms enables spirofusion of C–C σ-bonds
abstract: Spirocyclic frameworks, polycyclic structures in which two rings share a single carbon atom, constitute key structural motifs across diverse areas, including optoelectronic and hole-transporting materials1–3, ligand design for coordination complexes4–6, and numerous natural products7. In a spiro skeleton, the two molecular units adopt an orthogonal arrangement, generating a rigid three-dimensional (3D) architecture. Introducing a single carbon atom to join two components to form the spiro centre therefore represents a direct strategy for constructing such frameworks. Previous carbon-atom-transfer approaches have largely relied on π-bond reactivity, whereas controlled insertion of a carbon atom into C–C σ-bonds remains challenging8–11. Here we report a rhodium-catalysed spiro-carbon-atom insertion reaction that converts biphenylene substrates into spirocyclic structures through sequential C–C bond activation. Using N-isocyanoiminophosphorane (PINC)12–14 as an atomic carbon equivalent, the reaction forms four new C–C bonds at a spiro centre. The transformation enables both homo- and cross-spirofusion of biphenylenes and can be extended to reactions combining σ- and π-bond activation. These results establish a catalytic strategy for constructing structurally complex spirocyclic frameworks through C–C σ-bond activation, with a single carbon atom serving as a central linchpin.

title: Electric rectification by a redox-conductive metal-organic framework bilayer electrode
abstract: Redox-conductive metal-organic frameworks (RC-MOFs) combine molecularly tunable redox chemistry with crystalline, porous architectures. Stacking two RC-MOFs with different redox potentials creates a bilayer in which the direction of electron flow is governed by thermodynamically allowed interfacial redox reactions. This chemical rectification establishes RC-MOF bilayers as electrochemical diodes and provides a molecular strategy for programming directional charge transport.

title: Tautomeric Metal-Polymer Coordination Enables Damage-Free Laminated Carbon Electrodes in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Integrating dry carbon electrodes (CEs) into inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) offers a solvent-free, scalable route to low-cost photovoltaics. However, mechanical stress during lamination and the large work-function mismatch between the CE and the electron transport layer (ETL) can compromise performance. Here, we report an interface engineering strategy utilizing a silver-2-mercaptobenzothiazole (Ag-MBT) metal-polymer buffer layer to enable high-efficiency inverted CE-based PSCs (C-PSCs). XPS reveals Ag-induced changes in the sulfur and nitrogen chemical environments of MBT, consistent with the formation of an Ag-MBT interfacial coordination layer involving Ag–S coordination. This coordination-derived interlayer serves a dual function: it acts as a structural buffer, enabling damage-free dry CE lamination, and it establishes an energetic band alignment that bridges the ETL/CE work-function gap. Consequently, our devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.12% and maintain their initial efficiency after 1000 h of dark N2 storage, establishing metal-polymer interfacial coordination as a viable pathway for robust inverted C-PSCs.
