Mixed bone marrow (BM) chimeras reconstituted with wild-type and MBD3-deficient BM revealed a cell-intrinsic defect in thymic Treg cell lineage differentiation in MBD3-deficient cells. Transcriptional, phenotypic, and functional analyses of thymocyte subsets further revealed that MBD3 deficiency particularly affected the activation of a Treg-specific enhancer of the
                    Il2ra
                    gene encoding CD25, hence impaired CD25 expression in immature CD4 single-positive thymocytes (ImCD4SP) but not in peripheral T cells. The impairment markedly limited thymic Treg precursor cell generation and substantially reduced overall thymic Treg cell output. By contrast, MBD3 deficiency scarcely impacted the TGF-β/IL-2-dependent in vitro Treg cell generation from Tconv cells. Thus, Treg-specific developmental properties such as high IL-2/CD25 dependency of their thymic differentiation may render them more sensitive than Tconv cells to epigenetic changes of the whole T cell compartment. The results provide a mechanistic basis by which general epigenomic alterations in the T cell compartment can be causative of autoimmune and other immunological diseases through selectively affecting thymic Treg cell development.

title: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase–VB inhibition rescues brain endothelial stress and memory in Alzheimer’s disease models
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disorder with no effective cure, characterized by the cerebral parenchymal and vascular accumulation of aggregated amyloid-β (Aβ) and hyperphosphorylated tau. Cerebrovascular and mitochondria dysfunction are early causal events in the progression of AD. Previous studies support that inhibiting carbonic anhydrases (CAs) may prevent mitochondrial and cerebrovascular dysfunction in AD models. Here, we selectively target the mitochondrial CA isoform CA-VB by pharmacological and genetic manipulation in human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (hCMEC), and we confirm the protective effects of the CA-V inhibitor in AD mice. CA-V inhibition and CA-VB KO prevent Aβ induced mitochondria-mediated endothelial apoptosis, loss of barrier resistance, and hCMEC inflammatory activation. Strikingly, CA-V inhibition also mitigates caspase activation and endothelial cell activation in the brains of 3xTg AD mice, resulting in preserved memory function. Our results demonstrate that selective CA-V inhibition is an effective and promising strategy against AD-mediated cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment.

title: Maternal vaccination with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugates protects against murine Klebsiella pneumoniae neonatal sepsis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Klebsiella pneumoniae
                    is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and the foremost cause of infectious deaths in young children.
                    K. pneumoniae
                    isolates are becoming increasingly resistant to antibiotics, creating a great need for additional therapies or preventative strategies. Maternal vaccination serves as an attractive approach to protect from
                    K. pneumoniae
                    neonatal sepsis. Herein, we report a murine model of maternal immunization followed by pup challenge to evaluate putative
                    K. pneumoniae
                    vaccines. Dams were immunized with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugate vaccines at mating and boosted with two different immunization schedules throughout the gestational period. After parturition, offspring were tested for antigen-specific antibody levels and later challenged with a lethal dose of
                    K. pneumoniae.
                    Pups born to dams immunized with K1- and K2-conjugate vaccines demonstrated significant protection from sepsis relative to control pups. Antibodies transferred from vaccinated dams persisted and remained protective in pups for at least six weeks after birth. Collectively these results demonstrate a feasible and reproducible murine model of maternal immunization verifying the efficacy of bioconjugate vaccines in protecting against lethal neonatal
                    K. pneumoniae
                    infection.

title: Spectral tuning and signaling of diverse and far red–sensitive rhodopsins in mantis shrimp eyes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Stomatopod crustaceans (mantis shrimps) have extraordinary eyes with unmatched visual rhodopsin diversity, but their potential for broad color detection remains unclear. Here, we report that 17 rhodopsins, mostly from the midband eye region, are involved in color sensing and functionally diverse signaling via Gq/Gi coupling and describe the underlying mechanisms of spectral tuning. Two mid-wavelength rhodopsins preferentially absorb blue light and a majority of long-wavelength opsins absorb in the green range, but three absorb light beyond 600 nanometers, representing exquisite far red–sensitive animal rhodopsins. Several blue and red rhodopsins exhibit photoreversibility with opposite spectral shifts explained by retinal binding interactions, revealing unrecognized photochemical flexibility in stomatopod photoreception. Row-specific spectral sensitivity results from combining carotenoid filters with multiple individually tuned rhodopsins, altogether extending broad vision to the far-red spectrum.

title: TIME FOR COFFEE coordinates phase separation and chromatin regulation for salt tolerance
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The circadian clock enhances plant fitness by aligning internal timing with the external photoperiod, but how it coordinates spatiotemporal regulation with chromatin dynamics to improve salt tolerance is not well understood. Here, we show that the clock component TIME FOR COFFEE (TIC) forms biomolecular condensates in response to salt stress, but not to osmotic stress alone. Consistently,
                    tic
                    mutants were hypersensitive to salt stress yet displayed enhanced salt tolerance under 21-hour light-dark cycles matching their shortened circadian period, highlighting the importance of circadian clock in salt tolerance. Salt stress increases H3K9ac levels at the salt stress–responsive genes and induces their expression in a time-of-day–dependent manner in wild-type plants, whereas both H3K9ac level and transcriptional activation are attenuated in
                    tic
                    mutants. TIC physically associates with HD2-type histone deacetylases, and a subset of HD2 partially colocalizes with TIC condensates in the nucleolus under salt stress. Genetic and biochemical analyses showed that salt stress promotes TIC condensate formation, accompanied by reduced HD2 occupancy at salt stress–responsive loci, thereby elevating H3K9ac levels and promoting gene expression. Together, these findings uncover a mechanism by which salt-induced TIC condensate formation links chromatin regulation with circadian timing, thereby promoting plant adaptation to salt stress.

title: Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ and the enduring value of old ideas
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Alaska’s Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ looks a lot like fluted point sites south of the North American ice sheets. Archaeologists have expected this for 60 years.

title: Rewilding the atoll engine
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Seabirds and native forests reconnect ocean, reef, and island processes, strengthening the physical foundations of atoll resilience.

title: Ice-ray pentagonal packing of pseudo-fivefold helices
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
While fivefold point symmetry is common in nature, fivefold spatial symmetry is seldom observed. Regular pentagons cannot tile a plane without leaving voids, and even the densest “ice-ray” packing is exceptionally rare. Fivefold helices are equally elusive. We report a small molecule that self-assembles into hydrogen-bonded pseudo-fivefold helices and adopts an ice-ray pentagonal packing motif over crystallographic length scales using peripheral disorder that partially occupies regions that would otherwise be void in an ideal pentagonal tessellation. The resulting structure exhibits weak and nondirectional interhelical interactions within the (
                    bc
                    ) plane and comparatively strong and directional intrahelical hydrogen bonding along the
                    a
                    axis. This structural anisotropy gives rise to single crystals with large aspect ratios and distinct mechanical behavior. This realization of two rare structural motifs within a single crystal shows the capability of simple organic molecules to form complex structures and highlights an untapped potential for symmetry engineering in molecular solids through the interplay of intermolecular interactions with pronounced differences in strength and directionality.

title: Plasmonic metasurface microfluidic accelerates redox reactions for rapid phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Electron-accepting chain reactions play crucial roles in diagnostics for bacterial infections, from nucleic acid amplification for bacterial identification to metabolic assays for phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing. When coupled with redox mediators, these reactions can be interrogated using an electroanalytical method. We demonstrate kinetic acceleration of loop-mediated isothermal amplification–based identification and resazurin-based phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility profiling through enhanced electromagnetic fields and modulated hot electron injection at the multilayered plasmonic metasurface-fluidic interface. We systematically investigate rounded versus sharp-apex plasmonic architectures, quantifying near-field magnitude and decay to identify geometries that maximize kinetic amplification under electrochemical readout. This approach is further combined with machine learning–assisted Gaussian fitting to improve data quantification and interpretation. Across diverse bacterial species, we achieved rapid identification with no cross-reactivity and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing without overnight culture. In a prospective pilot clinical study of urine specimens directly from patients with suspected urinary tract infections, we observe high accuracy and strong essential and categorical agreement with standard clinical microbiology assays for bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

title: Remote allosteric control of single-atom Cu sites in Zr-MOFs enables selective CH4 hydroxylation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Highly selective oxidation of methane to liquid oxygenates under mild conditions remains challenging because of the difficulty in controlling overoxidation at highly reactive sites. Here, we demonstrate remote control of single-atom Cu reactivity through outer-shell coordination engineering in Zr-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). By anchoring Cu
                    1
                    to Zr-oxo nodes in UiO-66-X (X = -NO
                    2
                    , -H, and -CH
                    3
                    ), remote X-BDC ligands systematically modulate the electronic properties of Cu
                    1
                    sites and the catalytic microenvironment. In situ characterization combined with ab initio molecular dynamics in an explicitly solvated aqueous environment reveals a dynamic outer-shell-to-inner-shell regulation that reshapes the active structure and reactive oxygen species around Cu
                    1
                    sites, thereby facilitating CH
                    4
                    activation. In particular, the electron-withdrawing NO
                    2
                    -BDC ligand creates electron-deficient Cu
                    1
                    -
                    •
                    OH* sites, while adsorbed water further regulates active-site conformation. Consequently, Cu
                    1
                    /U6-NO
                    2
                    achieves a turnover frequency of 322.4 h
                    −1
                    with nearly 100% oxygenate selectivity under mild conditions, establishing a general strategy for overcoming activity-selectivity trade-offs in methane conversion.

title: A “Progenitor Cell Ark” hydrogel system for intervertebral disc regeneration via mitochondrial targeting and mitophagy enhancement
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), driven by progenitor cell loss and oxidative stress, remains a major clinical challenge with limited effective regenerative therapies. Here, we present a “Progenitor Cell Ark,” a triple-layered hydrogel microsphere system designed for synergistic cell delivery and microenvironment remediation. The Ark comprises an outer nucleus pulposus progenitor cell (NPPC) layer for cell replenishment, a middle GelMA/HAMA scaffold for support, and an inner SS31-modified ultrasmall Prussian blue nanozyme (SS31-UPN) layer that specifically targets mitochondria to scavenge ROS and promote mitophagy. In vitro, SS31-UPN effectively protected NPPCs from oxidative damage, restored mitochondrial function, and enhanced mitophagy. Critically, in severe IVDD rat models, the Progenitor Cell Ark significantly improved intervertebral disc structure, promoted neo-tissue formation, and restored biomechanical function, outperforming cell or bioscaffold therapy alone. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that SS31-UPN’s mitochondrial targeting enhances mitophagy, drives ECM and energy metabolic remodeling, and preserves NPPC stemness, thereby creating a proregenerative milieu. This integrated “cell-in-a-box” strategy offers a robust platform for reversing IVDD and holds notable translational potential for regenerative medicine.

title: Deep learning reveals ecological decoupling and rate heterogeneity in Hymenoptera wing evolution
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Quantifying biomorphological evolution and integrating phenotypic data into large-scale ecological and evolutionary studies are often limited by the scalability, subjectivity, and poor interpretability of existing methods. We introduce HAIKA (Hierarchical Attention-based Interpretable K-dimensional Autoencoder), a self-supervised residual channel-attention autoencoder that extracts continuous morphological representations from unlabeled standardized images and highlights the image regions that contribute to those representations. Applied to insect forewings across broad pterygote lineages, HAIKA outperformed most baseline deep learning models and conventional descriptors in clustering, dimensionality reduction, and morphological embedding. When applied to Hymenoptera (i.e., ants, bees, and wasps), the HAIKA-derived continuous characters improved morphology-based phylogenetic reconstruction and illuminated the evolutionary dynamics of wing shape and venation. Our results reveal that wing morphological evolution in Hymenoptera proceeds at decoupled rates across shape and venation modules and is not consistently aligned with key ecological transitions such as parasitoidism or eusociality. HAIKA provides a scalable, image-based route for phenotypic analyses, broadly applicable across diverse taxa and to both 2D and 3D datasets.

title: Humans experienced abrupt environmental changes at White Sands during the Last Glacial Maximum
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park have unearthed 20 stratigraphic horizons containing in situ human footprints, megafaunal trackways, and linear features created by travois. Advances in radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, combined with ages of aquatic seeds, refines the chronology of the footprint-bearing sequence to between 23.5 and 21.7 thousand years ago (ka). Biomarker, pollen, and stratigraphic evidence indicate a complete overturning of the environment from a perennial lake to a playa and capture a large aridification episode coincident with Dansgaard-Oeschger event 2 at 23.2 ka, which shrank pluvial Lake Otero and allowed people to traverse the former shoreline area for nearly two millennia. This well-dated and highly resolved paleoclimate record provides compelling evidence that humans in North America experienced marked environmental changes during the Last Glacial Maximum.

title: Sustainable solar water purification: Exploring the structural advantages of higher plants
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Solar vapor generation is a promising technique for water purification, although the development of efficient and sustainable systems for practical use remains challenging. Here, we introduce a higher plant–derived evaporator, leveraging the structural advantages of plants and the synergistic integration of multiple components, including carbon black–coated ultrathin wood slices with perforated pores, nanocellulose aerogel, and vertically aligned wheat straws. This configuration facilitates low-tortuosity water transport within the internal framework while promoting interfacial evaporation at its surface. Under 1 sun, the evaporator achieved an evaporation rate of up to 3.2 kilograms per square meter (kg m
                    −2
                    ) per hour. The material’s scalability and the capability to continuously collect clean water in outdoor environments were successfully demonstrated. Outdoors, under a solar intensity of 0.5 to 0.9 sun, the assembled device achieved a daily fresh water yield of up to 10.9 kg m
                    −2
                    from seawater. With highly accessible renewable raw materials, low production cost, and exceptional water purification efficiency, this cost-effective solar evaporator is edge closer to viable, real-world applications.

title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Together, our findings uncover a fast-acting iron homeostasis pathway in plants that dynamically couples nutrient availability with immunity, thereby shaping host microbe interactions at the onset of infection.

title: Ultrasound-driven electronically programmable microbubbles
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Ultrasound-actuated microbubbles have served as efficient microscale engines demonstrating wireless actuation, simplified robotic architectures, and rapid response. Despite recent advances, a limitation of many microbubble technologies is that they use passive capturing of bubbles. The lack of control over bubble placement and size hinders the ability to individually address specified bubbles, a feature that would be important for performing multiple functions. Here, we present an on-chip bubble customization platform that enables active control of individual microbubbles. Instead of trapping bubbles, we purposely generate them via electrolysis on electrode arrays. The bubbles, when actuated by an external ultrasound input, create a variety of programmed flows ranging from streaming due to volumetric oscillation of a single bubble to diverse symmetry-broken directional flows when multiple bubbles interact. The bubble configuration can also be altered by simply increasing the electrolysis voltage on specified electrodes to detach the unneeded bubbles. We find that in this regime, when coupled to acoustic oscillations, we can generate a distinct bubble shooting flow pattern whose flow direction is selectively controlled by the incident ultrasound frequency. Collectively, the active bubble reconfiguration ability unlocks a range of previously inaccessible acoustofluidic functions in a single device with unprecedented controllability.

title: The network structure of the urban revolution
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Long-distance interaction has deep prehistoric roots, but the networks that emerged during the Urban Revolution were unprecedented in scale and organization. How early cities sustained this extensive connectivity in the absence of formal markets or centralized states remains a fundamental question. Focusing on the Uruk Expansion in Mesopotamia (ca. 3900 to 3000 BCE), we assemble the largest spatial dataset currently available and reconstruct transportation networks across three successive phases. Using network analysis, we show that an initially dendritic, river-based system evolved into modular regional clusters and ultimately into a more integrated structure linked by selective long-distance shortcuts. This transformation reduced dependence on key intermediaries and generated small world–like patterns combining strong local cohesion with efficient system-wide reach. These results demonstrate that decentralized interaction processes, supported in part by mobile intermediary communities, played a central role in sustaining early urban connectivity.

title: Photomapping electrically coupled networks of the mature thalamus and cortex
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Electrical synapses are expressed ubiquitously across the brain and are crucial components of active neural circuitry and connectomes. Identification of coupled networks in living tissue is limited by technical demands of multiplexed recordings, and no dyes, fluorescent reporters, or genetic labels can now fill the gap. We introduce a novel method of identifying and quantifying electrical synapses, opto-δ
                    L
                    , that combines focal photostimulation of soma-targeted opsins with a spike timing–based computation for the strength of electrical synapses to rapidly measure and map electrically coupled networks in vitro. We leverage opto-δ
                    L
                    to show that coupled networks of the mature thalamic reticular nucleus extend as far as 100 micrometers, synapse promiscuously across genetic subtypes of neurons, and couple one to four neighboring neurons to each recorded hub cell. We applied opto-δ
                    L
                    to cortical networks, where we found that somatostatin neurons were more strongly and prevalently coupled. These results highlight the broad potential of opto-δ
                    L
                    to interrogate the identity and roles of electrical synapses in circuitry, behavior, and cognition.

title: An inspiration-off attractor supports the robust and flexible control of breathing
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Breathing is a fundamental motor rhythm necessary to sustain life. The rhythm and pattern of breathing arises from the coordination of a rostrocaudally extended ventral respiratory column (VRC) in the medulla. Although recurrent excitation is sufficient for rhythmic bursting in reduced in vitro preparations, comparatively less is understood about how inhibition and excitation interact with feedback circuits to generate the breathing rhythm in vivo. Here, we expand on the classical “inspiratory-off switch” model that inhibitory signaling from lung stretch afferent pathways plays a critical role in generating the breathing rhythm in vivo. We perform high-density extracellular recordings along the length of the VRC during optogenetic and physiological manipulations and apply computational analyses to characterize how these perturbations govern low-dimensional neural dynamics. We show that stimulation of GABAergic afferents of the nucleus of the solitary tract advance or delay breathing in a manner similar to, but quantitatively distinct from, inhibition local to the VRC. We use generative dynamical models to show that inhibitory activity controls respiratory activity through transient stabilization of an attractive region of the low-dimensional manifold corresponding to expiration. Together, these results propose an “inspiratory-off attractor” model that underlies network level control of breathing in vivo.

title: Rising global population coexposure to heatwaves and landscape fire-sourced air pollution
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Landscape fires are increasingly threatening public health by causing substantial fire-sourced air pollution (SFAP), with risks amplified during heatwaves. We investigated the global spatial, temporal, and sociodemographic distribution of the population coexposure to heatwaves and SFAP from 2000 to 2019. We found that 52.4% of populated areas and 55.9% of the global population experienced increasing coexposure. On average, 916 million people per year were exposed to at least one coexposure day, increasing by 287 million people per decade. The global annual average exposed days per person was 1.3 days, rising from 1.0 days in 2000–2009 to 1.7 days in 2010–2019. Coexposure person-days increased by 5.5 billion per decade, of which 70.5% was attributable to increasing coexposure intensity and 29.5% to population growth. Countries with a low human development index (HDI) experienced the highest coexposure days per person and the greatest increases. These findings provide high-resolution data to inform health impact assessments and target mitigation and adaptation strategies.

title: How inequality became durable before states: Evidence from 6000 years in the Central Plain of China
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: How did durable inequality emerge before the rise of states? Drawing on a synthesis of previously published mortuary data from more than 2300 burials, together with isotopic, zooarchaeological, and osteological data spanning nearly 6000 years (7000 to 1500 BCE) in the prehistoric Central Plain of China, we reconstruct long-term patterns of relational mortuary inequality. We show that inequality followed a strongly nonlinear trajectory and cannot be explained primarily by agricultural intensification or population scale. Instead, substantial disparities were structured by differential positions within social-relational networks that mediated access to labor, resources, and symbolic capital. Transformations in subsistence, the rise of mobile and appropriable wealth, and escalating conflict reorganized these networks, concentrating ritual and political-military power and technological control. Early states stabilized rather than created these preexisting disparities by institutionalizing control over resources, violence, and network-based access. These findings highlight the central role of social networks in shaping durable inequality before formal state institutions.

title: Bioinspired supramolecular thermistor for resolving subtle temperature variations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Precise detection of subtle temperature variations under cryogenic conditions is critical for environmental monitoring but remains challenging because conventional thermistors suffer from limited sensitivity and mechanical interference. Here, we report a bioinspired supramolecular thermistor that achieves thermal transduction through molecularly gated charge transport. The hybrid polyurethane/carboxymethyl cellulose (PU/CMC)/MXene/NiO composite integrates dynamic hydrogen-bond reconfiguration, hydrated ionic conduction, and temperature-dependent electronic transport. Upon cooling, cooperative supramolecular evolution continuously modulates coupled ionic and electronic pathways, producing an ultrahigh negative temperature coefficient of −22,280% °C
                    −1
                    between −80° and −75°C. The thermistor resolves detectable temperature changes below 0.01°C while maintaining negligible hysteresis, excellent reproducibility, and effective thermal-mechanical decoupling. Combined with a dedicated low-noise readout circuit, it enables reliable monitoring of subtle temperature evolution during simulated atmospheric cooling. Integrated into a multichannel sensor array, it further provides force-independent thermal mapping for robotic manipulation. This work establishes molecularly gated supramolecular thermal transduction as a strategy for ultrahigh-resolution cryogenic temperature sensing.

title: Highlights from an early base camp in Beringia 13,800 years ago: Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ and the Late Pleistocene peopling of Alaska
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Human dispersal across the Bering Land Bridge (BLB) was a key event in the peopling of the Americas, but Beringia’s archaeological record remains poorly understood. In response, the Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ site in interior Alaska has been the focus of a multi-disciplinary study since 2016. The site contains three archaeological components dating to the Late Pleistocene, 13.8, 13, and 12.7 thousand years ago. The oldest component yielded an expressive array of cultural remains, including a unique hafted-biface form, osseous tools, diverse fauna, and well-preserved activity areas, a record unparalleled for this age in Beringia. Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ represents the earliest known Nenana Complex occupation east of the BLB, and its distinct hafted-biface form occurs in coeval sites west of the BLB, providing an important trans-Beringian cultural link. Although not Beringia’s oldest site, Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ reveals important information about Late Glacial peopling and settling-in behavior in this far northern setting.

title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse Malat1 long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
In most cells,
                    Malat1
                    long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons,
                    Malat1
                    is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame. In vivo chemical probing and structural modeling defined a three-stem-loop RNA secondary structure that encompasses the active IRES segment and coincides with a mouse B1 SINE (short interspersed element) repetitive element. In affinity purification experiments, a minimal IRES/B1 RNA selectively bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors, and the known IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1. Depletion of Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 inhibited IRES-dependent translation of the reporter and expression of the endogenous M1 peptide. Our study identifies an unexpected functional unit hidden within a widely studied long noncoding RNA.

title: Global conservation additionality hindered by persisting fishing pressure in marine protected areas
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are the cornerstone of global marine conservation strategies. Yet, their capacity to achieve conservation gains (i.e., conservation additionality) hinges on the decrease in human threats to biodiversity within their boundary, a feature rarely measured or reported. Here, we test a central but underexamined question in global conservation policy: Have MPA implementations actually reduced within-boundary fishing pressure, currently the main direct human threat to marine biodiversity? Using a stratified before-after-control-impact approach, we investigated 861 MPAs of varying levels of protection across all ocean basins, representing half of global MPA coverage, and found that most implementations were not followed by decreases in industrial fishing effort. Protection levels strongly predicted the direction and magnitude of relative changes in fishing effort after implementation. Only fully protected areas were associated with significant decreases in fishing effort within boundaries. Highly protected areas were only associated with lower rates of increase in fishing effort within compared to outside boundaries. Both fully and highly protected areas were implemented in areas experiencing initial low fishing effort, reducing the overall abatement in fishing effort achieved. Conversely, areas with higher initial fishing effort tended to be attributed to MPAs with low levels of protection, also limiting abatement. Larger MPAs were associated with greater decreases in fishing effort, while time since implementation had no significant effect. Complementing targets of protection coverage and protection levels with conservation additionality targets, such as pressure abatement, could shift incentives from quantity to effectiveness of interventions and ensure positive biodiversity conservation outcomes.

title: Bedrock erodibility governs transient erosion and CO2 release in alpine landscapes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Differences in lithology within alpine watersheds lead to strong contrasts in bedrock erodibility, which modulate climatic and tectonic influences on erosion, chemical weathering, and carbon dioxide exchange. However, the difficulty of measuring denudation rates in fine-grained rocks has limited our ability to quantify the magnitude of erodibility differences between weak sedimentary and strong igneous rocks. Here, we combine newly developed cosmogenic beryllium-10 measurements in shale with conventional beryllium-10 measurements in intrusive rocks, topographic analysis, solute data, and landscape evolution modeling in the East River watershed, Colorado. Shale-dominated catchments denude three times faster than adjacent intrusive catchments despite having gentler topography. Hydrochemical data and modeling indicate that elevated shale denudation enhances solute generation and net inorganic weathering–driven carbon dioxide release during prolonged landscape adjustment over million-year timescales. These results show that spatial variability in rock type alone can substantially alter the carbon dioxide balance of alpine landscapes by hiding the fastest erosion rates in relatively gentle terrain.

title: Vitamin D binding protein in ventral CA3 of the hippocampus drives stress-induced depression
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The ventral hippocampus plays a crucial role in regulating emotional and motivated behaviors. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its dysfunction in major depressive disorder (MDD) remain poorly understood. Here, we identified elevated expression of vitamin D binding protein (VDBP) in the hippocampi of chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)–susceptible mice, which correlated with the severity of depression-like behaviors. Notably, VDBP up-regulation was specifically in ventral CA3 excitatory (vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    ) neurons. CA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    VDBP overexpression led to inhibited neuronal activity, synaptic and dendritic impairments, and, ultimately, depression-like behaviors. Conversely, vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    -specific VDBP knockdown enhanced resilience to chronic stress. Mechanistically, VDBP directly interacted with PIK3R3 to inhibit the PI3K-Akt-mTOR pathway in a cell-autonomous manner, leading to excessive autophagy and subsequent neuronal dysfunction. Chemogenetic activation, intervention using the Akt-specific activator SC79, and site-specific mutation disrupting the VDBP-PIK3R3 interaction ameliorated vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    VDBP-induced depression-like phenotypes. Collectively, these findings underscore the critical involvement of vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    neuron–derived VDBP in stress-induced depressive pathology and highlight its potential as a therapeutic target for MDD.

title: Shading enhances Se accumulation in tea leaves through promoting CsMYB7-like-mediated conversion of Se (VI) to Se (IV)
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Limited selenium (Se) accumulation in agricultural products contributes to widespread dietary Se deficiency, posing a global nutritional threat. Efficient agronomic strategies to enhance Se biofortification in crops are still lacking. Here, we reveal the synergistic effects of shading and Se nanoparticles application on Se biofortification in tea leaves. Field experiments demonstrate that shading enhances Se accumulation in tea leaves under sufficient Se supply, through activating Se metabolism pathway. We identify CsAPR1 functions at the early stage of Se assimilation, catalyzing the reduction of Se (VI). The transcription of
                    CsAPR1
                    is activated by CsMYB7-like and is further promoted by shading through interaction with CsbHLH70. Under sunlight, CsHY5 competes with CsbHLH70 for binding to CsMYB7-like, thereby attenuating CsMYB7-like-mediated transcription of
                    CsAPR1
                    and suppressing Se accumulation in tea plants. Our findings reveal the molecular mechanisms underlying shade-induced enhancement of Se biofortification, offering insights and strategies for Se-enriched crop production.

title: Radical-induced autoxidation dominates squalene oxidative aging under environmental conditions
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Ozone has been viewed as the principal oxidant of skin oils and other unsaturated surface films, but their fate under realistic indoor conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use squalene (SQ), a major component of skin lipids, to investigate the dominant oxidation pathways in occupied indoor environments and laboratory flow reactors. With exposure to indoor air, SQ decay and reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation accelerated over time, consistent with autoxidation. Laboratory experiments with ozone alone drove first-order SQ loss and humidity-dependent emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). In contrast, exposure to both ozone and
                    •
                    OH produced nonexponential SQ decays, higher ROS yields, a much stronger in-film
                    •
                    OH source, and condensed-phase products enriched in highly oxidized organic hydroperoxides that closely match those observed indoors. Unexpectedly, gas-phase
                    •
                    OH strongly suppressed VOC emissions. These results demonstrate that gas-phase radical-induced autoxidation governs SQ aging, challenging the prevailing ozone-centric view of indoor skin oil oxidation.

title: Nonlinear Electro‐Optic Visible Photonic Circuits for Solid‐State Quantum Defects
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Integrated visible photonic engines for solid‐state quantum defects provide a foundation for scalable quantum networks. While miniaturization is advancing, active manipulation remains limited by the difficulty of achieving simultaneous milliwatt‐scale visible light generation and high‐contrast modulation. Despite extensive efforts, the concurrent chip‐scale realization of nonlinear frequency conversion and fast temporal gating for high‐fidelity quantum control has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate a monolithic thin‐film lithium niobate (TFLN) platform integrating periodically poled frequency conversion with GHz‐bandwidth electro‐optic (EO) switching. The device delivers off‐chip green‐light power exceeding 1 mW with an extinction ratio (ER) of 42.2 dB, enabling coherent spin control and time‐resolved lifetime measurements of individual nitrogen‐vacancy (NV) centers in diamond through nanosecond gating. System performance is validated through pulsed optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR), Rabi oscillations, and Ramsey interference, supported by time‐tagged photon counting with nanosecond resolution. By unifying sufficient nonlinear light generation with high‐speed active manipulation, this platform establishes a scalable framework for the realization of high‐rate quantum communication nodes.

title: A Universal Spin‐Polarization‐Engineered Antibonding‐Orbital Modulation Paradigm for Accelerating Reaction Kinetics in Ultrahigh‐Rate Sodium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Conversion‐type anode materials hold great promise for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), yet their practical rate performance is fundamentally constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics beyond mass‐transport limitations. Despite notable advances in accelerating ion/electron transport, intrinsically reducing the large reaction kinetic barrier and activation energy associated with robust metal–chalcogen (M─S) bonds remains a long‐standing challenge. In this study, we propose a universal spin‐polarization‐engineered (SPE) antibonding‐orbital modulation paradigm to fundamentally regulate M─S bond strength and enable ultrahigh‐rate sodium storage. As a proof of concept, magnetic manganese heteroatom doping into heterojunctions enhances the saturation magnetization by ∼210%, inducing a spin‐state transition from low‐spin to high‐spin configurations, which increases the electron occupation of antibonding orbitals formed between metal e g orbitals and chalcogen p orbitals, and thereby regulates M─S bond strength. Benefiting from this spin‐engineered electronic reconstruction, Mn‐FeS 2 /CoS 2 anode delivers an ultrahigh‐rate capability of 300 mA h g −1 at 120 A g −1 , together with exceptional long‐term durability (∼100% retention over 13 000 cycles at 100 A g −1 ), ranking among the best record. The generality of this strategy is further validated by extending SPE modulation to other magnetic dopants. Moreover, the industrial‐level pouch cell is assembled to demonstrate the practical potential of this strategy.

title: Turning Nd‐Fe‐B Swarf Into High‐Value Bulk Feedstocks via Sustainable Hydrogen Plasma: From Rare‐Earth Oxides to Metals and Hydrides
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Rare‐earth permanent magnets (REPMs) are crucial for electric vehicles, wind turbines, and other high‐efficiency electric motor systems. However, their production is energy‐intensive, and global recycling rates are below 0.2%. Machining swarf is the main industrial waste from REPMs production. Despite its high rare‐earth elements (REEs) content (∼20 wt.%), it has received limited attention for sustainable recycling. We introduce hydrogen plasma reduction (HPR) as a new environmentally friendly method to recover REEs from REPM swarf. By tuning the hydrogen content and treatment time, we achieve phase separation into metallic Fe and a Nd 2 O 3 ‐rich rare‐earth fraction, providing a concentrated intermediate for subsequent REPM production. The process also enables direct rare‐earth hydride formation, confirming the plasma‐assisted partial rare‐earth metallization in the molten state. This procedure turns REPM swarf into separated, high‐value, high‐purity feedstock in a single, acid‐free step. Against the ∼70 kg CO 2 ‐eq kg −1 footprint of conventional REPM production, this recycling route offers a pathway toward substantially lower‐emission magnet production while reducing reliance on primary REE supply.

title: Molecular Design of Fluorinated Ester Electrolytes via Skeleton Regulation Enables Aggressive Cathode Chemistries in 5V‐Class Fast‐Charging Lithium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐ion batteries can deliver higher energy densities when using high‐voltage cathodes such as LiNi 0.5 Mn 1.5 O 4 (LNMO), yet their practical application is hindered by the catalytic nature of high‐voltage cathode materials which usually cause electrolytes decomposition. Although the utilization of fluorinated carbonates as electrolyte solvent considerably inhibited the parasitic reaction at cathode side, the irrational fluorination often leads to the sluggish Li + transport which finally causes poor rate performance. Here, we design a family of trifluoromethyl‐substituted carboxylate esters as electrolyte solvents. We found that the spatial arrangement between the ‐CF 3 and the carbonyl group in these fluorinated esters is critical for regulating the electrolyte solvation structures. A short distance (α‐substitution) severely weakens the solvating power of the solvent, resulting in a substantial decrease in ionic conductivity, whereas an extended separation (γ‐substitution) compromises the oxidation resistance against high‐voltage cathodes. Only the trifluoromethylation at the β‐position yields optimal solvent (methyl 3,3,3‐trifluoropropionate, MTFP) that can simultaneously meets high‐voltage and fast‐charging requirements of LNMO||Gr cells when pairing with fluoroethylene carbonate and 1 M LiPF 6 . In such electrolyte, the Ah‐level LNMO||Gr pouch cells deliver 78% capacity retention at 6C charge/discharge rate (13.2 mA cm −2 ), and stably operate over 300 cycles at the high rate of 3C.

title: Local Coordination Asymmetry Engineering Activates Oxide Path Mechanism in Dopant‐Free RuO2 for Ultra‐Durable Acidic Water Oxidation
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing ruthenium‐based anode electrocatalysts to replace commercial iridium is crucial for reducing the cost of proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis. However, conventional RuO 2 suffers from limited long‐term stability and severe overoxidation drawbacks. Herein, we employ dynamic H 2 bubble template (DHBT)‐assisted electrodeposition combined with calcination to fabricate disorderly connected regular/irregular Ru‐O 6 octahedra. In situ experiments and theoretical calculations reveal that this local coordination asymmetry favors an oxide path mechanism (OPM) involving direct O‐O coupling while suppressing *OOH formation and substantial lattice‐oxygen participation. The optimized d‐RuO 2‐x catalyst requires an overpotential of only 154 mV to reach 10 mA cm −2 and maintains stable operation for over 3200 h at this current density. Crucially, in a PEM water electrolyzer, the catalyst operates robustly for over 2100 h at 200 mA cm −2 under continuous and start‐shutdown conditions. These results demonstrate that local coordination asymmetry engineering can tune OER pathway selection in dopant‐free RuO 2 ‐based catalysts and provide a promising route toward durable acidic OER anodes.

title: Antiferrodistortive Matrix Engineering Reprograms Polarization Pathways for Ultrahigh Energy Storage at Moderate Electric Fields
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Relaxor ferroelectrics (RFEs) are promising dielectric materials for pulsed multilayer ceramic capacitors because of their rapid polarization response. However, under practical electric fields, polarization rapidly approaches saturation as polar nanoregions exhaust their nonlinear switching capability, fundamentally limiting energy‐storage performance. Here we demonstrate that antiferrodistortive matrix engineering reprograms the polarization evolution pathway through a polarization dormancy–awakening process. Long‐range antiferrodistortive modulation, introduced by the intrinsic lattice instability of CaZrO 3 in a (Bi 0.5 Na 0.4 K 0.1 )TiO 3 matrix, creates local strain fields that temporarily suppress PNR switching and progressively awaken dormant polarization under moderate electric fields. This substantially extends the nonlinear polarization‐response regime without inducing ferroelectric or antiferroelectric ordering. Atomic‐resolution electron microscopy, electron diffraction, and phase‐field simulations collectively reveal the structural origin of the awakening behavior and its coupling to local polarization dynamics. Consequently, the engineered relaxor ceramic achieves an ultrahigh recoverable energy‐storage density of 12.3 J cm – 3 with an energy‐storage efficiency of 87.4% at 520 kV cm – 1 , representing a benchmark performance for bulk RFE ceramics operating under moderate electric fields. This work establishes antiferrodistortive matrix engineering as a promising design strategy for reprogramming polarization evolution in RFEs toward high‐performance dielectric energy storage.

title: Asymmetric Interfacial Charge Gradients Enable Dual‐Pathway Proton Transfer for High‐Flux Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Accelerating water dissociation while maintaining efficient proton transfer remains a substantial challenge in high‐flux alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, we introduce an interfacial engineering strategy to develop a high‐flux alkaline HER electrocatalyst with controllable spatially asymmetric interfacial charge gradients, by incorporating size‐tunable Ni nanoparticles at Mo 2 N/Ni 0.2 Mo 0.8 N interfacial regions to create a Ni‐nanoparticle‐bridged dual‐interface heterogeneous structure with coordinated proton‐transfer pathways. The resultant electrocatalyst achieves an industrial current density of 1.0 A cm −2 at 1.74 V in an anion‐exchange membrane electrolyzer, outperforming commercial Pt/C by 10%, while sustaining 100 h intermittent operation under 10–1000 mA cm −2 current cycling, demonstrating robust operational stability under high‐flux conditions. Such high‐flux HER capability can be attributed to the formation of asymmetric charge gradients along the Ni/Mo 2 N and Ni/Ni 0.2 Mo 0.8 N interfaces, which reorient interfacial water molecules into favorable configurations to promote dissociation at apical Ni nanoparticle sites and continuously supply protons. Simultaneously, the generated protons are directed through two coordinated pathways consisting of electrostatically guided surface migration at the negatively polarized Ni/Mo 2 N interface and hydrogen‐bond‐network‐mediated hopping at the positively polarized Ni/Ni 0.2 Mo 0.8 N interface, safeguarding against proton‐transfer bottlenecks and active‐site blockage under high‐flux conditions. This work establishes interfacial charge gradient regulation as a design principle for high‐flux alkaline HER.

title: Pathway Engineering Enables Durable Iridium‐Free Acidic Water Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT The pursuit of noble metal‐free alternatives to iridium for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically impeded by a pervasive activity‐stability trade‐off, wherein non‐precious metals undergo rapid oxidative dissolution under operating potentials. Here, we report a lutetium‐stabilized cobalt oxide catalyst (Lu 0.08 Co 2.92 O 4 ) designed through site‐specific electronic modulation, achieving a synergistic enhancement of both activity and stability in acidic OER for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Operando spectroscopies combined with theoretical simulations reveal that Lu incorporation introduces robust Lu‐O bonds and induces charge redistribution that strengthens Co‐O covalency and suppresses Co 2+ dissolution, which is critical for improved OER durability, and simultaneously optimizes the Co‐Co distance to favor direct O‐O radical coupling with a reduced energy barrier. Leveraging these structural advantages, a practical PEMWE employing Lu 0.08 Co 2.92 O 4 delivers an industrially relevant current density of 1000 mA cm −2 at 1.837 V. Separately, it maintains stable operation for over 900 h under a stepwise current density from 200 to 500 mA cm −2 , highlighting its potential for sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Nonreciprocal Bending in Ferroelectric Membranes Driven by Flexoelectricity
abstract: ABSTRACT Nonreciprocity reflects the asymmetric propagation or motion of an object in two opposite directions and can achieve directional transport in physics. However, nonreciprocity in natural quasi‐static mechanical systems, including nonreciprocal bending, has rarely been explored. Here we demonstrate nonreciprocal bending in a freestanding ferroelectric single‐crystalline PbTiO 3 membrane using suspended‐membrane nanoindentation. The mechanical bending of the ferroelectric membrane is strongly asymmetric in the two opposite bending directions with a difference in effective elastic modulus of up to 33%. The elastic recovery of bending deformation also becomes polarity‐dependent. Such unconventional nonreciprocal bending originates from the asymmetric ferroelectric domain switching driven by the crucial flexoelectricity, as revealed by phase‐field simulations. This work enriches the nonreciprocal functionalities of ferroelectrics and presents a route for exploring more nonreciprocal effects by flexoelectric engineering.

title: Linear and Branched Alkanes Separation Through Conjugated‐Polymer‐Framework Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT The separation of linear and branched alkanes is critically important for improving the research octane number (RON) and advancing the sustainable development of the petrochemical industry. However, owing to their nearly identical kinetic diameters and closely related physicochemical properties (e.g., solubility parameters and boiling points), membrane‐based liquid‐phase separation of such linear and branched alkanes remains highly challenging. An example is the n‐ heptane/ iso ‐octane pair, which exhibits minimal differences in molecular size and physicochemical properties but a dramatic difference in RON. Herein, we report a conjugated‐polymer‐framework (CPF) membrane that enables molecular‐level separation of linear and branched alkanes. The crystallized selective layer of CPF membrane features intrinsic sub‐nanometer pores of ∼5.5 and 8.4 Å. With ethanol as an assisting agent, the membrane achieves a separation factor of 5.24 for n ‐heptane/ iso ‐octane mixture, together with a total mixture permeance of 0.020 kg m −2 h −1 bar −1 . This pronounced selectivity stems from ethanol‐induced modulation of transmembrane transport, which selectively mitigates the transport barrier of linear alkanes while exerting negligible influence on their branched counterparts, thereby enhancing kinetic selectivity. Furthermore, the CPF membrane exhibits robust separation performance over extended operation and across a wide range of feed compositions and pressures, highlighting its robustness for linear/branched alkane separation.

title: Magnetic‐Field‐Annealing‐Induced Short‐Range Order in High‐Entropy Alloys for Enhanced Electromagnetic Response
abstract: ABSTRACT The growing demand for microwave absorbers in 5G/6G technologies motivates processing routes that balance matching thickness, attenuation, and temperature response. Here, magnetic field annealing (MFA) is investigated in rGO‐supported FeCoNi, FeCoNiCr, and FeCoNiCrCu compositionally complex alloys at 0, 0.5, and 0.95 T. Among the investigated FeCoNiCr samples, the 0.5 T sample exhibits a favorable combination of dielectric and magnetic responses. Reflection loss yields a minimum of −72.30 dB at 1.59 mm, and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 4.40 GHz. At 85°C, the maximum bandwidth is 4.08 GHz, corresponding to 92.7% retention of temperature‐specific maxima. Local microscopy, field‐associated atomistic modeling, and fixed‐composition electronic‐structure calculations support an interpretation of the electromagnetic response in terms of Co‐centered chemical correlations. Finally, flexible antennas and strain sensors based on this composite demonstrate stable wearable responses, validating this SRO strategy from atomic design to device integration.

title: Cation‐Mediated Interface Engineering Directs Electrogenerated Reactive Oxygen Species Pathways
abstract: ABSTRACT Persistent organic contaminants are increasingly accumulating in saline waters, where high ionic strength and complex electrolytes hinder oxidative remediation. Electrogenerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) offer a promising route for pollutant degradation, yet the role of electrolyte cations in controlling ROS pathways remains poorly understood. Although singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) is more persistent and matrix‐tolerant than hydroxyl radicals (•OH), whether cation‐induced changes in interfacial water structure govern ROS selectivity remains unclear. Here, using atomically dispersed Cu on Fe 2 O 3 ‐carbon nanotubes (Cu 1 /Fe 2 O 3 ‐CNTs) as a dual‐ROS electrocatalyst, we show that alkali‐metal cations exert distinct effects on ROS generation. •OH production follows the expected cation‐size‐dependent trend, whereas 1 O 2 generation exhibits an anomalous maximum in Na + ‐containing electrolytes, leading to superior contaminant degradation. Quantitative ROS measurements, in situ electrochemical analysis, spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations show that this behavior is primarily governed by selective stabilization of the *OOH intermediate rather than enhanced O 2 adsorption. Na + promotes a highly interconnected interfacial hydrogen‐bond network that stabilizes *OOH and favors 1 O 2 formation. In natural seawater, this regulation enables >98.2% contaminant removal within 8 h at an estimated energy demand of 0.779 kWh m −3 . These findings identify electrolyte cations as important regulators of ROS selectivity and provide a basis for efficient saline‐water decontamination.

title: Dibenzophenazine‐Fused Heterocyclic Luminophores: Decoding High‐Performance Organic Light‐Emitting Diodes Based on Long‐Wavelength Exciplex
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing highly efficient long‐wavelength exciplexes remains a challenge due to the constraints of the energy gap law and severe non‐radiative loss. In this study, we report a rigid nitrogen‐rich donor, 3N, featuring the first fused framework constructed from two anti‐aromatic phenazine units. This unique architecture ensures 3N has good planarity and an exceptionally shallow highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level of −4.88 eV. Meanwhile, the effective suppression of structural relaxation by its rigid scaffold contributes to a narrow emission at 456 nm. By pairing 3N with planar boron‐containing acceptors through strong intermolecular interactions, highly efficient exciplex emissions ranging from green to orange‐red were successfully achieved. Two representative exciplex systems reached outstanding photoluminescence quantum yields of 92% at 557 nm and 78% at 604 nm, respectively. Correspondingly, organic light‐emitting diodes based on these exciplexes delivered maximum external quantum efficiencies of 25.6% at 556 nm and 24.7% at 586 nm, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, these values rank among the highest performance metrics reported for long‐wavelength exciplexes. These results demonstrate that fusing multiple phenazine units could significantly raise the HOMO level and enhances structural rigidity, thereby enabling highly efficient long‐wavelength exciplex electroluminescence.

title: Ordered Crystallographic Orientation of Dion–Jacobson 2D Perovskites for Ultrastable Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites show great potential in stability but do not meet theoretical expectations for photovoltaics due to the random crystallographic orientation in films. We herein report ordered crystallographic orientation of the DJ 2D perovskite, achieved by modifying the intermediate‐phase film with a Ruddlesden‐Popper (RP) phase 2D perovskite based on the two‐step processing method. The introduction of the RP 2D perovskite lowers the energy barrier for the transition from the intermediate phase to the 2D perovskite phase with the ordered alignment, and this strategy is applicable to various organic diammoniums‐based DJ 2D perovskites. Solar cells with oriented DJ 2D perovskite films achieve an efficiency of 21.1% (19.05% for 1 cm 2 devices) and exhibit outstanding stability by retaining 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1‐sun illumination (ISOS‐L‐2 protocol) and 98.7% after 2500 h testing at a relative humidity of 85%.

title: All‐In‐One Integration of Inherently Flame‐Retardant, UV‐Resistant, and Antibacterial Polymer by a Biguanide Unit
abstract: ABSTRACT The increasing fire accidents, excessive UV exposure, and health threats posed by bacterial infections urgently require advanced polymer materials integrating multiple safety protections. In this study, we propose an ultra‐efficient strategy to achieve the all‐in‐one integration of inherently flame‐retardant, UV‐resistant, and antibacterial polymer materials through a single biguanide unit. The key lies in the unique triple protection mechanism exerted by the biguanide unit: high‐temperature char‐formation for flame retardance, n →π* transition absorption for UV‐resistance, and disruption of the negatively charged bacterial surface for antibacteria. As a result, the biguanide‐containing polymer material achieves the best UL‐94 V‐0 flame‐retardant rating with excellent self‐extinguishing properties, ≥99.3% ultra‐high shielding rate for UV light, and ≥99.0% remarkable antibacterial rate. Importantly, the biguanide unit is chemically bonded to the polymer main chain, which not only avoids the health risks and performance degradation caused by the additive migration, but also exhibits outstanding heat resistance, thermal stability, and easy processability. This work simultaneously achieves triple functional integration of polymer materials through a single biguanide unit, realizing previously unattainable multiple safety protections against dangerous fires, harmful UV, and widely‐existed bacteria.

title: Beyond Facet Engineering: Dislocation‐Mediated Nucleation Enables Stable Lithium Deposition on Practical Polycrystalline Cu Collectors
abstract: ABSTRACT Uniform Li deposition on practical Cu current collectors remains challenging in lithium metal batteries. Despite extensive efforts in facet engineering, achieving homogeneous Li deposition on practical polycrystalline Cu collectors remains elusive, highlighting an incomplete understanding of the structural factors governing Li deposition. Herein, a defect‐mediated interfacial engineering strategy is developed by simultaneously introducing a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and enriched / textures on commercial electrodeposited Cu foils. Theoretical calculations and experiments reveal that densely distributed dislocations provide thermodynamically favorable Li adsorption sites and abundant preferential heterogeneous nucleation sites, while the enriched / textures promote Li surface diffusion and lateral growth. This combined effect promotes uniform and compact initial Li deposition, guiding path‐dependent deposition evolution and suppressing interfacial heterogeneity. The control experiments further support a key contribution of dislocation defects, while variations in surface chemistry or morphology alone cannot account for the observed performance differences. The optimized Cu foil sustains over 1200 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.52% ± 0.20% over the final 200 cycles ( n = 4) in Li||Cu cells and improves N/P = 0 Cu||NCM811 full‐cell cycling. This work establishes dislocation‐mediated nucleation and orientation‐regulated growth as a design principle for practical Cu current collectors.

title: Anatomically Accessible Local mRNA Therapeutics: From Anatomical Access to Disease‐Focused Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have expanded from clinically validated prophylactic vaccines toward protein replacement and supplementation. Yet mRNA delivery remains centered on intramuscular vaccination and intravenous administration, largely optimized for systemic adaptive immunity or circulation‐mediated biodistribution. Many localized diseases, however, are confined to tissues or compartments accessible by topical, transdermal, inhaled, oral, catheter‐based, ocular, or intra‐articular administration without initial reliance on circulation. For these diseases, the therapeutic objective is likewise local: therapeutically relevant mRNA expression occurs within the affected tissue, and efficacy derives predominantly from the local biological activity of the encoded protein rather than from downstream systemic effects initiated by local expression. This therapeutic paradigm is defined here as Anatomically Accessible Local mRNA Therapeutics (ALmT). The review first distinguishes ALmT from intravenous mRNA delivery and intramuscular mRNA vaccination, then organizes site‐specific barriers and engineering strategies across major anatomical sites. It further examines disease‐focused ALmT applications, highlighting protein restoration, cytokine or growth‐factor supplementation, local antibody‐fragment production, regenerative modulation, and tissue repair. Finally, it discusses general design principles, quantitative PK/PD evaluation, repeat‐dose safety, and clinical translation. Overall, the ALmT framework may facilitate the design, quantitative evaluation, and clinical translation of mRNA therapies for localized diseases.

title: Synchronized Ablation of Multifocal Tumors Enabled by Multi‐Channel Lanthanide Nanocomposites
abstract: ABSTRACT The multifocal nature of orthotopic breast tumors makes it difficult to treat due to individual tumor differences, requiring multiple therapeutic interventions. Here, a customized therapeutic strategy is presented for multiple tumors by using the same prescription based on a multi‐channel lanthanide nanocomposite and orthogonally controlled drug release. The upconversion luminescence of the nanocomposite at different wavelengths can monitor pH‐responsive mitoxantrone (MXT) release, reduced glutathione‐responsive near‐infrared (NIR) absorbance change, and eigen temperature, respectively, allowing modulation of photothermal treatment and temperature‐responsive paclitaxel release through customized whole‐body irradiation to achieve synchronized ablation of different individual tumors. Small animal experiments confirm multifocal breast tumors can be treated through this customized therapeutic strategy with both high efficiency and low overtherapy risk.

title: Applications of a novel model-based real-time observer for electron density profile control experiments in TCV
abstract: Real-time estimation and control of the electron plasma density profile is fundamental for monitoring and regulating particle confinement, fusion power, heating efficiency, exhaust performance, impurity concentration, and proximity to the density limit (Greenwald et alNucl. Fusion28 2199–207) in present and future tokamaks. This work presents the experimental applications of a multi-rate electron density observer (Pastore Fusion Eng. Des.192 113615) based on RAPDENS (Blanken Fusion Eng. Des.126 87–103), integrated into the TCV plasma control system, to control the density profile in a range of plasma scenarios relevant to future fusion power plants. Three main experimental contributions are reported. First, the observer enables control of the line-averaged electron density within the last-closed flux surface ( ) in ohmic, nitrogen-seeded plasmas with alternative divertor geometries, decoupling upstream density from scrape-off layer pickup in the interferometer signal—a limitation of the traditional control scheme. Second, local control of the central electron density below the ECH cutoff is demonstrated in L-mode plasmas with mixed ECH and neutral beam injection heating, where auxiliary-heating-induced profile peaking is treated as a disturbance to the control task. Real-time estimation and adjustment of the electron pinch velocity-to-diffusivity ratio improves the spatial accuracy of the profile reconstruction, especially in the core region. The underlying turbulent transport in this scenario is characterised via linear and non-linear gyrokinetic simulations with GENE, confirming quantitatively a TEM-dominated pumpout regime during ECH, which affects the amount of gas flux needed to sustain the target density reference. Last, simultaneous control of the edge-normalised density fraction and toroidal beta is demonstrated in high-performance H-mode plasmas ( , ), yielding reproducible scenarios with a device-agnostic density metric and robust handling of interferometer fringe jumps.

title: Harnessing Photoexcited-State Pathways in Boron Dipyrromethene for Phototheranostics and Photopolymerization
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) dyes are widely recognized for their strong visible-light absorption, high fluorescence, and structural modularity. Beyond fluorescence, molecular engineering can redirect their photoexcited states toward distinct photochemical pathways, expanding their utility in photomedicine and materials chemistry. This Spotlight examines BODIPY photochemistry from this excited-state perspective and connects recent advances in phototheranostics and photopolymerization. In phototherapy, BODIPY excited states can be directed toward triplet-state energy transfer for singlet-oxygen generation, photoinduced electron transfer to form radicals and biomolecular redox modulation, or nonradiative relaxation for photothermal and photoacoustic applications. The same photochemical principles extend to polymer synthesis, where electron transfer with co-initiators or direct photoinduced bond cleavage supports visible-light photoredox catalysis, photobase generation, and Type I photoinitiation. These pathways have been used in applications ranging from panchromatic photocuring to hydrogel formation, holographic patterning, and 3D printing. Overall, BODIPYs provide programmable photoactive platforms whose functions depend on how molecular structure and the local environment distribute excitation energy among competing pathways. Across these applications, excited-state energies, redox properties, and bond dissociation energies provide complementary parameters for directing BODIPY photochemistry. Emerging quantitative structure–property relationship (QSPR) and machine-learning approaches may further complement these mechanistic design principles by enabling prediction of BODIPY photophysical and photosensitization behavior from molecular structure.

title: Fast, Hybrid Perovskite Deposition via Gas Flow Assisted Single Source Flash Evaporation
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract A large number of publications, using diverse production techniques, are demonstrating the potential of metal halide perovskite thin-film devices. Promising records in power conversion efficiencies, device lifetimes and photo-electrical applications have been reported worldwide. A simple and rapid deposition method, however, is still missing. This work introduces a possible answer: Gas Flow Assisted Flash Evaporation (Gas-FE). Gas-FE is a solvent-free deposition method operating under modest vacuum conditions that enables the deposition of complex perovskites with components having varying vapor pressures. We demonstrate its capabilities by subliming complex powder compositions relevant for perovskite photovoltaics and show a proof-of-concept methylammonium lead iodide-based (MAPbI3) solar cell containing methylammonium chloride and lithium TFSI as dopants. Growth rates exceeding 1 µm/min are obtained for crystalline, highly oriented perovskite films with good optical and electronic properties. The perovskite film is integrated into a fully vacuum-deposited p-i-n photovoltaic device, yielding a promising power conversion efficiency of 9.6%.

title: Ammonium Ion Intercalation Enabled Stable 1T-VS2/WS2-Nb2CTx Heterostructures during Electrochemical Charge Storage
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The performance of energy storage devices utilizing multilayered materials is governed by the complex interactions between electrolyte ions and the electrode. Consequently, inhibiting the irreversible oxidative failure of the electrodes is crucial. Herein, an in situ modification strategy that introduces NH4+ species in Nb2CTx MXene electrodes and integrates them with 1T phase VS2/WS2 heteronanosheets is evaluated. The resulting VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+ electrodes demonstrate a specific capacity of up to 217.48 mA h g–1 at 1 A g–1 with excellent electrochemical stability at high current densities. Density functional theory simulations confirmed the strong electronic interaction between the NH4+-intercalated Nb2CTx and 1T-WS2/VS2 nanosheets, resulting in higher OH– adsorption energies. Operando Raman analysis revealed that the process involves cation dehydration and K+ rehydration. These results highlight the importance of NH4+ dynamics, thermodynamic stability, and interfacial interactions. A VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+//N-doped nanocube-based asymmetric supercapacitor was fabricated, exhibiting a peak energy density of 54 Wh kg–1 and long-term cycling stability without significant performance degradation.

title: Graphene-Oxide-Reinforced Perfluorocyclobutyl Polymer Coatings for Tunable Tortuosity-Driven Corrosion Protection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polymeric coatings are widely used to mitigate corrosion by limiting the transport of water, oxygen, and aggressive ions, yet their long-term performance is often constrained by permeability, electrostatic heterogeneity, and mechanically induced defects. Perfluorocyclobutyl (PFCB) polymers offer intrinsically low permeability and high chemical stability, but opportunities remain to further engineer ion-transport pathways without sacrificing adhesion or durability. The role of two-dimensional nanofillers in fluoropolymer matrices and the limits at which they enhance rather than degrade corrosion resistance also remain poorly understood. Here, we examine how the dispersion state of graphene oxide (GO) in an elastomer-modified PFCB (EPFCB) network couples ion-transport resistance with the electrical response of the coating and buried interface. At 0.10 wt % GO, the coating sustains low-frequency electrochemical impedance values on the order of 109–1010 Ω·cm2 for over 30 days in 3.5 wt % NaCl solution, representing three orders of magnitude improvement over the neat EPFCB coating. This performance is supported by Raman-verified defect-rich GO, homogeneous platelet dispersion observed by electron microscopy, suppression of surface potential fluctuations by Kelvin probe force microscopy, and a controlled increase in glassy modulus from ∼218 MPa to ∼1.6–1.9 GPa without excessive brittleness. In contrast, higher GO loadings (>0.25 wt %) promote aggregation, greater morphological and electrostatic heterogeneity, earlier electrolyte breakthrough, and accelerated scribe creep during cyclic corrosion testing. These findings demonstrate that GO influences EPFCB performance through the combined effects of platelet-induced transport obstruction and dispersion-dependent electrostatic behavior, rather than through tortuosity alone.
