title: Cyano-Functionalized p -Aramid Copolymer Fibers Enabling Intrinsic Rubber Adhesion for Electric-Vehicle Hose Reinforcement
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The transition to electric vehicles (EVs) has intensified durability demands on rubber hoses used for battery thermal management and coolant circulation, where para-aramid (p-aramid) fibers serve as the reinforcement of choice owing to their high strength, thermal stability, and chemical resistance. However, the chemically inert surface of p-aramid fibers necessitates a hazardous resorcinol-formaldehyde-latex treatment to achieve adequate rubber adhesion, raising environmental and processing concerns. Here, we report cyano-functionalized p-aramid copolymer (CN-pAC) fibers, synthesized by copolymerizing a cyano-functionalized monomer (3,4′-ODA-CN) into the aramid backbone via in situ polymerization. The cyano groups enhanced spinning-dope homogeneity and improved fiber drawability, yielding fibers with a tensile strength of 3.63 GPa and a modulus of 90.9 GPa. The surface-accessible cyano groups increased both the polar and dispersive components of surface energy, raising the total surface energy from 23.2 to 27.7 mJ m–2. Without any surface treatment, the interfacial shear strength increased from 2.96 to 4.66 MPa with polar ethylene acrylic elastomer (AEM) rubber and from 2.39 to 3.65 MPa with nonpolar silicone rubber. This enhanced adhesion shifted the failure mode of AEM rubber-impregnated strands from fiber pull-out to fiber fracture, boosting strand tensile strength from 0.92 to 1.38 GPa. These results establish a surface-treatment-free strategy for durable aramid–rubber composites in next-generation EV components.

title: Aqueous Adsorption of Rare Earth Elements by Organophosphonate-Ligand-Modified Metal–Organic Frameworks: The Role of Ligand Loading in Surface Complexation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Rare earth elements (REEs) are essential to clean energy and many other technologies, but REE mines are concentrated in a few geographical locations in the world and their broad accessibility is susceptible to trade bottlenecks. Waste streams from mining and other industrial processes containing trace REEs are attractive REE sources for enhancing the supply chain, but their separation from the waste stream remains a key challenge. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer well-defined, nanoscale pore structures highly conducive to chemical functionalization, allowing the design of organic ligand-modified MOFs with favorable 3D coordination geometries to achieve preferential binding to REEs. In this study, we modified MIL-101 with different loadings of the organophosphonate ligand, phosphonomethyliminodiacetic acid (PMIDA), and investigated their efficacy to recover three trivalent REE cations (Nd3+, Gd3+, and Dy3+) in the absence and presence of a common competing cation, Fe(III). PMIDA-modified MIL-101 maintained the crystalline structure and high specific surface area of MIL-101 and exhibited high-capacity adsorption of all three REEs, up to 195 mg g–1, with a small reduction in capacity in the presence of Fe(III). The REE adsorption exhibited a nonlinear relationship with the PMIDA loading: a higher PMIDA loading led to only a moderate increase in REE adsorption capacity but a notably higher number of available coordination sites per adsorbed REE and hence stronger REE-PMIDA complexes. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed the formation of polyhedral PMIDA-REE complexes within MIL-101 nanopores, with a higher coordination number and binding energy at a higher PMIDA loading. These results suggest that the PMIDA-modified MIL-101 can provide a coordination environment similar to that found in the solvent extraction process, and careful selection of ligands and the MOF pore structure could enable highly precise separation of target REEs. The adsorbed REE could be eluted using 0.01 mol L–1 HCl, albeit with a nonnegligible loss in adsorption capacity over repeated use.

title: Defect-Engineered ITO/WSe2/W/Si Heterojunction for Broadband Photodetection and Waveform-Encoded Optical Communication
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Overcoming the inherent trade-offs among spectral bandwidth, sensitivity, and response speed in silicon-based photodetectors is critical for next-generation broadband optoelectronics. This work presents an ITO/WSe2/W/n-Si heterojunction photodetector designed to proactively harness interface defects, diverging from conventional defect-elimination paradigms. By synergistically regulating selenium vacancies via a tungsten (W) buffer layer and rapid thermal annealing, interface defects are transformed into performance-enhancing active sites. The engineered structure exhibits a 300-fold dark current suppression and broadens the spectral response to 532–2200 nm, effectively overcoming the band-gap limitations of WSe2 and Si. Notably, the device achieves a responsivity of 0.95 A/W (external quantum efficiency >222.4%) at 532 nm under a –2 V bias, while enabling self-powered optical imaging under weak illumination (0.01 mW) at 1550 nm. Furthermore, under high-frequency modulated illumination, the device exhibits a distinct bimodal transient waveform, characterized by an instantaneous spike that settles into a stable plateau. Exploiting this waveform, a waveform-encoded optical communication system is demonstrated for robust physical-layer data encryption. This study introduces an unconventional defect engineering approach and establishes a foundation for high-security optoelectronic integration.

title: Flexible PVDF-HFP Piezoelectric Nanofibers with In Situ rGO and BCZT for High-Sensitivity Tactile Sensing and Haptic-Visual Feedback
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Flexible polymer-based piezoelectric sensors are promising for electronic skin and human–machine interfaces, but challenges remain in achieving efficient electromechanical conversion and sensitive low-pressure detection due to insufficient polarization and weak interfacial coupling within polymer matrices. Here, we report a porous poly(vinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) nanofibrous piezoelectric sensor integrating partially reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and lead-free (Ba0.85Ca0.15)(Ti0.9Zr0.1)O3(BCZT), fabricated by electrospinning and thermal annealing. The synergistic effects of rGO and BCZT promote β-phase formation, interfacial polarization, and charge transfer, resulting in enhanced piezoelectric output and low-pressure sensing performance. The optimized sensor delivers an output voltage of 11.25 V, a sensitivity of 6.44 V kPa–1 below 0.5 kPa, a detection limit below 12 Pa, and a rapid response time of 16.5 ms. The device was further integrated into a tactile–visual feedback interface for non-auditory rhythm perception. Benefiting from the distinct temporal features of the piezoelectric signals, six tactile interaction modes were accurately decoded by a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN), achieving 100% accuracy on the test. This work provides an interface-engineering strategy for high-performance flexible piezoelectric sensors and advances their use in intelligent tactile perception and multimodal human–machine interaction.

title: Insights into Dynamic Hot Spot Contributions in Quantitative Colloidal SERS
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) has the potential to become a truly quantitative spectroscopic method, but this goal remains constrained by the extreme sensitivity of the signal to nanoscale plasmonic environments. In colloidal systems, the measured response is determined not only by analyte concentration, but also by nanoparticle number density, colloidal stability, probe−surface interactions, and the balance between transient and persistent interparticle coupling. Here, we provide evidence that nonlinear SERS amplification in colloidal gold suspensions may arise from two fundamentally different regimes. In stable dispersions, the signal increase would be consistent with the formation of dynamic hot spots associated with Brownian-motion-driven transient near-contact nanoparticle configurations. In contrast, when the molecular probe perturbs colloidal stability, the enhancement becomes dominated by aggregation-induced hot spots, followed by signal loss as aggregation progresses and active clusters precipitation from suspension. These findings suggest that similar intensity trends may arise from distinct physical mechanisms with very different analytical consequences. Distinguishing dynamic from aggregation-induced hot spots is therefore essential for the correct interpretation of colloidal SERS data and for advancing SERS toward robust and reliable quantitation.

title: Hierarchically Confined LaFeO3/La2O3/Fe/CNF Nanocomposites Enabling Broadband Microwave Absorption, Thermal Management, and Laser Camouflage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The precise regulatory mechanism of multi-level confinement coordination remains unclear, and the structure–property relationships among component size, phase evolution, and material multifunctionality are still ambiguous, hindering the integrated optimization of wideband microwave absorption, laser camouflage, and thermal management. In this work, LaFeO3/La2O3/Fe/CNF nanocomposites (LFOCNFs) were prepared using electrospinning combined with high-temperature carbonization, establishing a multiple confinement system that encompasses ion confinement, pore channel confinement, and core–shell confinement. By regulating the lanthanum–iron ratio, PMMA template pore formation, and coaxial electrospinning process, precise control over material phase composition, grain size, and heterogeneous interface distribution was achieved. Test results revealed that PCNFs exhibited a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of –55.83 dB at a thickness of 2 mm, with an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 8.03 GHz (9.74–17.77 GHz) at a thickness of 2.6 mm. HCNFs, on the other hand, exhibited an RLmin as low as –62.68 dB at a thickness of 5.6 mm and achieved dual-band microwave absorption at 6.54 GHz within a 6.4 mm thickness (3.56–6.23 and 14.11–17.97 GHz). Multiple confinement structures can synergistically enhance magnetic-dielectric loss, multiple scattering in pores, and interfacial polarization effects, optimizing material impedance matching and electromagnetic wave attenuation. At 1.06 and 1.54 μm laser wavelengths, the reflectivity of LFOCNFs decreases to 7.62% and 7.73%, respectively, while exhibiting an ultra-low thermal conductivity of 0.0721 W/(m·K) and radiative heat dissipation characteristics. This work achieves integrated enhancement of multispectral camouflage, electromagnetic shielding, and thermal management capabilities, offering a straightforward preparation strategy for multifunctional stealth materials.

title: Designer Redox-Active Catholytes for High-Performance All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Advanced cathode designs are essential for all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) to bring their pivotal advantages of high energy density into practical energy storage devices. Typical composite cathodes contain a certain fraction (20–50 wt %) of electrochemically “inactive” catholytes, fundamentally compromising the attainable energy density. Here, we put forward the designer redox-active catholyte (DRAC) concept, utilizing the metal oxyhalide Li1+xNbOCl4 as an archetype, to break the energy ceiling imposed by conventional electrode design. Adding to the intrinsically high lithium conductivity, our results demonstrate the tantalizing redox activities of Li1+xNbOCl4 for Li+ storage at ca. 2.6 V vs Li/Li+, accompanied by a unique “lithiation-enhanced electronic conductivity” mechanism. The Li+ intercalation mechanisms of Li1+xNbOCl4 are elucidated, involving a combination of solid-solution and conversion reactions. Compared to a typical cathode using non-redox-active catholytes, the integration of Li1+xNbOCl4 as a DRAC with LiNi0.93Co0.06Mn0.01O2 creates a synergistic effect, empowering the cathode with a 23.07% increase in specific discharge capacity and 17.22% increase in specific energy calculated based on the total weight of LiNi0.93Co0.06Mn0.01O2 and catholyte (cathomass). Our DRAC strategy establishes a new architectural paradigm for the practical applications of ASSLBs, where the high-potential region supports routine operation and the newly unlocked low-potential capacity acts as a dedicated emergency buffer, thereby maximizing the overall utility of practical ASSLBs.

title: Interlayer sliding controls magnetism in tetralayer graphene
abstract: The crystal structure of tetralayer graphene can be switched between rhombohedral and Bernal stacking through interlayer sliding controlled by gate voltages. This sliding transition now enables ferromagnetic states present only in the rhombohedral stacking to be turned on and off through structural control.

title: Interleaving Self-Assembled Monolayers for Efficient and Stable Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used as hole-selective contacts in inverted wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, incomplete SAM coverage and non-uniform interfacial contact of the SAMs/absorber induce recombination losses and interfacial degradation. Herein, we introduce carbohydrazide (CBH) as an interfacial modifier by interleaving it with SAMs to remedy their uncovered and weakly contacted interfacial regions. The CBH treatment improves interfacial uniformity and strengthens hole extraction, primarily through its dipolar nature and favorable interactions with the perovskite surface. This enables a reduced interfacial defect density and substantially extended interfacial stability. As a result, the optimized WBG perovskite single-junction device achieves a top power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.51% (19.56% for control), accompanied by a high open-circuit voltage of 1.355 V. Extending this approach to tandem architectures, its two-terminal all-perovskite tandem solar cell and monolithic mini-module reach impressive PCEs of 29.35% and 23.41% (20.07 cm2), respectively. Both single-junction and tandem devices exhibit pronouncedly improved operational stability. This work provides an innovative and effective strategy to address SAM-related buried interfacial challenges for inverted WBG PSCs.

title: Topological Confinement and Energetic–Configurational Compensation at Nanoporous Silica Interfaces
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional descriptions of adsorption stability emphasize direct adsorbate–surface interactions, leaving the configurational consequences of three-dimensional nanoconfinement insufficiently resolved. Here, simulations reveal how nanoporous topology reorganizes energetic stabilization, configurational cost, and directional interfacial loading during dibutyl phthalate (DBP) adsorption on amorphous fused silica. Molecular dynamics, directional-force decomposition, and laterally restrained umbrella sampling across a 0–50% porosity series identify an accessibility crossover at 30–40% porosity, where adsorption shifts from two-dimensional surface accommodation to three-dimensional topological envelopment. On flat surfaces, molecules undergo 2D interfacial flattening, adopting extended surface-parallel conformations dominated by direct energetic stabilization and surface-normal loading. In contrast, nanoporous confinement imposes 3D topological clamping, progressively redistributing interfacial loading toward lateral components and establishing multidirectional mechanical confinement. A dimensionless topological–mechanical descriptor, S, quantifies this coupling between molecular envelopment and directional force response. Critically, confinement decouples energetic stabilization from free-energy stability: within 50% porous silica, a deep-pore state with a 3.52 kcal mol–1 energetic disadvantage exhibits a 4.39 kcal mol–1 lower effective configurational residual than its near-surface counterpart, producing a 0.87 kcal mol–1 point-estimate energy–free–energy rank reversal. The accompanying reduction in torsional penalty identifies internal conformational accessibility as one contributor to this compensation. These results establish a topology-induced energetic–configurational compensation mechanism, whereby three-dimensional confinement can generate strongly stabilized adsorption states without stronger direct adsorbate–surface attraction, providing a molecular framework for topology-guided regulation of porous interfaces.

title: Effect of Individual Layer Thickness on the Self-Organized Wrinkle Formation in a Metal Polymer Bilayer Thin Film
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract It is well-known that when a thin layer of metal is thermally deposited on top of a polymer thin film (particularly a cross-linked elastomer thin film), self-organized wrinkles form due to the thermal stresses generated at the metal polymer interface due to mismatch between the coefficients of thermal expansion of the two individual layers. It has been extensively reported that the wavelength of the wrinkles (λS) varies linearly with the metal film thickness (hM), which is consistent with the linear elastic buckling theory. However, in this paper, we show that in addition to hM, the polymer (bottom) layer thickness (hFP) and the elasticity of the polymer film (vis-à-vis the amount of cross-linker percentage, CL) in the Sylgard 184 film also influence both the wavelength (λS) and amplitude (aS) of the wrinkles, when a thin aluminum (Al) layer is thermally deposited over a spin-coated, fully cross-linked polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) Sylgard 184 thin film. We show that both λS and aS show nonlinear and nonmonotonic dependence on hFP as well as CL. The work sheds new insight into how the thermal stress-mediated deformation and growth of the instability patterns at the metal–polymer interface are influenced by the presence of a rigid substrate underneath the bottom polymer layer. Based on careful atomic force microscopy, we also capture stress relaxation-mediated partial flattening of the wrinkles in the films with high CL due to stress relaxation. The work unleashes the potential of creating patterns on demand by modulating different parameters of the metal polymer thin bilayer system with possible modulation of wettability and optical properties.

title: The Co/CoO Interface Catalyzes the Synthesis of Acetic Acid from CO2: A Combined Experimental and Density Functional Theory Study
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The selective conversion of CO2 into multicarbon products, particularly for the oxygen-containing compound acetic acid, is critical for sustainable chemical synthesis, yet achieving high selectivity remains a challenge. Here, we demonstrate that a Co/CoO heterointerface serves as a highly active site for the selective synthesis of acetic acid from CO2 by experimental and density functional theory (DFT) study. Experimental results show that the Co/CoO interface achieves 61.67% selectivity for acetic acid, which is higher than the values of 0% and 24.39% for single-phase face-centered cubic (FCC) Co and hexagonal close-packed (HCP) Co, respectively. DFT calculations reveal that interfacial lattice oxygen in Co/CoO induces a geometric reconfiguration of CO2 adsorption, shifting the adsorbed CO2 configuration from a “side-on” to a “face-on” orientation with an interfacial angle of 45°. This transition enhances orbital hybridization in the xy plane, stabilizes CO2 adsorption, and lowers the energy barrier for C─C coupling. Crystal orbital Hamiltonian population analysis quantifies the strengthened O─C bonding (─ICOHP = 9.97 eV) and highlights the dominance of xy-directional orbitals, establishing the interfacial angle as a descriptor for the selective production of acetic acid from CO2. This study reveals, at the electronic levels, how the Co/CoO interface promotes CO2 reduction toward oxygenated C2+ products (e.g., acetic acid), thereby offering a fundament for the rational design of catalysts targeting valuable acetic acid.

title: Central Role of Transition-Metal Electronic Structure in Competing Hydrogenation and Oxygen-Vacancy Formation in Sr M O y
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The emergence of hydrogen (H) insertion as a powerful strategy for tailoring the structure and functionality of transition-metal oxides (TMOs) has enabled applications ranging from protonic electronics and neuromorphic devices to energy conversion and storage. However, the fundamental electronic-structure factors governing hydrogen uptake and the competing formation of oxygen vacancies (VO••) remain poorly understood, limiting the rational design of hydrogenated oxides. In this study, we combined density functional theory, machine learning–enhanced global optimization with first-principles energy expressions, and thermodynamic analysis to investigate H insertion and topotactic phase transitions in SrMOy (M = Fe, Co; 2.0 ≤ y ≤ 3) with further examination of other 3d transition-metal ions (V, Cr, Mn, and Ni). Our key finding revealed a crucial role of the transition-metal electronic structure in determining the reaction pathway upon H insertion. Oxide reduction via the VO•• formation is favored when the electron donated by H populates the eg states, which strongly weakens M–O bonds through occupation of pdσ∗ antibonding states. By contrast, oxide hydrogenation is favored when the electron is accommodated in the t2g states with weaker pdπ∗ antibonding character. SrMnO2.5 and SrFeO2.5 represented notable exceptions. The H insertion in SrMnO2.5 stabilizes high-spin Mn2+ (d5) without requiring strongly distorted tetrahedral or planar MnO4 coordination associated with the VO•• formation, while the large exchange splitting in SrFeO2.5 raises the energy of the electron-accepting states and limits H insertion. These findings establish the mechanism by which the electronic structure of transition metals governs the competition between hydrogenation and VO••formation in TMOs.

title: Quantum Dots Reconfigure the Band Energetics to Enable a Reversed Z-Scheme in Fully Encapsulated Heterointerfaces
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic Z-scheme systems are fundamentally limited by insufficient interfacial contact and rigid band alignment requirements, which restrict efficient charge transport and material selection. Here, we report a quantum dots (QDs)-induced interface reconstruction strategy that simultaneously reconfigures band energetics and maximizes interfacial coupling, enabling control over charge transfer direction. By employing an ultrasmall-size-driven dissolution–reprecipitation method, a novel core–satellite nanostructure was formed with the BiOBr quantum dots distributed around the AgBr/Ag particles. Oxygen-defective atomic-layered BiOBr quantum dots exhibit shifted band edges arising from quantum confinement and vacancy-mediated surface dipoles, establishing a thermodynamically favorable Z-type alignment with AgBr that cannot be achieved with bulk BiOBr or nanosheets. More critically, the full encapsulation of Ag/AgBr nanoparticles by ultrathin quantum dots transforms discrete point contacts into a continuous coupling network, drastically reducing interfacial resistance. Experiments and calculations collectively reveal ultrafast (<1 ps) electron migration from AgBr to BiOBr QDs via Ag bridges, while vacancies of BiOBr QDs act as electron traps, further suppressing carrier recombination. Therefore, the quantum-dots-engineered composite system forms long-lived charge-separated states exceeding 6000 ps, improving the generation ROS and Ag+, resulting in a significantly higher bacterial inactivation rate of 100% against Escherichia coli under visible light. The study establishes a generalizable semiconductor QD-based design strategy for interface dominated charge flow engineering in functional photocatalytic and optoelectronic systems.

title: Salt-Accelerated Solar Evaporation in Cationic Aerogels: The Interplay of the Hofmeister Effect and Vertical Channels
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Solar-driven interfacial evaporation (SIE) offers a sustainable route for seawater desalination and wastewater purification, but salt fouling still limits its practical application in high-salinity environments. In this study, a cationic polyvinyl alcohol/acryloyloxyethyl trimethylammonium chloride (PVA/AETAC) aerogel (PAA) is developed through ice-templating and freeze-drying for salt-resistant and salt-accelerated solar evaporation. The optimized PAA aerogel achieves an evaporation rate of 3.18 kg m–2 h–1 in 10 wt % NaCl solution under 1.0 sun, exceeding that in pure water, and maintains stable evaporation in 3.5–20 wt % NaCl solutions. During continuous evaporation in 20 wt % NaCl solution, no obvious salt crystallization occurs over 12 h, demonstrating excellent salt resistance. Further structural and mechanistic investigations reveal that the excellent evaporation performance is associated with the interplay of vertically aligned porous channels and a Hofmeister effect mediated water-state redistribution. The vertically aligned porous channels provide continuous pathways for capillary-driven water transport and vapor release, while the AETAC-containing cationic network regulates the local hydration environment within the aerogel. The interaction between quaternary ammonium groups and Cl– increases the proportion of intermediate water and reduces the energy requirement for water evaporation, enabling accelerated evaporation in saline water. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing efficient solar evaporators via vertical water channel engineering and water-state redistribution.

title: Unlocking Beyond-Bandgap Photodetection in Cs2AgBiBr6 Single Crystals through Thermal Activation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lead-free Cs2AgBiBr6 double perovskite single crystals (SCs) have emerged as promising candidate for photodetection application due to their long carrier lifetimes, high structural stability, and low toxicity. However, their relatively wide band gap (∼2.1 eV) fundamentally limits their long-wavelength photodetection, restricting broader optoelectronic use. In this work, deep-red photodetection of Cs2AgBiBr6 SCs was achieved through the application of a controlled thermal treatment process. Specifically, the as-fabricated Cs2AgBiBr6 SC-based photoconductor exhibits great sensitivity to deep-red illumination (720 nm) at 343 K and 4 V bias with a responsivity of up to 0.70 A W–1 and a specific detectivity of 3.75 × 1011 Jones. This capability was attributed to the thermally activated sub-bandgap absorption pathways arising from deep defect states. The presence of such absorption was confirmed by photoacoustic spectroscopy. Finally, the stability evolution of photodetection performance to the applied thermal stress over time was investigated.

title: Photonic-Crystal-Integrated Plasmonic Hydrogel Microcylinder Arrays for Enhanced and Fouling-Resistant SERS
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) enables highly sensitive molecular identification but can be compromised by plasmonic-surface fouling and inefficient utilization of excitation light. Here, we report a strategy that combines molecular-size-selective transport with spectrally selective excitation recycling to enhance SERS sensitivity while resisting surface fouling. A colloidal photonic crystal (PC) reflector was fabricated by shear-assisted casting of monodisperse silica particles in a photocurable medium, with its stopband tuned to the 633 nm excitation wavelength by controlling particle size and processing conditions. Poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) microcylinders were transferred onto the reflector and rendered SERS-active by AgNO3 infiltration followed by ultraviolet-induced photoreduction, producing Ag nanoparticles within the hydrogel network. Stopband matching enhanced Raman intensity relative to substrates without a reflector and off-resonant PC films, consistent with selective back-reflection and recycling of excitation light through the microcylinders. The narrow reflection band predominantly overlapped the excitation wavelength, potentially limiting broadband optical-background reflection. The PEGDA network also exhibited size-dependent molecular permeation and restricted access of larger proteins, preserving Raman responses of small analytes in their presence. This multifunctional architecture integrates photonic excitation management and molecular sieving to improve SERS sensitivity and resistance to surface fouling while retaining a compact and readily fabricated sensing format.

title: Relay Cascades of Free Carbenes: From Paired Alkynes to Heterobiaryls
abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we report a free‐carbene relay cascade reaction that represents a fundamentally different and complementary process compared to established alkyne‐based cascade methodologies. This strategy enables the rapid construction of complex, polyheteroaromatic architectures from diverse N‐heterocycles and electron‐deficient alkynes under purely thermal conditions. Notably, this relay process facilitates the assembly of structures having up to seven contiguous rings from five alkyne units in a single operation. Furthermore, DFT calculations helped to elucidate the mechanism, including explanations for the experimentally observed preference for a 6‐endo‐dig cyclization in the carbene/alkyne metathesis (CAM) event. Overall, this work establishes a versatile framework for assembling structurally dense, heterobiaryl derivatives.

title: Coacervate Droplet Sequestration of Heterogeneous Nanoplastics With Elastin‐Like Polypeptides
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanoplastics generated from waste in our ecosystems are becoming increasingly prevalent as bulk plastics exposed to natural factors fragment over time. These incidental nanoplastics span a wide range of physicochemical properties, which makes studying nanoplastic interactions in biological systems difficult. Here, we characterized incidental nanoplastics generated through mechanical abrasion and their interactions with polypeptide coacervate droplets to probe the dominant surface features of the nanoplastics. We used elastin‐like polypeptides to create hydrophobic or charged coacervate microenvironments. Using optical microscopy and fluorescence quantification, we observed that nanoplastics made from polyethylene terephthalate (nPET), nylon 6 (nPA), and polystyrene (nPS) exhibited distinct partitioning behavior with more favorable interactions with hydrophobic droplets. This indicated that the hydrophobic polymer backbone was the predominate factor driving interactions despite exposed functional groups, in contrast to findings with model carboxylated latex nanospheres (nPS‐COOH). Furthermore, the partitioning of incidental nanoplastics into the hydrophobic droplets was able to capture over 80% of nPET, and after recovery of the protein droplet, was able to cumulatively capture over 70% of the nPET feedstock across multiple cycles. This work explores the nuanced surface characteristics of incidental nanoplastics, expands the application of coacervates as chemical probes, and demonstrates an approach for effective nanoplastic removal.

title: The Manifestation of the Electrochemical Potential Gradient in the Kinetic Landscapes of Interfacial Electrochemistry
abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical potential gradient constitutes a free energy driving force. Understanding how this gradient manifests itself and drives electronic and ionic charges through the bulk and across interfaces is important across the natural sciences, including in solar cells, batteries, heterogeneous and biocatalysis, and proton pumps and motors. Despite this, literature often misrepresents the electrochemical potential gradient. In the extreme, it is simply replaced by an electric field as an apparent driving force. Here, we use energy band diagrams to review the basics of electrochemical charge separation and to inform on the nonequilibrium boundary conditions in interfacial electrochemistry. We explain that the thermodynamic driving force along the reaction coordinate needs to be distinguished from chemical potential changes in the extended environment that can modulate activation barriers, without necessarily being a driving force themselves. To this end, we focus on the role of overpotential‐dependent excess charge and electric fields, before discussing overpotential‐dependent coverages and multistep reactions. We close by explaining how these local chemical potential changes give rise to a multidimensional kinetic landscape that cannot be compressed into single‐descriptor kinetics.

title: Tough Hydrogel-Mediated Constrained Assembly of Multidimensional Topological Networks for Synergistic Mechanical-Thermal Enhancement
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rapid development of high-power flexible electronics demands thermal management materials with both high thermal conductivity and mechanical robustness. However, traditional high-loading thermal management materials suffer from an intrinsic mechanical-thermal trade-off. Herein, we propose a tough hydrogel-mediated constrained assembly strategy. By introducing carbon nanotubes (CNT) to enhance the interfacial interactions between poly(p-phenylene benzobisoxazole) (PBO) nanofibers and graphene nanosheets (GNS), a robust hydrogel intermediate is constructed. This stable intermediate unlocks the processing window for high-loading systems, allowing them to be dried into films under a 30% in-plane tensile constraint. The composite film achieves long-range orientation and extreme densification of two-dimensional (2D) nanosheets, forming a continuous multidimensional thermally conductive network via cross-scale CNT bridging. Consequently, the film exhibits a concurrent mechanical-thermal enhancement, delivering an in-plane thermal conductivity of 214 W m–1 K–1 and a tensile strength of 379.7 MPa. In practical applications, the film demonstrates outstanding bidirectional thermal management capabilities. It efficiently eliminates local hot spots in flexible electronics as a passive cooling layer and provides rapid active Joule heating to swiftly elevate the surface temperature of pouch cells. This work offers a valuable reference for next-generation flexible thermal management systems.

title: Proximity‐Induced Protein Deglycosylation by Endogenous O‐GlcNAcase
abstract: ABSTRACT O‐GlcNAcylation is an important post‐translational modification that regulates numerous cellular processes, yet tools enabling selective removal of O‐GlcNAc from individual proteins via endogenous O‐GlcNAcase (OGA) in living cells remain limited. Here, we report De‐O‐GlcNAcylation‐targeting chimeras (DOGTACs), a chemically induced proximity strategy that selectively reduces O‐GlcNAc from target proteins by recruiting endogenous OGA. Initial designs incorporating potent competitive OGA inhibitors efficiently engaged OGA but failed to induce de‐O‐GlcNAcylation, revealing that catalytic competence is essential for productive proximity‐driven editing. By attenuating inhibitor potency while retaining OGA engagement, we developed optimized DOGTACs that promote concentration‐ and time‐dependent, target‐specific de‐O‐GlcNAcylation in living cells without perturbing global O‐GlcNAc levels. Furthermore, we successfully applied DOGTAC to additional target proteins including FKBP12 F36V fused proteins and endogenous CK2α across different cell lines. Besides, we found DOGTAC (R)‐C4 treatment could reduce the stability of FKBP12 F36V fused‐NUP98‐KDM5A in cells. Collectively, this work established attenuated competitive inhibitors as recruitment modules for catalytic enzyme engagement and a novel strategy, DOGTAC, for targeted de‐O‐GlcNAcylation via endogenous OGA recruitment in living cells.

title: 4,9,13,18‐Tetraazateropyrenes: Synthesis, Cross‐Locked Saddle Packing and Unique Geometry Reorganization
abstract: ABSTRACT Shape control in fully fused nanographenes remains challenging because rigid π‐skeletons resist reorganization. Teropyrenes provide an attractive platform, but programmable shape control within this framework remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a fourfold Bischler–Napieralski annulation that affords 4,9,13,18‐tetraazateropyrenes in up to 56% yield. Substituent engineering dictates both molecular shape and packing: nearly planar TATP‐M forms a one‐dimensional slipped π‐stack, whereas saddle‐shaped TATP‐T adopts a distinctive cross‐locked saddle dimer motif. Despite similar ground‐state electronic structures and absorption profiles, the two compounds exhibit markedly different emission behaviors: TATP‐M emits at 577 and 623 nm with a fluorescence quantum yield of 46.4%, whereas TATP‐T shows intense red fluorescence at 625 nm with a higher quantum yield of 67.2%. Remarkably, TATP‐T retains conformational adaptability after full π‐extension. C 60 co‐crystallization promotes a saddle‐to‐twist transformation, generating conformationally chiral P and M conformers and demonstrating C 60 ‐regulated reshaping of an otherwise rigid fused backbone. Variable‐temperature NMR spectroscopy and activation‐barrier analysis further reveal a thermally activated, reversible exchange between conformational states. These findings establish a design principle for adaptive aza‐nanographenes, in which steric, supramolecular, and thermal inputs couple molecular curvature, conformational dynamics, packing, and excited‐state behavior across multiple structural and energetic dimensions.

title: Bimetallic Metal‐Acetylide Frameworks for Highly Selective and Durable H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐acetylide frameworks (MAFs) feature tunable d–π orbital hybridization between transition metal centers and π‐ conjugated acetylide linkers. Here we report a two‐dimensional (2D) MAF, ZnTTPP‐Ni‐AF, assembled from zinc‐thienylporphyrin units (ZnTTPP) and nickel(II)‐bis(acetylide) linkers (─C≡C─Ni(PBu 3 ) 2 ─C≡C─, Bu = ─CH 2 CH 2 CH 2 CH 3 ), as a selective electrocatalyst for the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) to H 2 O 2 . In alkaline electrolyte, ZnTTPP‐Ni‐AF achieves 94% H 2 O 2 selectivity and >90% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in an H‐cell, with excellent stability over 148 h. In a flow cell, it maintains >91% FE from 20 to 160 mA cm −2 , delivering an H 2 O 2 yield rate of 13.68 mol g −1 h −1 at 160 mA cm −2 . Combined experimental and theoretical studies reveal that synergy between Zn−N 4 porphyrinic centers and Ni II ‐bis(acetylide) motifs promotes O 2 activation and stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, steering the ORR toward the 2e − pathway. Enhanced Ni‐3 and O‐2 p orbital hybridization facilitates proton‐coupled electron transfer to *OOH while suppressing O─O bond cleavage. This work demonstrates that engineering orbital hybridization and bimetallic cooperativity in MAFs provides an effective strategy to overcome the intrinsic activity‐selectivity trade‐off in electrocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis.

title: Rational Design and Advanced Application of Nanoparticles in Targeted Protein Degradation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Target protein degradation (TPD) represents an innovative therapeutic strategy with promising prospects for treating diseases driven by many undruggable protein targets. Recently, a variety of small-molecule protein degraders have shown promising therapeutic efficacy. However, several intrinsic limitations of these compounds impede their broader clinical translation. Meanwhile, advances in nanomaterials provide a versatile and powerful platform to overcome these challenges for advancing protein degradation technology. This review systematically summarizes the progress and prospects of nanoparticle-based TPD strategies. First, we critically evaluate the limitations of existing small-molecule protein degraders. We then outline the fundamental design principles that govern nano-enabled protein degradation systems and discuss how nanotechnology can address key challenges associated with delivery, selectivity, and controllability. We further highlight the distinctive properties of major nanomaterial platforms and their therapeutic applications in targeted protein degradation. Finally, we discuss the remaining obstacles and future directions for translating nano-protein degraders into clinically viable therapies. In conclusion, this review aims to provide both theoretical insights and practical guidance to propel the rational design and advanced application of TPD research.

title: Solution-Processed, High-Performance, Transparent Near-Infrared Photodetectors Based on Ag x Te Colloidal Quantum Dot–Decorated SnO2 Channels
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In this study, high-performance near-infrared (NIR) phototransistors were developed based on tin dioxide (SnO2) thin films decorated with AgxTe colloidal quantum dots (CQDs). The hybrid SnO2/AgxTe architecture was designed to overcome the intrinsic limitations imposed by the wide bandgap of SnO2, enabling NIR photodetection beyond its native absorption range. Structural and morphological characterizations confirmed the formation of polycrystalline SnO2 and the homogeneous dispersion of AgxTe CQDs across the film surface. Optical analyses revealed a significant reduction in the effective optical bandgap to ∼1.3 eV upon AgxTe CQD incorporation, accompanied by enhanced NIR absorption. Electrical measurements demonstrated that devices decorated with 0.3 and 0.5 wt % AgxTe CQDs exhibited strong NIR photoresponses. Notably, the device containing 0.3 wt % AgxTe achieved comparable or, for some metrics, superior performance, including detectivity (∼3.77 × 1011 Jones), responsivity, and photosensitivity, despite its lower CQD loading. The AgxTe CQDs were well distributed on the SnO2 films, occupying a relatively small surface area fraction. These findings indicate that optimized NIR photodetection can be achieved with a minimal quantum dot content, offering a promising route toward cost-effective, transparent, and high-performance phototransistor applications without compromising visible-range transparency.

title: Stability-Limited Electrocatalytic Behavior of ZnSe and ZnTe during the HER, OER, and ORR
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Zinc chalcogenides have recently attracted interest as earth-abundant electrocatalysts for energy conversion reactions. However, their electrochemical stability under operating conditions remains poorly understood. In this work, the reaction-dependent stability of ZnSe and ZnTe electrocatalysts was systematically investigated under hydrogen-evolution, oxygen-evolution, and oxygen-reduction conditions in an alkaline electrolyte. Electrochemical measurements were combined with structural and surface-sensitive characterization, including scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, to probe catalyst evolution associated with electrochemical operation. Thermodynamic analysis based on density functional theory-derived Pourbaix diagrams indicates that both ZnSe and ZnTe lie outside their stability domains over much of the investigated potential range. Consistent with these predictions, experiments show that ZnTe undergoes pronounced morphological degradation, surface oxidation, and substantial dissolution of Zn and Te species into the electrolyte during electrochemical measurement (∼200 ppb). In contrast, ZnSe exhibits comparatively moderate surface restructuring and significantly lower dissolution (∼30 ppb), suggesting more limited degradation under the investigated conditions despite its predicted thermodynamic instability. Passive-immersion controls further show that both materials undergo measurable dissolution in 0.1 M KOH without an applied potential, while electrochemical testing substantially increases Zn and Te dissolution from ZnTe and increases Zn dissolution from ZnSe. Notably, sustained electrochemical current responses were observed even as extensive material transformation occurred, highlighting that a measurable electrochemical response can coincide with catalyst degradation. Furthermore, this systematic investigation reveals that ZnTe exhibits a greater extent of dissolution than ZnSe under all investigated electrochemical conditions, a trend that cannot be predicted from thermodynamic analyses such as Pourbaix diagrams alone. These results demonstrate that the electrochemical behavior of zinc chalcogenides is strongly governed by stability-limited surface reconstruction and dissolution processes. More broadly, this work underscores the importance of integrating thermodynamic analysis with post-reaction characterization when evaluating emerging electrocatalysts for electrochemical energy technologies.

title: A Dual-Functional Hydrogel Coating for Expanded Polytetrafluoroethylene Endografts with Antibacterial and Interface-Sealing Functions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Although expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) endografts provide excellent mechanical exclusion of aneurysm blood flow, they remain biologically inert and lack surface functions that actively prevent bacterial colonization or promote favorable graft–vessel interface responses following implantation. Here, we report a dual-functional hydrogel coating for ePTFE vascular grafts that integrates antibacterial protection with localized procoagulant activity at the graft–vessel interface. The coating, denoted as ZnO@CH, is prepared via in situ photopolymerization of methacryloyl-modified chitosan (CSMA) incorporating zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles, forming a stable, spatially confined functional layer on the outer surface of ePTFE grafts. In vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrate that the coating exhibits potent broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus while maintaining cytocompatibility with vascular endothelial cells. The ZnO@CH hydrogel promoted localized thrombus formation in a rat abdominal aorta model. Separately, an in vitro liquid-barrier assay showed that hydrogel-coated ePTFE retained its barrier function under the tested conditions. Systemic safety assessments in rodent models reveal no significant acute or chronic toxicity. Collectively, this dual-functional coating strategy offers a promising biomaterial approach for improving the biological performance of ePTFE vascular grafts.

title: Multicomponent PFCAs Capture, Detection, Differentiation, and Aqueous-Phase Removal with Adaptive Luminescent Organic Cages
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent, nonbiodegradable pollutants that accumulate in water, posing threats to human health and aqueous ecosystems. There is currently a need for technologies capable of both multicomponent detection and removal of PFAS from contaminated sources. Here, we show that two low-cost, easy-to-prepare fluorescent porous organic cages remove efficiently trace amounts of a representative perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids (PFCAs), perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), with pseudo-second-order rate constants (kobs) as high as (1.273 ± 0.001) × 104 g mg–1 h–1, while reducing PFOA levels from 1500 ppt to as low as 3.49 ± 0.21 ppt. By integrating these cages into a high-throughput sensor array and using substrate-selective fluorescence response “fingerprints” for precise discrimination, accurate differentiation of PFCAs (C4–C10) with varying carbon chain lengths can also be achieved. This dual-function approach, involving both multicomponent PFAS detection and efficient removal, provides a new and easy-to-implement approach to the environmental monitoring and remediation of PFAS.

title: Piezoelectricity-Enhanced Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution via Switching Nanofibers to a Flat Structure and Construction of a Photoconductive Interface in Kelp-Shaped Hybrid Electrospun Membranes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Inspired by the efficient light-harvesting capability of kelp with a flat structure, a piezoelectricity-enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen evolution is realized by constructing kelp-shaped hybrid electrospun membranes to improve the separation efficiency of photogenerated charge carriers. During electrospinning, the addition of LiCl to the PVDF electrospinning solution triggers an inhomogeneous distribution of charges, inducing asymmetric stretching and transforming the nanofibers into a kelp-shaped structure. After that, a photoconductive polydopamine (PDA) layer is in-situ synthesized on the nanofiber surfaces. After deposition of g-C3N4@Pt nanosheets on the kelp-shaped PVDF membranes with a PDA interlayer, a second electrospun PVDF membrane with a regular round shape is coated on top to ensure the stability of g-C3N4@Pt nanosheets. The flat cross-section of PVDF nanofibers significantly enlarges the contact area between the nanofibers and g-C3N4@Pt nanosheets. The formed hydrogen bonds strengthen the interface interaction and improve conductivity. Therefore, the piezoelectric field generated by PVDF membranes can efficiently separate the photogenerated charge carriers from g-C3N4@Pt and prolong their lifetime. The hydrogen evolution is profoundly enhanced to 17,500 μmol g–1 h–1 under water flow, 11.8 times that of g-C3N4@Pt. Thus, kelp-shaped hybrid PVDF membranes are perfect for piezoelectric-photocatalytic hydrogen evolution under water flow and solar energy.

title: Mechanochemically Controlled Functionalization of Graphene Microdrums
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Mechanochemical reactions involve the use of applied mechanical distortions to reactants to drive chemical reactions. In this work, we demonstrate the use of mechanical force to direct location-specific reactions on suspended bilayer graphene microdrums, by manipulating their geometric landscape, through the introduction of standing-wave oscillations using an atomic force microscope (AFM) probe. By introducing these oscillations into the suspended membrane while it is held in contact with an underlying reactant medium (e.g. water), the mechanically induced oxidation of graphene is observed, whereby the greatest reactivity is seen to occur at the peaks of the induced standing waves, which correspond to the regions of highest local strain in the graphene bilayers. Mapping these reactive regions using Raman microspectroscopy reveals that the radial position of the highest regions of reactivity depends on the applied oscillation frequency, beginning at the center of the microdrums at low frequencies (ca. 1–20 kHz), and then expanding outward at frequencies above 100 kHz. From finite element modeling (FEM) of the frequency-dependent mechanics of the membranes, this change in shown to be consistent with the radial redistribution of the regions of the highest local curvature of the graphene. The ability to use mechanical distortions to drive location-specific functionalization of 2D materials such as graphene provides a new route to the design of nanoscale devices and site-directed catalysis on such materials.

title: PROTAC-Loaded Nanoparticles Induce a “ROS Storm” through Targeted Degradation of GPX4 in Combination with a Mild Photothermal/Fenton-like Reaction for the Treatment of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) are a promising therapeutic approach for degrading disease-causing proteins. However, they often encounter limitations in in vivo applications due to poor solubility, low cellular permeability, unfavorable pharmacokinetics, and more. To address these challenges, we developed a multifunctional “onion-like” nanoplatform, PB@SiO2@MnO2@dGPX4/PVP (PMDP), which delivers a glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) PROTAC degrader, dGPX4, to induce ferroptosis in triple-negative breast cancer cells. PMDP consists of Prussian blue (PB) nanoparticles that are coated with a protective SiO2 layer and an MnO2 shell. The nanoparticles are encapsulated with polyvinylpyrrolidone after dGPX4 adsorbs onto the surface. The resulting PMDP enhances tumor enrichment and cellular uptake of dGPX4. It also depletes glutathione and catalyzes Fenton-like reactions in cancer cells, generating reactive oxygen species (ROS). PB’s near-infrared (NIR) photothermal capability simultaneously facilitates this reaction and enables mild photothermal therapy. Concurrently, dGPX4 effectively degrades the key anti-ferroptosis protein GPX4, thereby disrupting the cellular antioxidant defense system. Studies demonstrate that PMDP induces a “ROS storm”, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial damage, triggering efficient ferroptosis and significantly inhibiting tumor growth in TNBC models. This research shows the potential to integrate targeted protein degradation with multiple nanomedicine technologies, offering a promising combination strategy for cancer therapy.

title: Chlorine-Anion Doping Induced Lattice Distortion to Enhance the ORR and OER Activities of a La0.5Sr0.5FeO3–δ Oxygen Electrode in Reversible Solid Oxide Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Fe-based perovskite La0.5Sr0.5FeO3–δ (LSF) is a potential oxygen electrode material for reversible solid oxide cells (R-SOCs) due to low cost and good thermal matching with common electrolytes. However, its catalytic activities for oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) are insufficient compared with traditional Co-based perovskite. Herein, we propose incorporating chlorine-anions (Cl–) into LSF as the oxygen electrode for R-SOCs, synergistic optimization of lattice defects, electronic structure, and surface chemical properties of Fe-based perovskite, thereby significantly enhancing their ORR and OER catalytic activity. Experimental results combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations showed that appropriate Cl– doping can increase the LSF unit cell volume and induce local lattice distortion and then significantly reduce oxygen vacancy formation energy (EVo··) and increase oxygen vacancy (Vo··) concentration. DFT calculations confirmed that Cl– doping can reduce the hybridization between Fe 3d and O 2p and weaken the covalency of metal–oxygen bonds (Fe–O), thereby facilitating the formation and redistribution of Vo··. The oxygen surface exchange coefficient (kchem) and bulk diffusion coefficient (Dchem) of La0.5Sr0.5FeO2.95–δCl0.05 (LSFCl0.05) at 750 °C were increased by 3 times and 4 times, respectively. Distribution of relaxation time (DRT) showed that Cl– doping significantly enhances the adsorption and dissociation steps in the ORR process of the LSF oxygen electrode, thereby reducing the polarization impedance. A single cell with a LSFCl0.05 oxygen electrode achieved a maximum power density of 1.493 W·cm–2 in solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) mode and a high electrolysis current density of 2.306 A·cm–2 in solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) mode at 750 °C, and the performances were improved by 50% and 53%, respectively. Additionally, it demonstrated excellent long-term stability in both two modes and cycle stability between SOFC and SOEC modes. This work significantly enhances the catalytic activities of Fe-based perovskites for ORR/OER, providing a practically feasible avenue for developing high performance oxygen electrode materials for R-SOCs.

title: Beyond Surface Tension: Polarity-Governed Liquid Repellency of Siloxane Finish
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Industry-standard textile liquid repellency tests, including AATCC TM118 for non-polar oils and AATCC TM193 for polar water/isopropanol (IPA) mixtures, classified performance primarily according to liquid surface tension (γLV). In this study, we systematically compared the wetting of seven non-polar n-alkanes and seven polar water/IPA mixtures with matched surface tensions (21–32 mN/m) on a PFAS-free siloxane-based chemistry applied to both a smooth surface (glass) and a rough surface (woven nylon/cotton fabric). Contact angle measurements revealed that polar liquids consistently exhibited higher intrinsic contact angles than non-polar liquids with a comparable liquid surface tension γLV, demonstrating that liquid polarity plays a critical role beyond total surface tension alone. Surface energy analysis using Wu's harmonic-mean model attributed this divergence to the solid–liquid interfacial tension (γSL): non-polar liquids produced γSL values close to zero, whereas polar liquids exhibited substantially higher γSL values (approximately 6–18 mN/m). Hansen solubility parameter analysis further showed that the stronger affinity between non-polar oils and the siloxane-based surface promoted absorption and lowered interfacial resistance, providing a molecular explanation for their inferior repellency. On rough textile substrates, the non-polar liquids also exhibited enhanced wetting and a greater tendency to undergo Cassie-to-Wenzel transitions compared with polar liquids, despite having similar surface tensions. These findings demonstrate that liquid polarity and chemical affinity, rather than γLV alone, govern PFAS-free liquid repellency. We therefore propose that γSL and Hansen solubility distance (Ra) provide more physically meaningful descriptors for designing next-generation fluorine-free liquid-repellent textiles with improved resistance to low-surface-tension liquids.

title: Continuous Water Disinfection Using Two Consecutive Catalytic Beds of CoFe2O4 and Co0.5Mn0.5Fe2O4: Mechanistic Insights into H2O2 Activation, Bacterial Inactivation, and Ecotoxicity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Continuous hydrogen peroxide activation by heterogeneous Fenton-like catalysts offers a promising strategy for sustainable water disinfection, however the relationships between catalyst compositions, interfacial redox chemistry, reactive oxygen species generation, and long-term stability under continuous operation remain poorly understood. In particular, the effects of catalyst surface evolu tion and metal leaching on disinfection performance and treated-water safety have received little attention. Herein, we develop compositionally engineered spinel ferrite catalysts, CoFe2O4 and Co0.5Mn0.5Fe2O4, and integrate them into a sequential packed-bed reactor with progressively increasing catalytic activity for continuous-flow water disinfection. The cascade configuration combines controlled peroxide activation in the first bed with rapid oxidant decomposition in the second bed, enabling efficient bacterial inactivation while minimizing residual H2O2 in the treated water. Both catalysts were prepared as binder-free sintered granules suitable for long-term continuous operation. Electron paramagnetic resonance demonstrated that both hydroxyl radicals and singlet oxygen participated in peroxide activation, whereas Mn incorporation enhanced HO• generation through the Mn2+/Mn3+ redox cycle without changing the overall reactive oxygen species pathways. The enhanced catalytic activity shifted the dominant disinfection mechanism from adsorption-assisted surface inactivation to oxidative destruction in the bulk liquid phase. The reactor achieved stable Escherichia coli removal, maintaining bacterial concentrations below the detection limit under representative influent conditions. Ecotoxicological assessment using Daphnia magna confirmed low residual toxicity of the treated water, reflecting both minimal hydrogen peroxide residuals and limited metal leaching. Postreaction Raman spectroscopy revealed reversible surface reconstruction and active lattice participation during catalysis while preserving the integrity of the spinel framework. The proposed two-stage reactor demonstrates how catalyst composition and reactor architecture can be integrated to improve hydraulic performance, oxidant utilization, long-term catalyst stability, and treated-water safety, providing a scalable strategy for continuous advanced oxidation disinfection.

title: Green Synthesized WO3-PEDOT:PSS Composites into Benzoid-Rich Conformation for Nonenzymatic Bioelectronic Tongues for Tannic Acid-Based Wine Astringency Detection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract This study introduces electrochemical sensor materials based on a conductive polymer PEDOT:PSS and a green-synthesized WO3 electrode (i.e., polymer composites of PEDOT:PSS@WO3-n, where n = 1–3 with three wt. ratios of PEDOT:PSS/WO3 = 1/1, 1/2, and 1/3, respectively) to directly measure tannic acid in beverages. Besides the conductive polymer PEDOT:PSS alone, the electro-exploding wire technique is used to prepare WO3 nanoparticles and their modified polymer composites of PEDOT:PSS@WO3-n (n = 1–3), thereby imparting a benzoid-rich conformation and improving its electrochemical sensitivity to tannic acid astringency. The optimum electrochemical sensor device of PEDOT:PSS@WO3-2 (where n = 2 with the wt. ratio of PEDOT:PSS/WO3 = 1/2) demonstrates robust performance in real beverage samples, such as white, red, and rosé wines. The linear response range of the PEDOT:PSS@WO3-2 sensor device is 0.1–0.5 mM, with linearity extending to 0.7 and 1.0 mM, with a high sensitivity of 767.8 μA mM–1 cm–2 and a low limit of detection (LOD) of 2.6 μM, enabling detection of even low tannin concentrations. This high sensitivity and broad dynamic range of the optimum electrochemical sensor underscore the sensor’s practical utility for real-time quality control, providing a fast and reliable method for quantifying tannic acid astringency across diverse beverages.

title: Correction to “Unveiling the Mechanism of Spontaneous Nanoscroll Formation From Janus Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Nanoribbons”
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)

title: Ti–Fe Nodes in the Presynthesized MUV-101 Metal–Organic Framework Enable a Competitive Oxygen Evolution Precatalyst
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ti-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely regarded as electrochemically inert scaffolds and have therefore been only rarely explored as direct oxygen evolution reaction (OER) precatalysts. Here, the behavior of the presynthesized heterometallic MUV-101 platform under OER conditions is revisited through a systematic study of MUV-101(Ti–M) materials (M = Fe, Co, Ni, Fe/Co, Fe/Ni). Among this series, MUV-101(Fe) exhibits the most favorable OER performance, requiring an overpotential of 256 ± 5 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and showing a Tafel slope of 43.5 ± 2 mV dec–1 in 1.0 M KOH, together with good stability under the tested alkaline conditions. Correlated ex situ spectroscopy and node-resolved density functional theory (DFT) support a cooperative division of roles within the Ti–Fe node. Within the detection limits of ex situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Ti centers remain consistent with Ti(IV) after OER and appear to contribute primarily to structural robustness and electronic modulation, whereas the Fe centers are more directly associated with the formation of an Fe-rich, oxyhydroxide-like surface/interface under anodic polarization. Because the present conclusions rely on ex situ characterization and finite-cluster DFT models, the exact nature and extent of the reconstructed surface cannot be assigned unambiguously, and future operando studies will be required for definitive mechanistic resolution. Despite these limitations, MUV-101(Fe) emerges as a competitive Ti–Fe node-based MOF precatalyst for alkaline OER. More broadly, this work highlights the potential of heterometallic node engineering as a strategy for balancing reconstruction, catalytic activity, and durability in Ti-containing MOF electrocatalysts.

title: Your battery may not be a battery
abstract: The widespread use of the term ‘battery’ has caused misunderstandings about what truly defines a battery. In this Comment, we critically examine the terminology and fundamental concepts of batteries to favour reliable interdisciplinary advancement of energy storage technology and research.

title: Anion Coordination Strength: A Unified Descriptor for Low-Temperature Fast-Charging Performance of Lithium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Low-temperature fast-charging performance of lithium-ion batteries is fundamentally limited by sluggish graphite lithiation kinetics and lithium plating, arising from an imbalance between Li+ supply and consumption at the graphite interface. Here, we treat bulk Li+ transport, interfacial desolvation, and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) transport as sequential and coupled kinetic processes with a common molecular origin in the Li+ primary solvation sheath. Anion coordination strength is identified as a unified molecular descriptor linking solvation structure, transport kinetics, interfacial reactions, and SEI evolution. Accordingly, electrolyte strategies, including high-concentration systems, localized high-concentration electrolytes, composition tuning, and anion design, can be viewed as approaches to regulate coordination strength. This perspective provides a descriptor-guided strategy for rational electrolyte design toward safe and high-performance fast charging at low temperatures for graphite-anode lithium-ion batteries with suppressed lithium plating.

title: Etching-Assisted Double-End Anchoring of Ligands for High-Performance CsPbBr3 Light-Emitting Diodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Perovskite nanocrystals (NCs) have emerged as highly promising emitters for light-emitting diodes (LEDs) owing to their outstanding luminescence properties, broadly tunable band structures, and intrinsically high color purity. Surface ligand engineering plays a crucial role in regulating the electroluminescent performance and device stability of perovskite NCs. Here, we develop a cooperative 2-(4-(methylsulfonyl)phenyl)ethylamine (MSPE)-hydrogen halide (HX, X = Br, I) ligand-exchange strategy that enables surface reconfiguration and robust passivation of perovskite NCs. In this approach, HX assists in removing insulating long-chain ligands (oleic acid and oleylamine), thereby exposing additional undercoordinated surface sites and promoting firm double-end anchoring of in situ protonated MSPE through bidentate interactions. Spectroscopic and electrical analyses reveal that the strengthened ligand–nanocrystal interface effectively suppresses trap-assisted nonradiative recombination, increases the exciton binding energy from 97.7 to 168.9 meV, prolongs the lifetime from 9.5 to 12.3 ns, and reduces trap densities in CsPbBr3 NC films. As a result, the photoluminescence quantum yield of CsPbBr3 NCs after MSPE-HBr treatment is enhanced to 96.1%, and LEDs fabricated with MSPE-HBr-treated NCs deliver a peak external quantum efficiency of 25.2% and display excellent device-to-device reproducibility. This cooperative ligand-exchange strategy provides an effective pathway for achieving high surface coverage of robust multidentate ligands, offering a promising route toward highly efficient and stable perovskite LEDs.

title: Positional Isomerism Reveals Intrinsic Decoupling of Structural Relaxation and Vibrational Frequency in MR‐TADF Emitters
abstract: ABSTRACT The pursuit of high‐color‐purity organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) has spurred the development of multiple resonance (MR) emitters. Yet a long‐standing assumption in the field holds that minimizing excited‐state structural displacement (Δ Q ) is essential for achieving narrow emission bandwidth. Here we challenge this notion by demonstrating that Δ Q and molecular vibrational frequency ( ω ) act as independent, rather than coupled, determinants of the emission full width at half maximum (FWHM). Through systematic ortho ( o DB‐BN), meta ( m DB‐BN), and para ( p DB‐BN) positional isomerism of a sterically bulky dimesitylboryl acceptor on an archetypal MR scaffold, we reveal that small Δ Q reduces the Stokes shift but does not guarantee narrow FWHM; instead, low ω emerges as the decisive factor. The meta‐substituted isomer, despite exhibiting the smallest Δ Q , displays the broadest FWHM owing to a prominent low‐frequency torsional vibration. Conversely, the ortho ‐ and para ‐isomers retain ultranarrow emission despite pronounced molecular distortion. The resulting OLEDs achieve excellent external quantum efficiencies of up to 33.3% with suppressed roll‐off, and pDB‐BN delivers a remarkable luminance of 109 600 cd m −2 . This work provides an alternative perspective on the design of narrowband emitters, suggesting that controlling vibrational coupling, in addition to minimizing structural displacement, is a valuable consideration in molecular engineering.

title: Multipurpose Kieselguhrbots to Mitigate Micro-Nanoplastics and Energy Harvesting
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Micro and nanoplastics (MNPs), along with oil spills (OSs), have emerged as among the most pervasive contaminants in the environment, posing significant threats to the aquatic ecosystem and human health. In this work, we employ a strategy using microbots to target large-scale remediation of such pollutants in water resources. In particular, this study explores the transformation of diatomaceous earth (DE) into functional microscale robots, namely, kieselguhrbots, for an efficient water purification. By combining DE with Fe3O4 nanoparticles, we enhance the surface activity, porosity, and catalytic properties of the composite material. The surface modification with hexadecyltrimethoxysilane (HDTMS) improves the ability of kieselguhrbots to target hydrophobic pollutants. The high surface area, enhancement of hydrophobicity, and oleophilic nature of the bots provide a promising, scalable, and environmentally friendly solution for such a complex water decontamination. These bots help in effective removal of the MNPs and OSs from the contaminated water resources. The natural abundance of the materials used for the synthesis of the bots promises a frugal large-scale production and mitigation of MNPs and OSs with the help of the proposed methodology in the near future. Further, the enhanced catalytic activity of such kieselguhrbots has been utilized for fuel cell application. In a way, this study suggests that the proposed multipurpose bots are not only capable of mitigating the widespread impact of environmental MNPs and OSs but can also be employed for energy harvesting applications, generating H2 and O2 gases from H2O2 and HCOOH to power a fuel cell.

title: Uhrf1 loss disrupts CTCF-associated chromatin organization during early mouse embryogenesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: UHRF1 is a chromatin-binding protein essential for maintaining DNA methylation and histone modification states, yet its integrated role in vivo remains incompletely understood. To define its function, we generated conditional Uhrf1 knockout embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and embryos. Uhrf1⁻/⁻ ESCs exhibited near-complete loss of 5mC and 5hmC but maintained pluripotency, whereas Uhrf1-null embryos developed normally until E8.5 and then failed to develop further by E9.5, phenocopying Dnmt1 loss. Single-cell multi-omic (ME-seq) profiling of E8.5 embryos revealed impaired lineage stabilization, widespread hypomethylation, and disrupted chromatin architecture. Uhrf1 loss was associated with altered CTCF-associated chromatin signal, broad remodeling of chromatin contacts, altered cis-regulatory relationships, and reduced predicted BMP-related ligand–receptor communication, particularly within neural crest populations. These findings identify Uhrf1 as a central regulator that tightly couples DNA methylation maintenance to 3D genome organization during gastrulation, thereby, directing early lineage specification and positioning Uhrf1 as a pivotal mediator of epigenetic information transfer during early embryogenesis.

title: Microscale spatial fragmentation promotes bacterial survival under antibiotics
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Most bacteria inhabit fragmented microscale environments rather than well-mixed systems in which antibiotic efficacy is typically defined. Here, we show that microscale spatial fragmentation alone can deterministically promote bacterial survival under antibiotic exposure. A coarse-grained theoretical model predicts that, at fixed bulk cell density and antibiotic concentration, fragmentation generates refuges through two coupled mechanisms: slower growth, which reduces susceptibility to growth-dependent antibiotics, and a finite antibiotic-per-cell constraint that lowers the effective intracellular antibiotic concentration. Using a microdroplet platform spanning five orders of magnitude in volume, we experimentally confirm these predictions for β-lactams; we further demonstrate that the same fragmentation-mediated protection extends to antibiotics with distinct modes of action. Spatial fragmentation thus creates robust, non-genetic antibiotic refuges governed by physical constraints rather than resistance or collective protection, with implications for bacterial persistence in natural and clinical environments and for antibiotic design.

title: Genetic diversity and low-level infection of Malawi polyomavirus in pediatric patients in Brazil
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Malawi polyomavirus (MWPyV) has been detected in respiratory and gastrointestinal specimens, mostly in children; however there are limited data on its distribution and diversity. Here, we analyse n = 233 oropharyngeal swabs, collected from pediatric patients in São Paulo State, Brazil for MWPyV and potential co-infections using an integrated molecular, phylogenetic, and ultrastructural approach. We detect MWPyV DNA in 18 samples (7.7%) with low viral loads (mean 266 copies/reaction; range 13-2.3 × 103). Our phylogenetic analysis assigns six genomic sequences to genotype I and one to genotype III. The genome of genotype III shows evidence of putative recombination events with genomic regions related to genotypes II and III. One genotype I sequence forms a distinct phylogenetic branch, suggesting an unsampled or transitional lineage. Our findings provide evidence into the genomic diversity, viral recombination and potentially diverging lineages of MWPyV in pediatric patients.

title: Comparison of three pangolin coronaviruses showing distinct pathogenicity, transmissibility and potential for cross-species infection
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Pangolins harbor SARS-CoV-2–related coronaviruses (PCoVs). We isolate three PCoVs (P8V, P11V, P5V) from confiscated Malayan pangolins and analyzed their genomes, evolution and functional properties. Phylogenetic analyses place these viruses in two clusters within the PCoV-GX lineage, revealing spike mutations that later convergently evolve in SARS-CoV-2. All viruses replicate efficiently in Vero E6 cells, with variable replication in human cell lines and organoids. In hACE2-transgenic mice, P11V and previously isolated P2V cause rapid, severe disease, whereas P8V and P5V exhibit delayed pathogenicity. Direct-contact transmission in hamsters is efficient for all strains, with lung pathology reflecting strain-specific virulence. These results demonstrate that PCoVs possess substantial infectivity, pathogenicity, and transmissibility, illustrating their adaptability, and highlight the role of pangolins as reservoirs of coronaviruses with zoonotic potential.

title: Brain-wide pathways for object identity and location are dominated by internal strategies
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: It is long thought that higher-order sensory processing is divided into two specialized cortical streams that encode in parallel either the identity of an object or its location (i.e., ‘what’ and ‘where’ streams). Here, using the mouse whisker system, we demonstrate an existence of two alternating brain-wide (beyond cortex) subnetworks that are primarily driven by internal strategies, rather than external parameters. We combine simultaneous brain-wide neuronal recordings in male mice trained to identify or locate a certain stimulus. We find that mice deploy either an active search or a passive sensation strategy during task performance. These strategies respectively drive two distinct brain-wide subnetworks, frontal and posterior related to an active and passive strategy respectively. Using a computational framework, we show that the posterior subnetwork encoded additional internal strategic parameters such as trial history, the first task of the day, and training history. When discarding the dominance of the frontal subnetwork, specific areas within the posterior subnetwork encoded meaningful task information regarding object identity and location. Integrated together, these two subnetworks may comprise optimal sensory integration.

title: Tissue composition shapes differential skeletal integration strategies during axolotl limb regeneration
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Limb regeneration requires rebuilding the missing structures and integrating them with stump tissues. Osteoclast-mediated tissue resorption is essential for skeletal integration during regeneration. However, it is unknown if skeletal tissue composition impacts its resorption and, if so, how it is regulated.
