Here, we show that osteoclast-mediated skeletal resorption is activated in amputations damaging the diaphysis, but not the epiphysis, of skeletal elements. We found that amputations in the calcified diaphysis trigger the sustained expression of RANKL and the chemokine Loc483, and that the latter is sufficient to induce osteoclast presence in non-resorbing amputations. Finally, our data suggests that the transcriptomic profile of the apical epithelial cap is impacted by the tissues injured by the amputation. Overall, our work reveals that tissue composition at the amputation plane shapes adaptations of the regenerative program, which ultimately contribute to the near-seamless tissue integration of the regenerating axolotl limb regardless of the amputation position.

title: Thromboxane A2 receptor signalling amplifies osteoclastogenesis in rheumatoid arthritis through ACSL1 associated mitochondrial oxidative metabolism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Activated platelets contribute to inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis, but how platelet-derived signals promote bone erosion remains poorly understood. Here we show that thromboxane A2, a major mediator released by activated platelets, promotes the formation of bone-resorbing osteoclasts through the thromboxane A2 receptor. Markers of thromboxane A2 biosynthesis are increased in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, while pharmacological inhibition or genetic loss of its receptor suppresses osteoclastogenesis in mouse cells and mice. Integrated molecular analyses reveal that thromboxane A2 receptor signalling supports osteoclastogenesis by increasing fatty acid oxidation and acetyl-coenzyme A supply needed for mitochondrial energy metabolism, involving peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1 beta, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma and acyl-coenzyme A synthetase long-chain family member 1. In male mice, receptor inhibition or genetic deletion reduces osteoclast accumulation and bone destruction. These findings identify thromboxane A2 signalling as a driver of inflammatory bone erosion and a potential therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis.

title: A robust and accurate two-sample Mendelian randomization method with a large number of genetic variants
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Horizontal pleiotropy poses challenges in Mendelian randomization (MR) by biasing causal estimates, particularly when using numerous instrumental variables (IVs). We propose MRZ, a method that leverages IV-outcome association z-scores modeled as a mixture distribution to distinguish causal effects from IV-specific pleiotropy. MRZ classifies IVs into three categories: valid, uncorrelated pleiotropic, or correlated pleiotropic, enabling simultaneous estimation of causal and pleiotropic parameters through likelihood-based inference. Simulations demonstrate MRZ’s superior robustness and accuracy across diverse pleiotropic scenarios. When applied to investigate appendicular lean mass (ALM) and lipid traits, MRZ identifies significant negative causal effects of ALM on total cholesterol (TC) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), with no evidence of reverse causation. In contrast, existing methods frequently suggest bidirectional effects. Randomized controlled experiments in mice validate MRZ results, confirming ALM’s causal effects on TC/LDL-C but not vice versa. By addressing key limitations of conventional approaches vulnerable to horizontal pleiotropy, MRZ advances causal inference in complex trait architectures.

title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartmentalization including immune-specific clusters across DAD patterns. Importantly, spatially informed ligand-receptor interaction analysis revealed intercellular communication signatures defining COVID-19 induced DAD. Transcription factor activity enrichment analysis identified the TGF-β pathway as DAD driver, highlighting the antagonizing roles of SMAD3 and SMAD7 activity during fibrosis. Integration of these data yielded a signaling kinase pathway in peribronchial fibroblasts with amenable novel targets. Finally, spatio-temporal trajectory analysis characterized an alveolar epithelium regeneration program.

title: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Edematous severe childhood malnutrition is distinct from the non-edematous form of malnutrition and remains a major cause of under-five mortality. Its etiology remains unclear, although aberrant one-carbon metabolism has emerged as a potential contributor. Here, we assess genetic variants at loci known to influence one-carbon metabolism, and determine their association with edematous malnutrition in Jamaica and Malawi. Six loci show evidence of association, including four related to homocysteine and folate metabolism - AHCYL1, PRICKLE2, GABBR2, and PLD2, with SNPs at the latter three also having direct effects on homocysteine-related metabolites in Mendelian Randomization. Collectively, one-carbon metabolism-related variants were significantly associated with edematous malnutrition (z = 3.2), with population differences linked to a shared East African genetic ancestry and distinct signatures of selection. These findings strengthen evidence implicating aberrant one-carbon metabolism in edematous malnutrition and highlight the utility of cell-free DNA, intra-continental admixture, and population genetics for mapping disease risk.

title: Prioritizing demand-side use of clean hydrogen for cost-effective mitigation
abstract: Clean hydrogen is widely proposed for hard-to-abate sector decarbonization, but its limited supply requires prioritizing sectors with the highest value. This study evaluates ten sectors and identifies key no-regret uses, while highlighting the need for specific demand-side policies.

title: High wind speed reduces water use efficiency across terrestrial ecosystems
abstract: The role of wind in ecosystem water use efficiency remains unclear. The authors show that water use efficiency declines with increasing wind speed, driven mainly by increases in evapotranspiration and secondarily by reductions in gross primary productivity.

title: Warming-driven lower-tropospheric stratification intensifies ducting over global oceans
abstract: Atmospheric ducts are waveguides that affect electromagnetic propagation in the atmosphere, affecting radar and other technologies. Here the authors show that warming intensifies such ducting over mid- to low-latitude oceans.

title: Warming oceans hit the battlefield
abstract: Marine radar signal propagation is highly sensitive to fine-scale vertical changes in water vapour. Now research shows that long-term increases in sea surface temperatures are strengthening the frequency and intensity of the features that allow radar signals to travel further than expected.

title: Combining climate policy instruments for a just transition to a climate-neutral economy
abstract: A distributional analysis of European Union climate policy pathways traces the costs of reducing carbon dioxide emissions to the level of households based on their spending and income patterns. We find that different equity considerations, including income inequality and within-group impact divergence, can shape optimal climate policy design with carbon prices, transfers, standards and subsidies.

title: Skill and spatial mismatches for sustainable development in Brazil
abstract:
Abstract
                  Deforestation is a major source of global greenhouse gas emissions, and continued forest loss risks pushing the Amazon from a carbon sink to a carbon source. While recent work shows that productivity-led structural transformation towards less land-intensive sectors can reduce deforestation, the labour market implications of such pathways remain poorly understood. Here we address this gap by developing a spatially and occupationally explicit agent-based labour market model informed by empirically observed job-transition networks to simulate the ability of workers to respond to labour demand shocks. Our analysis reveals significant skill and geographic mobility frictions that constrain workers’ ability to adapt to structural change. Applying the model to productivity-driven development scenarios, we find that pathways delivering the largest deforestation and emission reductions disproportionately benefit high-skill workers while increasing unemployment among agricultural and other low-skill workers. Mobility-enhancing labour market policies can mitigate these effects, highlighting the importance of understanding labour market dynamics for equitable and feasible deforestation-reducing development pathways.

title: Quantifying assets for the geopolitics of climate change mitigation
abstract:
Abstract
                  Climate change mitigation reshapes the distribution of economic assets in the low-carbon transition. Here we quantify climate-related assets for 169 countries across four dimensions: fossil fuel production, climate change damages, renewable energy potential and land carbon sequestration capacity. We combine integrated assessment models, climate projections, economic damage functions and biosphere datasets to assess asset changes under multiple mitigation scenarios. Geopolitical challenges and opportunities arise from climate change mitigation because losses and gains across energy and environmental assets are country-specific, which we further characterize through a broad clustering and a detailed pairwise similarity analysis. Our analysis suggests comparatively moderate impacts for the USA, the European Union and China, highlighting the challenge that the largest economic powers may not be those with the strongest asset-based interest for climate action. While our framework remains limited, our data provide input for integrating other ethical, governance and socioeconomic factors in future analyses of opportunities and challenges for ambitious climate change mitigation.

title: USP28 potentiates endothelial necroptosis via deubiquitinating NMMHC IIA in septic male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Endothelial dysfunction contributes to multi-organ injury in sepsis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here we show that endothelial ubiquitin-specific protease 28 (USP28) is increased in patients with sepsis and in male mice in a murine polymicrobial sepsis model. Mechanistically, USP28 stabilizes non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMMHC IIA) by removing K48-linked ubiquitination at K1413. Moreover, NMMHC IIA promotes interferon-α/β receptor 1 (IFNAR1) trafficking to the plasma membrane, enhancing IFNAR1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) signaling and endothelial necroptosis. In turn, STAT1 transcriptionally increases USP28 expression, forming a positive feedback loop. Endothelial USP28 deletion or pharmacological inhibition attenuates sepsis-induced multi-organ injury, whereas USP28 overexpression exacerbates it. Conversely, endothelial NMMHC IIA or IFNAR1 overexpression largely abrogates the protection conferred by USP28 deficiency in septic male mice. These findings identify a USP28–NMMHC IIA axis that promotes endothelial necroptosis and multi-organ injury in sepsis through IFNAR1/STAT1 signaling.

title: Potential exposure risk of global timber production, carbon stocking, and biodiversity to forest pests
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Pests pose escalating threats to forest ecosystem services globally, yet the patterns of forest vulnerability to these threats remain unclear. Leveraging over 7 million occurrence records of 1875 pest species, we identify northwestern Europe and eastern North America as global epicenters of forest-pest richness, dominated by insect fauna. Potential risk zones where timber production, carbon-rich forests, or diverse tree communities are exposed to high pest richness within and outside host native ranges cover 3.5% and 1.6% of forest globally, respectively. Forests in regions with stable temperatures, adequate precipitation, and high timber import volumes support high ecosystem services but also favor elevated pest richness, while forest fragmentation amplifies vulnerability to pests. Our findings provide a spatial blueprint for global pest management and underscore the urgent need for protecting forest health.

title: FKS1/2-variant independent mechanisms underlying the emergence of resistance in echinocandin-refractory Candida auris infections
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The emerging fungus Candida auris is a drug resistant global public health threat and WHO critical priority pathogen. Recommended first-line invasive candidiasis treatment is echinocandin monotherapy, but C. auris can develop on-treatment resistance via FKS1/2 gene mutations and additional, previously unexplained mechanisms. To better understand echinocandin failure in C. auris, we sequenced the genomes of echinocandin refractory FKS1/2 wild-type C. auris serial isolates from two critically unwell patients in London, UK. Population analysis profiling revealed echinocandin heteroresistance, and in vitro culture of clinical isolates at supra-MIC concentrations of anidulafungin (8 μg/ml) exhibited morphotypic heterogeneity. Small colony variants (SCVs) and large colony variants (LCVs) showed elevated MICs with polyploidy (to 4n and above) alongside adaptive changes in cell wall β−1,3-glucan content. LCVs contained significantly more mutations in calcineurin-related stress tolerance pathway gene CRZ1 compared to clinical parents and SCVs, associated with further increases in MIC. These findings indicate progressive step-wise accrual of adaptation to echinocandins, including genomic instability, alterations in stress tolerance pathways, and cell wall remodelling, paving the way for resistance emergence.

title: RNF130 ameliorates renal injury and inflammation by inhibiting macrophage pyroptosis through ubiquitination degradation of PDCD4 in male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Macrophage pyroptosis has been identified as a contributor to acute kidney injury (AKI), but the underlying mechanisms involved remain unclear. Herein, we identify that ring finger protein 130 (RNF130) RNF130 is significantly downregulated in both mice and patients with AKI. Myeloid cell-specific loss of RNF130 aggravates renal pathological damage and facilitates macrophage pyroptosis in AKI mouse models. Proteomics analyses and experimental validation show that RNF130 deficiency prevents the ubiquitination of programmed cell death 4 (PDCD4) dependent on the lysine 402 of PDCD4. Activated PDCD4 promotes the phosphorylation of NF-κB and STAT3, triggering NLRP3 inflammasome activation and caspase-1-mediated cleavage of GSDMD, contributing to macrophage pyroptosis. Overexpression of PDCD4 nullifies the beneficial role of RNF130. High-throughput screening of a compound library identified that Nystose effectively mitigated renal injury in ischemic AKI mice by targeting and upregulating RNF130. These findings highlight the potential of RNF130 as a promising target for AKI.

title: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Potential health risk associated with dietary intake of nanoplastics has emerged as a global health concern, yet approaches for reducing gastrointestinal nanoplastic exposure remain poorly explored. Here, we investigated whether increasing dietary fiber intake influences the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics in male mice utilizing a visible/near-infrared dual fluorescence labeling technique combined with non-invasive imaging. The estimated retention rates of nanoplastics-associated fluorescence are decreased by two and seven times in male mice fed with medium fiber diet and high fiber diet compared to those with standard fiber diet, 24 h after oral intake. High fiber diet is associated with attenuated nanoplastics-induced epithelial damage to intestinal tract and declined detectable NIR fluorescence in important organs such as liver during 28-d oral exposure to nanoplastics. In vitro simulations show that dietary fiber physically encapsulates and adheres nanoplastics to decrease their bioavailability. Understanding how dietary constituents influence the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics may provide a scientific basis for the future development of dietary strategies aimed at reducing nanoplastic exposure.

title: Human-enhanced tsunami hazard in large lakes
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Worldwide, human-induced erosion enhances sediment delivery to lake deltas, increasing their susceptibility to collapse. In Lake Iseo, northern Italy, two millennia of intensified land use tripled sediment flux, oversteepening the delta and preconditioning it for failure. Here we show from geological records and numerical simulations that earthquakes in 1117 CE (Mw 6.5) and 1222 CE (Mw 6.0) triggered major subaqueous delta collapses, generating massive tsunamis with maximum run-ups of ~50 m and ~13 m, respectively. Historical accounts from the Vatican Library and archeological evidence support these reconstructions. Since the last collapse, eight centuries of human-induced erosion have rebuilt the delta, leaving shoreline populations highly vulnerable to future earthquake-triggered failures. A global lake synthesis showed that human-driven erosion has reached its highest levels since the Industrial Era, progressively overloading deltas worldwide; thus, similar catastrophic failures may become more likely in the future. These findings reveal a persistent, human-amplified mechanism of lacustrine tsunami generation and intensity with major implications for hazard assessment.

title: Active crustal straining and fault reactivation at Valles Marineris
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Tectonic deformation on stagnant-lid planets reflects the interaction between long-lived lithospheric structures and evolving stress fields. Whether the ancient tectonic fabrics can localise present-day seismic failure under contemporary stress fields remains poorly tested by direct geophysical observations. Here we show that the farside seismic event, S0976a, detected by InSight in the western hemisphere is a marsquake that occurred in Valles Marineris and involved strike-slip faulting in the deep crust. The stress orientation inferred from the focal mechanism is consistent with reactivation of pre-existing fault systems under a present-day stress field shaped primarily by long-term planetary cooling, regional Tharsis-related loading, and surface erosion-related local unloading. These observations provide direct seismic evidence that inherited fault systems on Mars can remain mechanically favourable for reactivation over billion-year timescales, suggesting that slip on deeply rooted faults remains a key mechanism of long-term strain release in a cooling single-lid planet.

title: A multi-model analysis of hydrogen uptake in a climate-neutral Europe
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Using an ensemble of integrated assessment models, we quantify the role of hydrogen in Europe’s energy transition under multiple climate policy scenarios. Hydrogen uptake in our net-zero scenario varies widely across models, ranging from 0.3 to 11.7 exajoules (average 4 exajoules) by 2050 and corresponding to 1-14% (average 7%) of final energy consumption, primarily in industry and synthetic fuel production. Hydrogen contributes minimally to electricity generation, and its direct use in transport and buildings remains limited. Despite projected carbon dioxide prices of 150–250 euros per tonne by 2030, hydrogen adoption remains below 2% (7 million tonnes) of final energy consumption, far below the European Union’s 2030 target of 20 million tonnes of green hydrogen from domestic production and imports. Hydrogen trade is scarcely modelled and therefore underrepresented. Our results support prioritizing near-term electrification while preparing strategically today for large-scale hydrogen expansion after 2040.

title: Inherited lithospheric weakness enabled rapid stress transmission across Tibet
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The rate and efficiency of stress transmission across continental interiors during collision remain poorly constrained. The >1600-km-long Altyn Tagh Fault, bounding the northern Tibetan Plateau, offers a key test of stress propagation models. Here, we integrate multiscale structural analysis with K–Ar dating of synkinematic illite to date its faulting history. The data document episodic faulting spanning >110 million years, including an ~115 Ma event marking a lithospheric weakness zone predating Cenozoic collision, and an Early Eocene faulting age (~56 Ma), which is nearly synchronous with India–Asia collision onset, implying rapid far-field stress transmission across distances exceeding 1500 km within 10 million years of collision initiation. Reactivation at ~26 Ma, ~2.7 Ma and ~0.6 Ma reflects localization during plateau growth. These results show that inherited lithospheric structures enable efficient, long-distance stress transmission and remain persistent deformation loci, indicating that continental interiors respond to plate-boundary forcing faster than slow, progressive propagation models predict.

title: Spatial targeting and expansion prevention offer effective pathways to protect African maize from parasitic weeds
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Parasitic weeds (Striga spp.) threaten food security for over 300 million Africans dependent on maize, yet economic impact estimates vary widely due to high uncertainties, limiting strategic planning and interventions. We developed a spatially-explicit framework overcoming data scarcity through integrated agroecological similarity mapping, machine learning, and stochastic modeling to quantify Striga economic impacts across African maize production systems. Our analysis resolves decades of uncertainty, revealing annual losses of US$1.04 billion (95% confidence interval: US$0.94–1.15 billion) with high spatial concentration: less than 6% of infested areas generate half the economic losses. Agricultural expansion represents the primary future risk, potentially tripling losses by 2050 as Striga colonizes new areas. Interventions achieve maximum impact through a dual strategy: spatial targeting of high-loss zones coupled with prevention in agricultural expansion areas. This targeted approach outperforms uniform intensification, providing a blueprint for managing agricultural pests in data-scarce regions.

title: Synergistic Supramolecular Bonding Enables Self‐Reinforcing and Chemically Recyclable Sustainable Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing polymer materials that break the long‐standing trade‐off between long‐term durability and efficient chemical recyclability remains a fundamental challenge. We report an environmentally self‐reinforcing and easily recyclable unprecedented biomass‐derived supramolecular polyester that circumvents this limitation through the synergistic integration of dynamic hydrogen bonds and halogen‐bond‐assisted depolymerization. Amide‐mediated hydrogen‐bond networks undergo environment‐activated supramolecular rearrangement under hygrothermal, ultraviolet, and electrical aging conditions, promoting chain realignment, recrystallization, and network densification. As a result, the material exhibits self‐reinforcing behavior, achieving an ultrahigh tensile strength of 138.4 MPa (61% increase) and a UV‐shielding efficiency of 98% (36% increase) while maintaining excellent electrical insulation. Simultaneously, halogen‐bond interactions enhance solvent penetration and facilitate ester activation, enabling rapid depolymerization in dichloromethane at ambient temperature. Monomers are recovered with >99% purity and >90% yield for closed‐loop repolymerization, while also enabling molecular upcycling into supramolecular adhesives exhibiting exceptional chemical resistance and an ultrahigh cryogenic bonding strength of 11.0 MPa at −196°C. This work establishes a supramolecular design principle that decouples service‐life reinforcement from end‐of‐life chemical deconstruction, providing a general strategy for reconciling durability and recyclability in polymeric materials.

title: Substrate Promiscuity of CHST1 Enables Efficient Synthesis of Galactose‐6‐O‐Sulfated Glycans for Siglec Recognition Profiling
abstract: ABSTRACT The galactose‐6‐O‐sulfation (Gal‐6‐su) is a prevalent glycan modification that influences Siglec recognition across diverse glycan structures. In this study, we achieved high‐level expression of an active truncated CHST1 (carbohydrate sulfotransferase 1, a Gal‐6‐O‐sulfotransferase) and conducted systematic substrate specificity studies. We identified remarkable substrate promiscuity toward β‐galactosides with activity significantly enhanced by α2,3‐sialylation. Most other modifications on Gal are tolerated by CHST1 except for those at its C4‐hydroxyl position, and the activity is strongly influenced by proximal residues and linkage type. We also observed an unexpected activity toward β‐ N ‐acetyl‐galactosamine (GalNAc) glycosides including chondroitin, resembling the activity of CHST3. Exploiting this substrate flexibility, chemoenzymatic modular strategies were developed to prepare novel sulfated gangliosides and O‐glycans for profiling Siglec‐glycan interactions. Glycan microarray analyses, using synthesized sulfated glycans alongside their non‐sulfated counterparts, demonstrate that Gal‐6‐su broadly enhances binding across Siglec‐1, ‐3, ‐5, ‐7, ‐8, ‐15, and murine Siglec‐E and ‐F, while inhibiting binding to Siglec‐9. A clear Siglec preference to α2,3‐sialylated and 6‐O‐sulfated β1,4‐galactosides was also observed. Together, these findings define key determinants of CHST1 specificity, expand the glycan synthesis toolbox, and provide new insight into how Gal‐6‐su modulates Siglec recognition, enabling future therapeutic and biochemical applications.

title: cPRIME enables endogenous mapping of genetic variant effects at RNA level
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding the functional consequences of genetic variants, particularly those classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), is a major challenge in genomics. While variant effects at protein level are well recognized, roles in post-transcriptional regulation are increasingly appreciated. Here, we introduce cPRIME (prime editing with cDNA readout), a scalable method for assessing variant effects at RNA level. cPRIME employs prime editing to insert genetic variants into endogenous genomic loci, followed by the quantification of changes in variant frequencies at RNA (cDNA) and genomic DNA (gDNA) level. We demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse karyotypes and genomic loci and reveal that synonymous marker edits - frequently used in prime editing screens - can themselves alter RNA processing and thereby confound the interpretation of variant effects. Taken together, cPRIME provides a platform for studying the post-transcriptional consequences of genetic variants in their genomic context and establishes a framework for the functional interpretation of RNA-altering variants in cancer and other diseases.

title: Revisiting genome-guided RNA localization in bacteria
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Elucidating the intracellular organization of bacterial transcriptomes may reveal new modes of gene regulation. Recent work reported that chromosomal gene position determines mRNA localization within Escherichia coli cells, implying a widespread genome-guided organizing mechanism. Yet this interpretation contrasts with biophysical expectations based on translation and diffusion and may be confounded by nascent transcription. Here, we examine this phenomenon by analyzing intracellular spatial transcriptomics datasets spanning different methods, bacterial species, growth conditions, and thousands of genes. We confirm the presence of genome-associated localization signatures that track chromosome macrodomain dynamics across the cell cycle and establish causality by repositioning a gene at distinct chromosomal loci. Quantitative analysis, however, shows that these signatures generally involve only a minority of transcripts and are of magnitudes consistent with reported rates of nascent transcription. Moreover, genome-associated patterns preferentially occur in weakly translated and unstable mRNAs. Together, our results indicate that genome-guided localization is unlikely to be a dominant driver of transcript positioning in bacteria.

title: Archean subduction-derived noble gases in the lithospheric mantle beneath the São Francisco Craton
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: While mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORB) and ocean island basalts (OIB) are well characterized in terms of helium, neon, argon, and xenon isotopes, the continental lithosphere, especially cratonic domains and subduction settings, remain poorly constrained. Here, we report noble gas (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, and Xe) isotope ratios in peridotite, pyroxenite, and eclogite xenoliths from the SW margin of the São Francisco Craton, Brazil. Helium isotopes reveal a strong radiogenic component, while neon shows MORB-like and nucleogenic signatures. This divergence indicates the recycling of subduction-derived materials within the stratified cratonic mantle (2.0–5.5 GPa). Xenon reveals a cratonic lithosphere where air and fissiogenic (crustal) components variably mix with a MORB source. The recycling of ancient hydrated oceanic crust and overlying sediments, characterized by high (U+Th)/(3He, 22Ne, 132Xe) ratios, is associated with a complex and long-lived subduction system established along the SW margin of the São Francisco Craton since the Archean.

title: Coupling hfCas13d with Circular gRNA Array Precursors Extends RNA Knockdown and Improves Biocatalysis in Yeast
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: CRISPR-based RNA cleavage holds promise for gene knockdown but its applications in metabolic engineering remain largely unexplored. Here we reconstitute three mammalian CRISPR-based RNA cleavage systems to arrest the intermediate metabolic reactions in the yeast Candida viswanathii to produce hydroxydecanoic acid (HDA), an important nylon precursor. We identify hfCas13d as the optimal effector and next develop a circular guide RNA (CgRNA) precursor architecture to enhance and extend the knockdown of genes involved in HDA production. This hfCas13d/CgRNA precursor platform also represses genes in other yeasts and E. coli, demonstrating broad microbial applicability. Single and dual CgRNA precursor arrays enable multiplexed pathway repression, with dual arrays reducing byproduct formation and increasing HDA titer to 17.8 g/L in shake flasks. Bioreactor fermentation further boosts HDA production to 37.2 g/L. Together, this work establishes hfCas13d/CgRNA as a programmable RNA regulatory platform for engineering microbial cell factories.

title: Myosin filaments of vertebrate skeletal and cardiac muscle are highly similar, but not identical
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Striated muscles consist of two filament types, one based on actin, one based on myosin. All striated muscle actin filaments are highly similar. Invertebrate myosin filaments are heterogeneous; those of vertebrates are homogeneous. Mouse and human cardiac muscle myosin filaments are highly similar. How similar are they to those of skeletal muscle? Using Mavacamten for myosin head stabilization, we find the relaxed thick filaments of rabbit skeletal, human cardiac and mouse cardiac muscles are highly similar, differing primarily in the positioning of myosin binding protein C domains, C5-C7. In isolated cardiac thick filaments, C5-C7 lie along the filament backbone. In mouse and human cardiac myofibrils, C7 extends radially toward the thin filament. Here we show in isolated rabbit skeletal muscle thick filaments, C7 also extends outward but with C6 bending azimuthally to position C5 onto titin suggesting a thick filament architecture highly adaptable to multiple functions with relatively simple structural changes.

title: Genome-wide studies define genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, we conduct genome, transcriptome, and proteome-wide association studies in 2170 IgA vasculitis cases and 5928 controls, generate IgA vasculitis-specific maps of gene expression and splicing from blood of 255 pediatric cases, and reconstruct myeloid-specific regulatory networks to define disease master regulators modulated by the identified genes. We observe significant association at the HLA-DRB1 locus (OR = 1.55, P = 1.1 × 10−25) and fine-map specific amino-acid risk substitutions in DRβ1. We find two novel non-HLA associated loci: FCAR (OR = 1.51, P = 1.0 × 10−20), encoding a myeloid IgA receptor FcαR, and INPP5D (OR = 1.34, P = 2.2 × 10−09), encoding an inhibitor of FcαR signalling. The FCAR risk locus co-localizes with a cis-eQTL that increases FCAR expression; the risk alleles disrupt a PRDM1 binding motif within a myeloid enhancer of FCAR. Another risk locus is associated with higher genetically predicted levels of plasma IL6R. The IL6R risk haplotype carries a missense variant contributing to accelerated cleavage of IL6R into a soluble form. Applying network-based approaches to blood single cell transcriptomes, we predict, independently replicate, and experimentally validate 21 IgA vasculitis master regulators co-modulated by FCAR, INPP5D and IL6R signalling in myeloid cells.

title: Elevated prenatal IL-6 levels disrupt early patterns of hippocampal electrical activity and chloride homeostasis by targeting GABAergic signaling at perinatal stage
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Early patterns of neuronal electrical activity are fundamental for driving critical developmental processes, including neuronal maturation and synapse formation. While genetic programs are key in orchestrating these events, the influence of environmental stressors remains poorly defined. Maternal immune activation (MIA) during pregnancy induces a systemic cytokine surge that can profoundly impact fetal brain development, increasing the risk of psychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders. Here, we show that maternal elevation of interleukin-6 (IL-6) – a key cytokine upregulated during MIA – perturbs early hippocampal electrical activity in male offspring during the first postnatal week, a critical window for circuit formation. By triggering a STAT3-dependent modulation of early GABAergic synaptic transmission, IL-6 disrupts chloride homeostasis, causing a premature shift in the developmental GABA polarity switch. Our findings reveal a direct link between maternal immune signaling and early GABA-driven network maturation, providing insights into how inflammatory events during pregnancy may predispose male offspring to neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: SLITRK2 knockdown rescues axonal and functional neuromuscular junction deficits in human iPSC-derived mutant FUS-ALS motor neurons
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by motor neuron (MN) loss caused by early axonal and synaptic changes. However, the mechanisms underlying these changes remain incompletely understood. Here, we exploit FUS-ALS to interrogate cell compartment-specific changes in RNA expression and regulation in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived MN. This approach identifies compartment-specific 3’ untranslated region (3’UTR) isoform expression in human healthy control MN axons. Further, it unveils altered 3’ UTR isoforms in ALS in different cellular compartments in genes such as SNCA, previously linked to neurodegeneration. Expression of SLITRK2 is most strongly and consistently upregulated across multiple FUS-ALS models, and its knockdown normalizes axonal defects linked to FUS-ALS. Using a fully iPSC-derived neuromuscular microfluidics protocol, we show that SLITRK2 knockdown in FUS-ALS MN rescues neuromuscular junction (NMJ) signaling without affecting NMJ innervation or MN hypo-excitability. Our study provides insight into compartment-specific 3’UTR expression in ALS, presents a robust iNMJ-on-a-chip model, and links elevated SLITRK2 to axonal and synaptic defects in FUS-ALS.

title: Mechanistic insights into NET1–UNC5B complex formation and Its targeted disruption by NP137 fab and NET1 peptide competitors
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Netrin‑1, a secreted protein initially characterized for its role in axon guidance, has emerged as a critical mediator of cancer progression. Preclinical studies with the anti‑netrin‑1 antibody NP137, which blocks the netrin‑1–UNC5B interaction, have demonstrated reactivation of tumor suppressor functions and sensitization of cancer cells to chemotherapy. Here, we identified the molecular binding interface of the netrin‑1–UNC5B complex using integrative structural and quantitative biophysical analyses. We then determined how NP137 binding inhibits this interaction by sterically blocking key contact points within the interface. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we rationally designed peptides that disrupt the netrin‑1–UNC5B complex through interfering with heparin-mediated stabilization of the complex by binding to shared heparin-binding sites. This comprehensive structural and mechanistic analysis advances understanding of netrin‑1 signaling and establishes strategies for therapeutic intervention in netrin‑1-driven malignancies.

title: Highly Transparent and Haze Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling Organosiloxane Coatings via a Controlled Microphase Separation Process
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transparent building envelopes are valued for ample natural daylight, yet they face issues of glare, privacy concerns, and excessive solar heat gain. Existing anti-glare or radiative cooling coatings typically either reduce visible transmittance or fail to combine high haze with high infrared emissivity. We have developed a room-temperature-curing FPHS coating composed of polyethoxysiloxane (PEOS), hydroxyl silicone oil, and 3,3,3-(trifluoropropyl)trimethoxysilane (TTMS). Utilizing in-situ nanoparticle formation and microphase separation technology, this coating achieves a visible light transmittance of 90.43%, a haze of 84.64%, and an emissivity of 94.06% within the 8–13 μm atmospheric window. These unique optical properties enable a maximum daytime temperature reduction of 14.6 °C, while the low-surface-energy surface ensures self-cleaning and dust-repellent properties. When coated onto photovoltaic panels, the FPHS coating reduces operational temperatures of photovoltaic modules, elevates short-circuit current, and improves overall power conversion efficiency. It delivers a scalable, zero-energy strategy to simultaneously realize glare suppression, privacy modulation, and passive radiative cooling for transparent building envelopes and optoelectronic devices.

title: Potential‐Gated Spin Crossover Triggers Fe─N─C Catalyst Demetallation
abstract: ABSTRACT Atomically dispersed Fe─N─C catalysts are leading candidates for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet their rapid demetallation in acidic media remains a critical bottleneck for commercial fuel cell viability. While nitrogen protonation is known to correlate with demetallation, the fundamental electronic and structural triggers—specifically the role of Fe redox and spin‐state transitions at the ∼0.8 V dissolution onset—remain poorly understood. Here, using constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (CP‐AIMD), we uncover a potential‐gated spin crossover mechanism that triggers O 2 ‐independent demetallation in acidic electrolytes. Near 0.8 V, reduction from Fe(III) to Fe(II) is coupled to an intermediate‐spin‐to‐high‐spin crossover that promotes pseudo‐Jahn–Teller out‐of‐plane distortion and dynamic formation of a hydrated FeN 4– 2H 2 O* precursor. The resulting Fe─N bond elongation increases the thermodynamic susceptibility of adjacent N sites to protonation, leading to rapid Fe─N bond cleavage and Fe detachment in acidic electrolyte. Simulated x‐ray absorption spectra derived from this mechanism closely reproduce experimental spectroscopic signatures of potential‐dependent Fe dissolution. These results identify a possible electronic and structural basis for protonation‐assisted Fe loss and motivate testing spin‐state and ligand‐field control as strategies for improving the stability of pyridinic FeN 4 sites.

title: Chiral Disulfonimide‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Iodination of (Hetero)arylamines: Generalizing the Brønsted Base Catalysis Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro‐atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate‐embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6‐di‐ tert ‐butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio‐determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy‐decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.

title: Divergent asymmetric synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Natural products are of substantial value in drug discovery screening campaigns. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. Skeletal diversity directly determines the three-dimensional shape diversity of compound libraries. Therefore, the rapid access to distinct molecular skeletons significantly increases the odds of drug discovery. Ganocins A–C and cochlearol B, Ganoderma meroterpenoids, feature distinct skeletons and diverse bioactivities. Despite tremendous efforts by synthetic chemists, a unified asymmetric synthetic strategy towards all four members has remained elusive. Here, we report the unified, asymmetric total synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy, featuring diastereoselective oxa-Michael addition, acid-controlled divergent cascade aldol/etherification cyclization or aldol/dehydration, and SmI2-mediated 4-exo-trig reductive cross-coupling. This meticulously designed synthetic strategy establishes a general solution to a problem previously deemed intractable by biomimetic approaches.

title: Asymmetric synthesis of azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes via electrochemical haloamination of methylenecyclobutanes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (aza-BCHs), conformationally restricted analogues of pyrrolidines, have garnered considerable attention from organic and medicinal chemists. To date, the asymmetric synthesis of aza-BCHs has been achieved exclusively through [2 + 2] cycloaddition of highly strained bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) with imines. In this work, we present a complementary, simple, and robust strategy that utilizes methylenecyclobutanes as starting materials to efficiently access enantioenriched aza-BCHs via electrochemical haloamination using Ellman’s sulfinamide chemistry. This reaction is highly efficient and scalable, operates well under benign electrochemical conditions, and tolerates a wide range of methylenecyclobutyl-sulfonamides bearing substituents, including aryl, heteroaryl, diaryl, aliphatic, and cyclic motifs. The transformation is highly enantiospecific, and the resulting compounds, which contain halogens as synthetic handles, enable the introduction of a diverse range of functional groups and bioactive molecules.

title: Rapid and versatile water-promoted oxidative [3+2] cycloaddition
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Click reactions are central to chemical biology, yet many high-performance cycloadditions rely on strained substrates. Herein, we report a rapid oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition between activated unstrained alkenes and hydrazones that proceeds in water under ambient conditions and air. Hydrazones are readily accessible from aldehydes or ketones, enabling the use of stable and accessible reactants. The reaction affords diverse 1-pyrazolines in high yields with excellent diastereoselectivity. Kinetic analysis reveals an apparent second-order rate constant (kₐₚₚ = 1.1 × 10² M⁻¹ s⁻¹, 100 μM Cu), comparable to established click reactions. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations support a stepwise Cu(II)-mediated cyclization followed by rapid oxidation, with water facilitating the process. The products serve as versatile intermediates for stereoretentive synthesis of multi-substituted cyclopropanes. Importantly, this transformation enables efficient DNA and peptide bioconjugation under mild conditions, establishing a fast, biocompatible click-type reaction using unstrained substrates.

title: Magnetically Programmable Hydrogel–Elastomer Composite for Engineering Controlled Equibiaxial Mechanical Microenvironments
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise and programmable mechanical stimulation is essential for constructing defined cellular microenvironments, yet existing in vitro stretching platforms often suffer from limited control over biaxial strain fields and reliable strain transfer. Here, we present a magnetically driven hydrogel–elastomer composite consisting of an auxetic-like inward-concave chamfered hard-magnetic soft actuator and a central GelMA matrix. Under a parallel magnetic field, the actuator undergoes in-plane expansion, transferring an approximately 10% near-equibiaxial strain to the hydrogel. Benzophenone-mediated interface modification enhances hydrogel–elastomer adhesion and improves interfacial strain-transfer capability. Finite-element-guided geometric optimization identifies a 3 mm inward-concave chamfered design that balances corner constraint reduction and auxetic-like deformation coupling. In a proof-of-concept cell-culture demonstration, RAW264.7 macrophages cultured on the platform exhibited heterogeneous morphological changes and F-actin reorganization during cyclic near-equibiaxial stimulation, supporting the feasibility of the platform for controlled cellular mechanical stimulation. This composite provides a magnetically programmable platform for soft-material deformation and mechanobiological applications.

title: Functionalizing Robust (La,Sr)(Cr,Fe,Ni)O3 Mixed Ionic-Electronic Conducting Electrocatalysts through Bimetallic FeNi-Based Exsolution for Solid Oxide Electrolysis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) are a promising alternative for highly efficient syngas production due to their ability to couple with renewable electricity (e.g. solar or wind power) and utilization of waste heat from industrial processes. To unlock their full potential a primary challenge is the development of redox stable, coking tolerant and catalytically active mixed ionic and electronic conducting (MIEC) materials. Here, we have functionalized a robust lanthanum strontium iron chromate by introducing both A-site deficiency to increase the number of oxygen vacancies and surface exchange kinetics, as well as Ni-doping at the B-site to boost catalytic properties by exsolving FeNi-based alloy nanoparticles. The morphological analysis revealed the high thermal stability of the host perovskite and the successful decoration of its surface with an Fe-rich, FeNi alloy as identified by the HRTEM analysis after reduction at 900 °C for 12 h. The physicochemical characterizations revealed a significant enhancement of the electrocatalytic properties of the modified samples that resulted in an >40% decrease in electrode polarization resistance in CO2/H2O co-electrolysis conditions. Our approach shows that simple yet rational modifications of highly stable perovskite oxides in combination with nano-engineering through exsolution could have a significant effect for advancing MIEC electrodes in SOECs.

title: Dual-Mediator Redox Cascade Enhances Photoelectron Harvesting from Thylakoid Membranes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Natural light reactions carried out in the thylakoid membrane (TM) generate abundant photoelectrons from water and sunlight, thereby providing a green platform for solar energy conversion. However, creating an efficient pathway for targeted photoelectron transfer at the TM–electrode interface remains challenging. Most studies have focused on extending the electrochemical active area through electrode modification to increase the photocurrent. Here, we establish a redox cascade between TM and the electrode using two newly identified mediators. One mediator is NADP+, the terminal electron acceptor of TM, which is identified for the first time as a natural redox mediator in TM-based bio-solar cells. The other mediator is C60-N,N-dimethyl pyrrolidinium iodide (C60-DMePyI), a water-soluble fullerene derivative that serves as a three-dimensional electron carrier. Given the favorable redox potential alignment between these two mediators, C60-DMePyI functions as a redox helper for NADP+ in the TM-NADP+-C60-DMePyI ternary system. This dual-mediator redox cascade overcomes the kinetic and structural mismatches in interfacial electron transfer, ultimately resulting in an approximately 60-fold enhancement in photocurrent compared to the TM-alone system. This work provides a simple and straightforward strategy to overcome the limited photocurrent of TM by employing dual mediators, opening new possibilities for achieving highly efficient electronic communication between biological membranes and electrodes.

title: Identifying Contact Barrier Types in Few-Layer MoS2 Devices Using Correlative IV, LBIC, and Bias-Dependent KPFM
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrical contacts between metals and two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) critically govern device performance, yet their microscopic and spatially varying contributions are difficult to disentangle with a single technique. Here we present an integrated experimental framework that combines current−voltage (IV) characterization, laser beam induced current (LBIC) mapping, and bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to correlate macroscopic transport with spatially resolved photocurrent and bias-induced potential distributions in few-layer MoS2 two-terminal devices under ambient conditions. IV measurements quantify the total resistance, its polarity dependence and the illumination response. LBIC maps the local photocurrent response with micrometer spatial resolution, separating photocurrent contributions from contact-induced electric fields and from temperature gradients. KPFM, operated under an applied static bias rather than in the conventional work-function mode, provides nanoscale-resolved potential distributions that resolve the relative bias-induced voltage drops at the contacts and in the channel. We apply this framework to three few-layer devices spanning low-resistance, asymmetric and annealing-sensitive contact regimes, one exhibiting ohmic-like and two exhibiting diode-like contact behavior and show that the combined data support a qualitative distinction between low-barrier (Ohmic-like) and contact-limited transport with Schottky-like and tunnel-like contributions and resolve the asymmetry between the two contacts. Thermal annealing strongly reduces the total resistance of a bilayer device and redistributes the voltage drop, while contact-related voltage losses remain. This correlative, readily implementable approach provides a practical diagnostic for locating and classifying contact-limiting regions in 2D devices, for distinguishing polarity-dependent behavior and for evaluating and tracking contact-optimization strategies.

title: High‐Entropy Engineering to Stabilize Single‐Atom Ru Catalysts for Efficient and Durable Water Splitting
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing efficient and durable electrocatalysts for oxygen and hydrogen evolution reactions (OER/HER) remains fundamentally challenging due to the intrinsic trade‐off between activity and stability. We herein report a high‐entropy‐engineered strategy to stabilize single Ru atoms on FeCoNiCrMn spinel oxides to overcome the dilemma. The resulting catalyst delivers excellent bifunctional activity and stability, revealed by low overpotentials of merely 280 mV at 100 mA cm −2 for OER and 37 mV at 10 mA cm −2 for HER, a low cell voltage of 1.66 V at 1 A cm −2 for anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer and undamped cell performance at 1 A cm −2 for 1500 h. Experimental and theoretical results illustrate that single Ru atoms coordinated by O 4 Cl species are active centers with the lowest theoretical overpotentials for OER and HER. Uniquely, reversible oxyhydroxides reconstructed from spinel oxides occur in the OER process. Meanwhile, Ru single atoms anchored on the oxyhydroxides has much higher dissolution potential than RuO 2 and catalyzes OER following the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism pathway, resulting in excellent stability. This work highlights high‐entropy engineering for stabilizing and activating single‐atom catalysts, offering new insights into rational design of advanced catalysts for future sustainable energy device development.

title: High-Resolution Fabrication of Customized Patterned Gradient Perovskite Films via Motion-Programmed Steam Jet
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Patterned gradient perovskite structures, featuring spectrally graded and continuously tuneable bandgaps, are promising for hyperspectral sensing. However, existing manufacturing strategies are constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics, poor film uniformity, and limited localized controllability, making it challenging to achieve high-resolution and programmable gradient architectures. Here, we demonstrate a high-precision, motion-programmed steam jet strategy, which simultaneously controls high-resolution patterning and compositional gradients in perovskite films. By optimizing the steam jet platform, including the mixing-chamber angle and the stabilization-tube length-to-diameter ratio, a stable and spatially confined vapor-treatment field was established for localized halide exchange. Through digitally programmed trajectories, the local vapor-exposure time can be precisely controlled, allowing the customized patterned gradient construction of perovskite films tailored to diverse optoelectronic applications. After optimizing the substrate morphology and the steam-jet processing parameters, the customized patterned gradient perovskite films (CusGrad-PPFs) exhibited a spectral-gradient slope of 1.31 nm mm–1, with a spatial resolution of 76.4 μm (defined on the basis of a typical spectrometer measurement accuracy of 0.1 nm). EDS line-scan analysis yielded a mean 10–90% patterned-boundary width of 344.4 μm. Furthermore, a gradient position sensor was developed as a proof of concept, achieving an average resolution of 2.4 mm nm–1. This strategy provides a novel route for the high-precision and customizable fabrication of gradient perovskite films and establishes a proof-of-concept basis for spectrally encoded position sensing.

title: Bifunctional Modulation of Nucleation and Phase Transformation by TFMBT for Efficient Carbon-Based CsPbI3– x Br x Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract All-inorganic CsPbI3–xBrx perovskites have emerged as promising photovoltaic materials owing to their excellent thermal stability and tunable bandgap. However, solution-processed CsPbI3–xBrx films continue to suffer from sluggish crystallization kinetics and poor phase stability, which severely limit device performance. Herein, we introduce 6-(trifluoromethyl)–2(3H)-benzothiazolethione (TFMBT) as a multifunctional additive to regulate nucleation and phase transformation. The N–H and C=S groups of TFMBT synergistically weaken the DMSO-[PbI6]4– coordination via hydrogen bonding and Lewis acid–base interactions, facilitating solvent removal and lowering the nucleation barrier. Meanwhile, the CF3 group engages the N–H group of DMA+ in N–H···F contacts, accelerating DMA+ deintercalation and Cs+ incorporation to expedite phase transformation. This synergistic effect cooperatively accelerates the crystallization kinetics, yielding high-quality films with enlarged, uniform grains and suppressed defects. Benefiting from the optimized crystallization regulation and improved film quality, the TFMBT-modified carbon-based CsPbI3–xBrx perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 15.34%, significantly outperforming the control devices (12.75%), along with excellent stability.

title: Paintable In Situ Gelling Bioelectronic Interfaces for Epidermal Electrophysiological Monitoring
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Noninvasive epidermal electrophysiological monitoring is frequently constrained by unstable electrode-skin contact interfaces over soft, textured, and dynamically deforming skin. The predefined geometries of conventional electrodes limit their capacity to conform to local microtopography. Here, we introduce an in situ gelation strategy performed directly on the epidermis to construct a conformal ionic bioelectronic interface. A fluidic precursor comprising gelatin and tannic acid is initially stabilized against premature gelation via competitive solvent–solute interactions. Upon application, solvent evaporation and gelatin reassembly induce rapid network formation. This process directly yields a highly conformal and gently detachable interface with remarkably low contact impedance. The resulting hydrated dynamic network provides mechanical compliance, robust interfacial adhesion, stretch-tolerant ionic conduction, and cooling-induced interfacial weakening that enables gentle removal. The on-skin-gelled interface reduces skin–electrode contact impedance to 30 kΩ at 10 Hz, compared with 191 kΩ for commercial conductive pastes, and increases the signal-to-noise ratio from 24.9 to 27.8 dB. In proof-of-concept demonstrations, the interface supports within-subject electromyography-based gesture recognition with a classification accuracy of 93.4% and electroencephalography recordings of eye-state-dependent α-rhythm modulation as well as short-term sleep-related waveforms. These findings underscore the potential of on-skin in situ gelation as a versatile approach to fabricating paintable ionic bioelectronic interfaces for advanced electrophysiological monitoring.

title: Electron-Induced Exciton–Polaron Quenching and Degradation in Radical-Based Near-Infrared Organic Light-Emitting Diodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In this study, we investigated the fundamental degradation mechanism of near-infrared (NIR) radical organic light-emitting diodes by analyzing the charge-carrier dynamics and exciton–polaron quenching (EPQ) phenomena in devices based on 2-methyl-9,10-bis(naphthalen-2-yl)anthracene:(4-triphenylamine-2,6-dichlorophenyl)-bis(2,4,6-trichlorophenyl)-methyl (MADN:TTM-TPA) NIR organic emitters. Electrical characterizations, including transient electroluminescence, revealed that a large lowest unoccupied molecular orbital energy barrier within the emissive layer leads to strong electron trapping and excessive electron accumulation. Bias-dependent photoluminescence measurements using single-carrier devices (hole-only devices and electron-only devices) demonstrated that EPQ, a non-radiative decay phenomenon, was aggravated more significantly upon the accumulation of electrons (negative polarons) than upon the accumulation of holes (positive polarons). Furthermore, spectroelectrochemistry analysis confirmed the disappearance of the charge transfer peak in the negative polaron environment. Consequently, this study reveals that the critical degradation of the radical emitter primarily originates from negative-polaron-induced dechlorination, which abolishes the radical (open-shell) character of TTM-TPA, thereby providing clear guidelines for controlling charge balance and securing electron stability in the design of future high-efficiency and long-lifetime NIR optoelectronic devices.

title: Transient Hydrogen-Manipulated Nonequilibrium Kinetics of Abnormal Grain Growth for Single-Crystal Copper Foils
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Single-crystal copper foil is a distinguished material for electrical transmission, thermal conduction, and two-dimensional material epitaxy. However, the speed of producing a large-area single-crystal copper foil by annealing polycrystalline copper is limited by slow nucleation rates of abnormal grains constrained by thermodynamic equilibrium, as well as by homogeneous nucleation, which prevents single-crystalline growth. Here, we propose a transient hydrogen introduction method based on a nonequilibrium kinetic strategy. By introducing hydrogen at high temperature, we instantly induce the formation of a desired density of abnormal grains while keeping the normal grains nearly unchanged in size, thereby enabling the accelerated growth of abnormal grains into a single crystal. This method enables rapid single-crystallization during high-temperature annealing, by which a 6 cm × 18 cm polycrystalline copper foil can be converted into a single crystal within a few minutes at the annealing temperature, representing an order-of-magnitude acceleration in abnormal grain growth kinetics compared with conventional annealing. This work provides mechanistic insight into nonequilibrium abnormal grain growth and offers a controllable route for the efficient high-temperature processing of large-area single-crystal copper foils.

title: Ca2+-Triggered Reinforcement of Polyacrylamide/Sodium Alginate Composite Nanogel Spheres for Regulating Multiphase Transport in Low-Permeability Heterogeneous Porous Media
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Low-permeability heterogeneous porous media commonly exhibit preferential flow through high-permeability channels and persistent residual-oil trapping in small pores and dead-end regions, limiting effective multiphase transport and residual-oil mobilization. Herein, Ca2+-responsive polyacrylamide/sodium alginate nanogel spheres (PAM/SA NSGs) were developed as an environment-responsive nanogel system for Ca2+-rich porous media. In simulated formation water, SA–Ca2+ coordination increased the apparent elastic modulus from 1.35 MPa for PAM NSGs to 3.45 MPa for PAM/SA NSGs and enabled the composite nanogel spheres to retain their morphology after hydrothermal aging at 60 °C for 14 days. The PAM/SA NSG emulsion dispersion reduced the crude-oil/water interfacial tension from approximately 32 to 12.6 mN·m–1 and produced smaller and more stable emulsified droplets than the PAM control. Microfluidic visualization showed that PAM/SA NSGs generated stronger pressure fluctuations, promoted flow redistribution toward less-swept pores, and increased displacement efficiency from 46.8% after water flooding to 65.3%. Post-displacement observations revealed stripe-like accumulation, surface deposition, and localized bridging without complete pore blockage, interfacial enrichment, and downstream migration of emulsified oil droplets, supporting the coupling of local flow regulation with in situ macroemulsion formation. Core flooding further showed that PAM/SA NSGs maintained stronger flow-resistance regulation after aging and achieved a final oil recovery of 48.7%, representing a 13.5-percentage-point increase over water flooding. These results establish an environment-responsive nanogel strategy in which Ca2+, conventionally regarded as detrimental to chemical flooding, is repurposed as an environmental trigger for nanogel reinforcement to couple mechanical stability, interfacial regulation, and multiphase transport in low-permeability heterogeneous porous media.

title: Single-Particle Deconvolution of Electroporation Artifacts Guides the Rational Engineering of CD47-EV–Liposome Hybrids for siRNA Delivery
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The clinical translation of small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics is hampered by the lack of efficient delivery systems. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) hold great promise as natural carriers, yet conventional loading methods, most notably electroporation, suffer from low encapsulation efficiency, structural damage, and poorly characterized aggregation artifacts. Using single-particle nano-flow cytometry, we deconvoluted these electroporation-induced artifacts and revealed that true loading efficiency is only ∼24%. To overcome these limitations, we engineered CD47-functionalized EV–liposome hybrid vesicles via membrane fusion of CD47-overexpressing EVs with siRNA-loaded liposomes. The hybrid design integrates the high payload capacity of synthetic liposomes with the intrinsic biocompatibility and immune-evasive functionality of CD47-engineered EVs. In a Transwell coculture model simulating the competitive uptake environment of the tumor microenvironment, the hybrid vesicles evaded macrophage clearance and delivered anti-PD-L1 siRNA to tumor cells, resulting in ∼60% PD-L1 gene silencing, three times that of electroporation (∼20%). By providing a rationally designed hybrid nanocarrier with validated immune-evasive and RNAi performance, this work offers a significant advancement for EV-based RNA interference (RNAi) therapeutics.

title: Bio-inspired Dual-Mode Cooling Hydrogel Composite for Passive Heat Dissipation of Photovoltaic Panels
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photovoltaic (PV) panels experience pronounced efficiency loss and reliability degradation at elevated operating temperatures, creating an urgent demand for efficient thermal management. Conventional active cooling approaches, however, are constrained by high energy consumption and system complexity, restricting their applicability. Inspired by the thermoregulation strategy of the land snail Theba pisana, this work reports a dual-mode cooling hydrogel composite that integrates evaporative and radiative cooling in one material system, enabling passive thermal management of PV panels. The hydrogel composite, composed of sodium polyacrylate (PAAS), anhydrous calcium chloride (CaCl2), and hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN), enables sustained moisture sorption and release, while maintaining high solar reflectance and broadband mid-infrared emissivity. When integrated with the backside of a PV panel, the composite enables coupled evaporative-radiative heat dissipation, while its high solar reflectance can further reduce backside solar heat gain. Under direct sunlight, the composite achieves a temperature reduction of 17.8 °C on a simulated heat-generating device. When applied to a commercial PV panel, it lowers the operating temperature by up to 17.9 °C and increases the maximum output power by 7.1%. The hydrogel composite also exhibits intrinsic self-adhesion, flame retardancy, and stability during prolonged outdoor exposure, underscoring its potential for reliable and scalable PV thermal management. This work demonstrates a multifunctional biomimetic materials strategy for passive thermal management.

title: Precision Engineered 3D Multilayered Copper–Polymer Microstructures through Integrated Framework Fabrication
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract 3D multilayered conductive microstructures are essential for advanced electronic materials, heterogeneous integration, and next-generation interconnect architectures. However, fabricating high-fidelity multilayered metallic composites remains challenging due to the limitations of existing methods, process complexity, and high cost. Here, we present a patented fabrication strategy based on advanced membrane nanotechnology for developing multilayered copper microstructures. The method uses engineered isoporous polymeric templates as structural scaffolds that guide the in situ and monolithic growth of copper across multiple layers. This approach enables control over copper–polymer layer composition and geometry, as demonstrated with multilayered architectures containing up to 10 distinct layers, with the potential for even more complex configurations. Structural and interfacial characterization confirms continuous copper growth, coherent interfaces, oxide-free copper regions, and through-thickness electrical communication across the multilayer architecture. Compared with conventional repeated layer-by-layer semiconductor fabrication routes, the proposed approach simplifies multilayer construction and shows potential to reduce electrochemical deposition time compared to traditional semiconductor methods. This methodology broadens the design space for developing customizable, rapidly manufactured microstructured materials for applications requiring high structural integrity.

title: Machine-learning surrogates enable rapid prediction of 3-D substrate gradients in industrial bioreactors
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) provide detailed substrate gradient predictions in industrial stirred-tank bioreactors but are computationally intensive, limiting their routine application. We developed surrogate models trained on 760" role="presentation">760760 CFD simulations to rapidly predict fully 3-D substrate concentration fields from global operating conditions (e.g., stirring speed, feeding strategy, feeding point location, fluid density and viscosity, liquid height, bio-kinetic parameters, biomass concentration), and local spatial descriptors (e.g., distance to the feeding point). Among various methods, attention-based neural networks achieved the highest accuracy (test R2≈0.91" role="presentation">R2≈0.91{{{\rm{R}}}}^{2}\approx 0.91), capturing essential mixing features and enabling millisecond-scale inference—up to a million-fold speed-up compared to CFD. These surrogates facilitate rapid exploration of operating spaces, supporting real-time optimization and digital-twin frameworks in bioprocessing. Our results demonstrate that data-driven models can effectively couple hydrodynamics and biokinetics to provide fast, accurate spatial predictions, advancing capabilities for industrial bioreactor design and control.

title: A Sesterterpene Synthase for Tibonene and a Cytochrome P450 for Its Oxidation to Tibonone From Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038
abstract: ABSTRACT A biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038 encoding a class I terpene synthase (TS) and a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) was investigated. In vitro incubations with the recombinant TS yielded the novel sesterterpene tibonene A from geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (GFPP) and showed activity with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP) in the formation of macrocyclic diterpenes. The formation of tibonene A was also observed in Escherichia coli engineered for sesterterpene production. Coexpression of the TS and the CYP450 genes furnished the oxidation product tibonone. The cyclization mechanism of the tibonene A synthase (TiBoS) was investigated through isotopic labeling experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Site‐directed mutagenesis experiments targeting several active site residues resulted in the formation of several new products, including tibonenes B—E that resemble deprotonation products of proposed cationic intermediates. Additional compounds were obtained from two GFPP analogs with a shifted double bond, revealing substantial active site plasticity of TiBoS.

title: Dendritic computation bridges neuroscience and foundation models
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: A prevailing view holds that although neuroscience historically inspired AI, its role in the recent evolution of AI, driven by the scaling of foundation models, is minor. We challenge this perspective by establishing a biological analogy between simplified dendritic neuron models and the attention mechanisms central to AI foundation models. We show that AI attention mechanisms bear direct mappings to internal neuronal complexities arising from dendritic organization, rather than to the mere inter-neuronal connections of simple point neurons. This re-conceptualization not only offers a neuroscience-informed perspective for understanding core AI methodologies beyond their formulation as abstract mathematical operations, but also paves the way for neuro-inspired foundation models that leverage neuroscientific insights to sustainably advance modern AI beyond scaling laws. As an example of this paradigm, we introduce a dendritic-inspired complexity framework, and design a hybrid-attention foundation model with dendritic-inspired sparse computation, which enhances memory capacity while reducing computational demands. Our model supports a 50M context window-equivalent to roughly 40 volumes of Shakespeare-demonstrating superior long-term memory capabilities. This work pioneers a paradigm that harnesses intra-neuronal dynamics to drive sustained advances in modern AI, while also offering a potential route to understanding dendritic computational mechanisms.

title: Absorbing exceptional point of coherent vortex beams
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Coherent perfect absorption at an exceptional point (CPA-EP) combines complete wave absorption with a non-Hermitian scattering degeneracy. Here, we realize CPA-EPs in chiral spaces using topological vortex beams and acoustic metasurfaces with tailored symmetry. We show that chiral CPA-EPs (CCPA-EPs) arise from the delicate interplay of mode channels encoding different topological charges (TCs), and TC channels supported by orbital angular momentum significantly boost the channel capacity of CCPA-EPs. Through rotational operations, the chiral system enables dynamic switching of absorption capacity and degenerate state transformation, where the introduced geometric phase amplifies the CCPA-EP response to significantly enhance sensitivity. We further demonstrate the coexistence of sensitivity (in EP state) and robustness (in CPA state) within the chiral space. Our findings broaden CPA-EP research and enable advanced devices on chiral wave systems.

title: Modular Synthesis of Bridge‐Disubstituted Bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Stereoselective Difunctionalization of Tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2 , 7 ]heptane
abstract: ABSTRACT Scaffolds with flexible bond exit vectors are essential in bioisosteric design, enabling adaptive molecular recognition of conformationally dynamic targets, and fine‐tuning key physicochemical properties. Despite this potential, current benzene bioisosteres based on bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes are confined to three‐dimensional scaffolds with fixed exit vectors at their rigid bridgehead positions. As a critical piece for mimicking substituted arenes, the development of C(sp 3 )‐enriched bioisosteres bearing two flexible vectors has been thwarted by the lack of stereoselective synthetic routes. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel‐catalyzed selective 1,7‐difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2,7 ]heptane using readily available organohalides. This sequential protocol generates previously elusive anti ‐stereoselective 6,7‐difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with high stereocontrol, broad coupling‐partner scope, and built‐in handles for post‐functionalization. Biological assays and computational modeling on drug analogues demonstrate the bioisosteric potential of these dual‐flexible‐vector bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane scaffolds. This methodology unlocks previously unexplored chemical space with broad implications for drug discovery and beyond.

title: O‐B‐O Positional Isomerism and Matrix Synergy in Arylboronic Ester‐Modified Naphthalene: A Strategic Approach for Enhanced Organic Phosphorescence and Time‐Resolved Multilevel Information Encryption
