Node-aware spatiotemporal carbon tracing and carbon-responsive control of electrified railways for emission reduction and tertiary reserves
abstract: The decarbonization of electrified transportation reshapes the interaction between power systems and mobile energy loads. As a key component of this sector, electrified railways draw large, geographically distributed traction loads whose emissions are governed by the power system’s spatiotemporally varying carbon intensity (CI). However, existing carbon tracing methods typically use spatially uniform emission factors, obscuring nodal carbon intensity (CI) differences. Consequently, long-distance trains cannot perceive or exploit spatial carbon heterogeneity when allocating traction power along their routes. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a unified framework that transforms heterogeneous railway fleets into active, carbon-responsive resources within the power system. First, a node-aware spatiotemporal carbon tracing method integrates Power Transfer Distribution Factors (PTDF) with dynamic train-node mapping, enabling real-time quantification of the nodal carbon intensity (NCI) experienced by mobile loads. Building upon this, a two-stage hierarchical coordinated control strategy is formulated, embedding dynamic NCI signals into an online receding-horizon predictive controller to achieve joint carbon minimization and tertiary reserve. The controller autonomously executes spatiotemporal load shifting by dynamically regulating traction and braking power to avoid high-carbon zones while maintaining schedule adherence. Case studies on high-speed and freight railways demonstrate that traditional system-average carbon accounting systematically obscures local low-carbon zones, overestimating the fleet’s true carbon footprint by more than four times under severe spatiotemporal mismatch. By actively exploiting these spatial zero-carbon opportunities, the proposed NCI-aware control achieves substantial carbon reductions, of 37.14% for high-speed trains and 34.74% for freight trains, while maintaining schedule adherence. Crucially, the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition reveals that these emission mitigations originate predominantly from the strategic utilization of low-carbon nodes, rather than mere energy conservation. These results demonstrate a promising framework for integrated power–transport system decarbonization, transforming electrified railways from passive loads into active carbon-aware grid participants.

title: Strategic scenario planning for hydrogen supply chains via graph convolutional networks: overcoming mid-stream infrastructure bottlenecks in energy transitions
abstract: : Hydrogen transitions require a combination of change in policy, production, distribution, and adoption, but current scenario consistency assessment only checks for trend coherence without incorporating the role of the relationships among the stakeholders in shaping those emerging pathways. This study introduces a Graph Convolutional Network-based Scenario Planning (GCN-SP) framework that extends scenario-consistency assessment by linking actor-node engagement with emerging trends to graph-based representations of representative hydrogen scenarios. Multi-driver interaction effects are transformed into strategic scenario graphs, clustered using k-means to derive representative configurations from cluster centroids, and classified using a graph convolutional network. The optimal model achieves weighted precision and recall exceeding 0.78 under both cross-validation and hold-out validation and outperforms two multilayer perceptron baselines. Three distinct structural configurations emerge. Coordinated: aligned actors across government, production, distribution, and adoption form a mutually reinforcing structure supporting system integration. Divergent: production and international connectivity advance while the producer becomes disconnected from the domestic network, creating an export-oriented pathway. Constrained: supply-side ambition and transport expansion outpace downstream adoption, leaving the value chain incomplete. Across scenarios, distribution emerges as a structurally important link whose connectivity determines whether production translates into integration. These results show that similar stakeholder activity can generate fundamentally different outcomes depending on interaction configuration. GCN-SP therefore enables structural distinction between coordinated integration, export-oriented divergence, and supply-led constraint.

title: Epeditor: A scalable platform for large-ensemble building energy simulation enabling agent-assisted automation
abstract: The data scale of energy simulation keeps increasing, particularly in urban building energy modeling (UBEM) and uncertainty analysis, where thousands of EnergyPlus runs are often required to explore complex parameter spaces and building variability. To simplify these data-intensive workflows, recent studies have introduced AI agents for end-to-end simulation tasks. However, in practice, both AI-assisted and conventional batch workflows remain constrained by unstable field inference and search bias, inefficient large-ensemble simulation execution, and cumbersome data processing. To address these problems, this study introduces Epeditor, a cloud-deployable simulation infrastructure for large-ensemble building energy analysis for both AI and human users. It combines three improvements on current workflows: a knowledge-assisted parameterization with more accurate and stable field search in IDF files; a simulator that improves parallel execution efficiency through Operating-System-Level deployment; and a data management system that enables memory-safe aggregation of large simulation inputs and outputs. The packaged Agent Skill allows AI agents to execute fully automated dataset generation, batch simulation, surrogate modeling, and interpretation through an auditable workflow. Epeditor is evaluated through a agent benchmarks with metrics for Artificial General Intelligence, and two case studies are introduced to show its ability in research and design practices including an AI-assisted surrogate-modeling case, and design-studio practices. The pipeline exhibits 99.98% robustness in IDF generation, up to four-fold acceleration in high-parallel simulation, and 76.28 ( F 1 ) in IDF field inference. These findings indicate that Epeditor can lower the technical and computational barriers to large-ensemble EnergyPlus simulation, supporting more accessible, reproducible, and AI-ready building energy analysis.

title: Accurately modeling long-term storage with minimum representative hours in large-scale renewable energy systems
abstract: Energy system optimization often relies on time series aggregation to ensure computational tractability. Aggregation generally loses the chronology of time steps, which renders the storage level representation challenging. Typically, this challenge is addressed by using representative days (RD) to utilize intra-day chronology, even though representative hours (RH) can describe the input time series more accurately at fewer representative time steps than RD. However, until now, the use of RH storage representation methods has been limited by high computational complexity, poor accuracy in clustering and storage representation, and restricted applicability. Here, we present a novel storage representation method based on RH that combines the high accuracy of time-series aggregation via RH with the high computational efficiency of RD-based methods. Through benchmarking the four most established storage representation methods on a model of a net-zero European energy system, we find that the proposed method can reduce the solving time by over 95% for the same objective value compared to the most established RD and RH methods. The proposed method exhibits particular strengths at strong aggregations of low- to mid-hundreds of representative hours per year, making it especially applicable to large-scale, sector-coupled transition pathway models. The developed method for accurately modeling both short-term and long-term storage, along with the presented findings, is of practical relevance to energy system modelers who seek computational tractability in large-scale applications while avoiding the misallocation of storage and conversion capacities.

title: Causality-constrained hierarchical LLM agents for online rule adaptation in building HVAC control
abstract: Adaptive multi-zone HVAC control often requires identifying a building-specific predictive model or training a policy through environment interaction. These requirements increase the effort needed to deploy adaptive controllers across buildings with different HVAC configurations. To address this challenge, we propose a causality-constrained hierarchical large language model (LLM) agent framework for online cooling-setpoint rule adaptation. The framework operates in two stages. Offline onboarding standardizes building management system (BMS) points and establishes a human-confirmed causal graph. During online rule adaptation, hierarchical agents propose hourly updates to rule-based controllers (RBCs), while the RBCs generate 15-min setpoints. Structural and causal checks, together with zone cooling allowances, determine whether each proposed update is incorporated into the RBC. We evaluate the framework in three BOPTEST cases with one, two, and five zones against basic and enhanced RBCs, hierarchical model predictive control, proximal policy optimization (PPO), and multi-agent PPO. The framework achieved the highest mean reward and the lowest mean energy use among the compared controllers in all three cases. Energy use was 2.2–43.2% lower than that of the baselines, accompanied by small accumulated PMV deviations of 0.0192–0.4542 PMV ⋅ h. The causal experiments showed that the complete causal layer reduced accumulated PMV deviation and safety interventions in every case, primarily by constraining and stabilizing rule adaptation. Further ablations quantified the effects of memory, cross-zone coordination, and LLM thinking on rule adaptation, control performance, and LLM inference overhead. Overall, the framework combines competitive energy and comfort performance with explicit, reviewable online rule adaptation, supporting its potential for adaptive multi-zone HVAC control across the evaluated HVAC configurations.

title: Learning scheduling-relevant joint uncertainty: Decision-aware compound-risk forecasting for microgrid dispatch
abstract: This paper studies joint probabilistic forecasting for renewable-rich microgrid scheduling, where costly operating outcomes are often caused by simultaneous high load and low renewable generation rather than by a large error in any single variable. The main challenge is to preserve calibrated load, wind, and PV marginals while assigning appropriate probability mass to the joint tail states that matter for dispatch. We propose a Compound-Risk End-to-End (CoRisk-E2E) framework that combines physically feasible marginal forecasting, conditional rank-diffusion scenario generation, compound-stress supervision, and decision-aware training. It preserves non-crossing marginals, captures temporal and cross-variable dependence, and emphasizes high-load and low-renewable conditions through progressive training with a continuous scheduling surrogate. The differentiable scheduling surrogate is used only for training, while all reported operating results are evaluated with the original exact two-stage CVaR MILP. The framework is evaluated in three data settings: the complete Rye load–wind–PV microgrid benchmark, a reduced IEEE load–PV case, and a public load–wind–solar transfer case. The results show that CoRisk-E2E improves joint-tail representation and exact-MILP operating performance, although NoDecision remains competitive on marginal and global scenario metrics. The operational benefit persists in the reduced-source case and the mapped transfer setting under the fixed Rye scheduler, but decreases with stronger domain shift. These findings indicate that explicitly learning scheduling-critical joint tails can improve microgrid decisions, while broader validation on additional complete microgrid systems remains necessary.

title: Optimal control strategy for compressed air energy storage under off-design conditions
abstract: Compressed air energy storage (CAES) serves as a critical enabling technology for grid-scale integration of renewable energy. Most existing studies on off-design CAES operation focus on improving efficiency through individual control strategies. However, systematic comparisons of different operating strategies, especially their combined effects on volumetric storage density and the underlying thermodynamic trade-offs, are still lacking. This study develops a thermodynamic model for a four-stage CAES system integrated with a dual-tank water-based thermal storage module, and systematically evaluates three operating strategies, namely unregulated operation, inlet guide vane (IGV) regulation, and speed regulation, under variable backpressure conditions. The results demonstrate that speed regulation yields the highest round-trip efficiency (RTE) of 65.68%, which is 1.00 percentage point higher than the 64.68% achieved under unregulated operation. This improvement stems from optimised off-design flow-matching within compressors, which reduces the specific charging energy consumption to 549.33 kJ/kg and lowers the compressor exergy destruction ratio from 36.68% to 33.51%. By comparison, IGV regulation achieves a maximum volumetric energy storage density of 2.78 kWh/m 3 , representing a 0.72% increment over unregulated operation. This density advantage is attributed to an increase in the cumulative stored air mass and an elevated thermal storage temperature. A fundamental thermodynamic trade-off between RTE and storage density is revealed under different control strategies. The quantitative findings provide a rigorous decision-making framework for CAES operational optimization: speed regulation is preferable for efficiency-focused peak shaving, whereas IGV regulation is well-suited for capacity-constrained operational scenarios. The study offers actionable insights for enhancing the thermodynamic performance and grid integration of large-scale CAES systems.

title: A physics-informed causal learning framework for power consumption of logistics drones
abstract: Accurate modeling and causal analysis of logistics drone power consumption are essential for energy-efficient operations and mission planning. This study develops an integrated framework that combines high-accuracy power prediction with causal effect estimation using logistics drone data in Shenzhen, China. We propose a Transformer with Physics-Informed Manifold Mixup and Mode-Stratified Self-Distillation (PM2D-Transformer). This framework improves power prediction by generating physically consistent mixed samples within each flight mode, thereby reducing the influence of sparse and heterogeneous training data. Embedded within a Double/Debiased Machine Learning module, the model accurately estimates the heterogeneous causal effects of key variables on power consumption. Results demonstrate superior predictive performance relative to baseline models, while revealing complex causal patterns. The framework provides actionable insights for energy-aware flight control, operational scheduling and mission optimization.

title: TinyBatteryNet: A compact neural architecture for embedded battery remaining useful life prediction across battery domains
abstract: Early prediction of battery remaining useful life (RUL) is important for safe operation, maintenance, and second-life decisions, and for understanding how degradation information emerges in early charge/discharge waveforms. Existing deep prognostic models are often dataset-specific, provide limited evidence about which waveform scales and cycle intervals support their predictions, and exceed microcontroller memory budgets. We propose TinyBatteryNet, a 43,379-parameter architecture trained separately in each battery domain. It integrates a three-branch depthwise-separable convolutional pyramid, Squeeze-and-Excitation recalibration, a masked learnable cycle gate, and a gated recurrent unit to represent intra-cycle morphology and inter-cycle evolution. Beyond model compression, the novelty is its joint design for accuracy and embedded deployment, supported by controlled ablations and learned-weight diagnostics that examine where early-life information is expressed without assigning unsupported causal electrochemical mechanisms. Across 995 Li-ion, Zn-ion, Na-ion, and commercial CALB cells, TinyBatteryNet obtains mean absolute percentage errors of 0.170, 0.368, 0.232, and 0.133, respectively. These values are lower than the strongest reported BatteryLife baseline in each domain (11.9% average and 28.5% maximum relative reduction), although training recipes differ, and TinyBatteryNet uses 24–50 × fewer parameters. Ablations identify complementary receptive fields as the most consistently beneficial component, whereas channel recalibration and cycle weighting are domain-dependent. Thus, predictive behaviour reflects local-to-broad waveform morphology and non-uniform cycle relevance rather than a universal learned mechanism; the higher Zn-ion error further exposes limitations under irregular degradation. STM32F407VG target-mode validation reports 44.2 KB peak runtime RAM and 0.32 ms kernel inference, supporting MCU-level feasibility but not complete physical-board battery-management-system validation.

title: Optimal design and thermodynamic performance analysis of a novel isothermal reservoir supercritical compressed CO2 energy storage system
abstract: Supercritical compressed CO 2 energy storage system (SC-CCES) is a novel physical energy storage technology derived from compressed air energy storage (CAES) and S-CO 2 Brayton cycle. In particular, SC-CCES is characterized as a closed-type energy storage system, with low and high-pressure chambers interacting mutually during charging/discharging process. However, there is rare research of optimal design for SC-CCES, specifically achieving system architecture and eight initial storage parameters of low and high-pressure chambers, and its thermodynamic analysis and unsteady operating characteristics are also limited. To this end, a novel isothermal reservoir supercritical compressed CO 2 energy storage system is first proposed herein, for which high-pressure chamber maintains isothermal throughout the whole charging/discharging process. Furthermore, S-CO 2 release mechanism of high-pressure chamber (adiabatic/isothermal) and low-pressure chamber is achieved, and then optimal initial storage parameters of SC-CCES are obtained with the objective of maximizing storing/releasing S-CO 2 mass. Thermodynamic performance of SC-CCES based on adiabatic/isothermal mode of high-pressure chamber (SC-CCES-ASC and SC-CCES-ISC) are comprehensively compared. Results show that there is an optimal initial storage temperature of high/low pressure chambers when releasing maximum S-CO 2 mass, which rises with increasing initial storage pressure. Optimal eight initial storage parameters of low and high-pressure chambers for SC-CCES are achieved, specifically there is smaller optimal initial storage temperature (380 K) for SC-CCES-ISC with S-CO 2 releasing mass increasing by 39.8%. Furthermore, S-CO 2 compressor's speed and consumed power increase with improving the pressure ratio, while its mass flow rate decreases. By contrast, S-CO 2 turbine's speed, generated power and mass flow rate decrease with expansion ratio declining. Compared with SC-CCES-ASC, SC-CCES-ISC's energy charging period (1100 s versus 750 s)/energy discharging period (1809 s versus 1653 s) are longer, meanwhile S-CO 2 turbine's output power increases by 9.7%. It highlights that the round-trip efficiency of SC-CCES-ASC (achieving the maximum value of 69.7%) decreases with increasing initial storage temperature of high-pressure chamber, while its energy storage density presents the opposite trend. In particular, the round-trip efficiency of the SC-CCES-ISC first increases and then decreases with increasing initial storage temperature of high-pressure chamber, and its energy storage density gradually increases. Specifically, the round-trip efficiency of SC-CCES-ISC (24.3%) is lower than that of SC-CCES-ASC (69.7%), while SC-CCES-ISC presents higher energy storage density over SC-CCES-ASC (0.63 kWh/m 3 versus 0.36 kWh/m 3 ).

title: AC OPF learning via modular decomposition and adaptation to topology changes
abstract: We propose a novel framework for efficiently solving the AC optimal power flow (OPF) problem under varying grid topologies. Traditional learning-based approaches to OPF often retrain entire models when the network topology changes, leading to high computational cost and limited generalization. The proposed approach exploits the fact that different components of the OPF problem respond to topology changes to varying degrees: device-level operating limits remain largely unaffected, the network equations are modified locally around a tripped line, whereas the resulting optimal operating point may change throughout the network. It consists of two complementary training phases. In Phase I (modular pretraining), the OPF learning task under the intact grid topology is decomposed into three sequential subtasks (voltage setpoint prediction, power generation estimation, and generation cost computation) representing distinct functional mappings. In Phase II (adaptive learning), these pretrained modules are jointly fine-tuned for new topologies using a composite loss that combines supervised objectives with physics-informed regularization for branch-flow accuracy, nodal power balance, and operational constraint satisfaction. Extensive evaluations on benchmark grids demonstrate accurate predictions for the intact grid as well as for grids with seen and unseen contingencies. In our numerical experiments, at most 60 N − 1 contingency topologies are used for adaptation, and the largest mean prediction error among the reported variables under unseen topologies is approximately 3.1%.

title: Life cycle and techno-economic analysis of hydrogen-based ship propulsion concepts in light of future regulatory environments
abstract: The shipping sector faces ongoing challenges in developing pathways to net-zero emission concepts. Hydrogen as an energy carrier offers the opportunity to provide a low- to zero-emission solution, depending on the fuel production pathway. However, high production costs as well as logistical challenges in transporting the fuel globally hinder the economic competitiveness compared to current fossil fuel alternatives. To enable a faster adoption of zero-emission concepts, regulators such as the European Union and the International Maritime Organization have developed mechanisms that provide financial incentives and regulatory specifications. This paper investigates hydrogen-based propulsion concepts for the use case of a short-sea RoPax ferry and a deep-sea liquid hydrogen carrier. System models of different propulsion concepts are used to model their techno-economic performance under different well-to-tank hydrogen production and supply pathways. The proposed IMO GHG Fuel Intensity standards and corresponding penalties/incentives are included in the techno-economic comparison. Results are compared to a fossil-fueled baseline case and a battery-electric benchmark.

title: Tokenizing battery degradation: a physics-informed and uncertainty-aware framework for state-of-health estimation
abstract: Accurate and trustworthy estimation of State of Health (SOH) is essential for the safe and efficient operation of modern battery management systems. While data-driven methods have achieved high accuracy, they often lack physical grounding and fail to provide reliable confidence metrics for their predictions, posing risks in safety-critical applications. In this work, we introduce TBD-SOH, an SOH estimation framework that combines physics-informed feature construction with uncertainty-aware regression. Specifically, each charging cycle is represented as a fused cycle-level token constructed from two complementary sources: statistical descriptors of charging behavior and a hardware-free pseudo-impedance representation derived from routine voltage and current measurements in the frequency domain. The pseudo-impedance branch is introduced as a degradation-sensitive proxy rather than a direct electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurement. In addition, an MC dropout-based regression head is adopted to provide confidence intervals together with point estimates. Comprehensive experiments on the public MIT and HUST battery datasets demonstrate that TBD-SOH achieves high accuracy, outperforming conventional deep learning models. More importantly, its uncertainty estimates are shown to be dynamically responsive to prediction difficulty, and provide a new reference point for developing trustworthy and reliable battery health monitoring systems.

title: Using cross-regional grid interconnection to relieve growing energy storage demand in renewable energy integration: A case study from China
abstract: With the rapid growth of wind and solar generation, power systems face increasing balancing and energy storage needs. Cross-regional interconnection provides spatial flexibility through tie-line power exchange, yet the implications of tie-line scheduling flexibility for capacity planning remain insufficiently understood. This paper uses the Gansu–Shandong–Zhejiang interconnected system in China to quantify how tie-line scheduling timescales affect storage requirements for bulk energy shifting and system balancing. Within a common capacity planning and dispatch optimization framework, three stylized tie-line scheduling strategies are compared: Daily Fixed, Monthly Fixed, and Annual Fixed, representing decreasing levels of scheduling flexibility. Results show that greater tie-line scheduling flexibility changes the optimal capacity configuration, particularly the required battery energy storage (BES) capacity. Compared with Annual Fixed, Daily Fixed reduces BES capacity additions by 59.2% and total system cost by 22.8%. Sensitivity analyses further show that this advantage remains robust to variations in storage parameters and tie-line capacity. These findings indicate that the planning value of cross-regional interconnection depends substantially on its operational flexibility.

title: Risk-aware and network-compatible bidding of aggregated DER under energy-as-a-service model
Frequency security-aware production scheduling of utility-scale off-grid renewable P2H systems coordinating heterogeneous electrolyzers
abstract: Renewable power-to-hydrogen (ReP2H) enables large-scale renewable energy utilization and supports the decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors, such as chemicals and maritime transport, via hydrogen-based renewable ammonia and methanol fuels. As a result, utility-scale ReP2H projects are expanding worldwide. However, off-grid ReP2H systems exhibit low inertia due to their converter-dominated nature, making frequency security a critical concern. Although recent studies show that electrolyzers can contribute to frequency regulation (FR), their support capability depends on operating states and loading levels, creating a trade-off between hydrogen output and frequency security. To address this challenge, this work develops a unified co-optimization framework for frequency security-aware production scheduling of utility-scale off-grid ReP2H systems coordinating heterogeneous electrolyzers. A system-level frequency response model is established to capture multi-stage FR from alkaline water electrolyzers (AWEs), proton exchange membrane electrolyzers (PEMELs), and other resources, including ammonia-fueled generators retrofitted in co-located chemical plants, battery energy storage, and wind turbines (WTs). Stage-wise transient frequency security constraints are derived, reformulated into tractable forms, and embedded into production scheduling, enabling coordinated on/off switching and load allocation across electrolyzers to maximize hydrogen output under uncertain renewable power input while enforcing frequency security constraints. Case studies based on real-world systems demonstrate that the proposed approach allows hydrogen plants to replace 55.52% and 96.85% of FR reserves from WTs and AFGs, respectively, while improving the system-level net hydrogen yield by substantially reducing ammonia-fuel consumption. Year-long simulations show an average 28.96% increase in annual net profit resulting from reduced reliance on conventional reserves.

title: Self-regenerating photocatalytic water treatment systems: integrating cognitive AI control, bio-inspired self-healing, and thermoelectric energy harvesting
abstract: Conventional photocatalytic water treatment systems face persistent limitations in terms of catalyst deactivation, energy consumption, and adaptability to variable influent quality. This review examines the integration of three emerging technological domains, machine learning driven process optimization, bio-inspired self-healing material strategies, and thermoelectric energy recovery, as a framework for developing more autonomous and resource-efficient photocatalytic treatment systems. A systematic literature search was conducted in Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and PubMed (January 2001 to June 2024), following PRISMA guidelines. After multi-step screening, 104 peer-reviewed studies were included in the quantitative synthesis. Reviewed studies reported degradation efficiencies above 85% for model recalcitrant pollutants under optimized conditions. ML approaches, particularly artificial neural networks and ensemble methods, improved predictive accuracy of degradation kinetics by 20–35% relative to empirical models. Self-healing polymeric matrices retained catalytic activity exceeding 80% after repeated use cycles. Thermoelectric modules integrated in solar-driven reactors generated partial energy offsets under laboratory conditions, though full energy self-sufficiency has not yet been demonstrated at the pilot scale. Critical challenges remain, including long-term material stability under real wastewater conditions, scalability of digital twin architectures, and rigorous techno-economic validation. A research roadmap to address these barriers is proposed, with an emphasis on pilot-scale demonstration and standardized performance benchmarking.

title: A probability-box framework for quantifying office building air conditioning flexibility under multi-source uncertainty
abstract: Air conditioning systems are important flexible resources in buildings. However, their flexibility potential is highly uncertain due to unpredictable load disturbances caused by weather and occupancy variations. These uncertainties often lead to inconsistent load reduction outcomes, even when identical operating strategies are applied. To address the challenge of accurate quantification, this study proposes a probability box (P-box) model to characterize such potential under uncertainty. After defining the perturbation ranges and probability distributions of uncertain parameters, a stochastic load scenario generation method is employed, combining Monte Carlo sampling with Savitzky-Golay filtering to simulate multi-source disturbance conditions. The proposed P-box model is then evaluated for its prediction accuracy and adaptability based on these scenarios. The method is demonstrated using a calibrated office-building model in Tianjin under summer cooling conditions. Results show that under temperature reset and precooling strategies, the P-box model yields remarkably low prediction errors, the Wasserstein-based prediction achieves relative errors of 9.22% and 4.58% with respect to load reduction simulated under field-measured inputs, compared with 16.98% and 7.90% for the traditional deterministic methods. Moreover, the 100% P-box interval enveloped all evaluated samples, while narrower confidence intervals provided risk-dependent coverage, which accurately delineates the adjustable load range of buildings under multi-source disturbance conditions. This provides a reliable representation method for flexible resource scheduling and demand response strategy formulation.

title: Geopolitical energy shocks and consumer protection under fiscal constraints
abstract: How can energy-importing governments protect fuel-dependent households during geopolitical crises without suppressing conservation incentives or making unaffordable fiscal promises? We develop conditional insurance based on pre-crisis reference fuel consumption, with transfers independent of current purchases. Under stated assumptions, fixed payments preserve the marginal pump-price signal; a strictly concave allocation problem determines how to distribute scarce assistance. A dated liquidity rule prioritizes binding infrastructure guarantees and committed low-carbon investment before discretionary relief, and identifies the conditions under which protection must be rationed or financing fails. Guarantees require verified project-specific external losses and contractual caps. French monthly fuel-price analyses for 2020–2026, a longer exploratory global VAR, and a European synthetic-control comparison of France’s September 2022 intervention illustrate implementation. The latter captures a combined public–private discount and has low-powered donor placebos; it does not isolate the causal effect of the state rebate. Externally released geopolitical energy and macro surprises provide additional exploratory transmission diagnostics; their underlying structural model is not re-estimated and French event samples remain sparse. The framework offers conditional, auditable policy rules rather than a demonstrated universal welfare ranking or unconditional sovereign solvency.

title: Who leads the global gas market? Geopolitics and price transmission between the U.S. and Europe
Energy shocks, firm resilience, and policy responses: Evidence from the 2022 crisis*
abstract: The 2022 energy price shock, triggered by geopolitical disruptions, prompted governments to implement widespread policy interventions to support firms and accelerate the energy transition. Using nationally representative firm surveys from the United States and Germany, this paper examines how firms adjusted to the shock and their reported responses to fiscal incentives. We document that firms were generally resilient, relying on a combination of price pass-through, margin adjustment, and energy-saving investments. Responses differed across countries: firms in Germany – facing a larger and more persistent shock – were more likely to invest in energy efficiency and reduce energy consumption, while firms in the United States primarily absorbed costs through lower profits. Evidence from input-output simulations suggests that, absent policy intervention, energy-intensive sectors would have faced substantially larger price pressures. We also find that firms with pre-existing plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions were more likely to report intending to utilize fiscal incentive programs, suggesting that policy targeting and credibility may play an important role in supporting the green transition. Overall, our findings provide descriptive evidence on firms’ responses to energy price shocks and announced policy measures, offering insights for the design of targeted and predictable energy and climate policies in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical environment.

title: Multi-head actor-critic proximal policy optimization for coordinated control of EV charging and battery storage in PV-integrated microgrids
Passive anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation: From mechanisms to applications
abstract: Frost formation in low-temperature environments causes significant efficiency losses and safety hazards across aerospace, HVAC, and manufacturing industries. Conventional active anti-frosting methods suffer from poor energy efficiency due to periodic energy input requirements. This review summarizes recent advances in passive anti-frosting through interfacial humidity regulation—a strategy that inhibits ice crystal nucleation and growth by actively controlling local water vapor, offering substantial energy-saving potential. We firstly discuss theoretical models of ice nucleation in supersaturated vapor, examining how surface energy, microstructure, and chemistry govern interfacial humidity distribution and phase transitions. Secondly, three widely reported humidity regulating media, ice, hygroscopic gels, and hygroscopic liquids, are examined in terms of their vapor regulation mechanisms and frost suppression performance. Thirdly, we address advanced anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation via hygroscopic materials, biological protein and inspired microstructured surfaces. This review provides theoretical foundations and technical guidance for next-generation energy-efficient frost suppression technologies.

title: Maximising self-consumption in energy communities: a comparative study of demand flexibility and dynamic sharing strategies
New approach methodologies in nanomedicine: bridging the gap between in silico , in vitro , and in vivo systems
abstract: Rapid advances in biomedical research and nanomedicine have driven the development and implementation of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) for predictive evaluations of novel formulations.

title: Autonomous Biogenesis of Early and Late Assembly Intermediates of a Large Ribosomal Subunit in a Minimal System
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cell-free autonomous biogenesis of ribosomes is important for the bottom-up assembly of an artificial cell and for engineering of functional ribosomes with novel activities. The challenge lies in establishing conditions for a single-step multicomponent synthesis and assembly process in a minimal transcription–translation reaction. We previously reported autonomous synthesis and assembly of a bacterial small ribosomal subunit, but the assembly pathway of the large subunit is more complex with dozens of proteins that bind, fold, and chemically modify its ∼3000-base-long rRNA (rRNA). Here, we cosynthesized all the large subunit components including 33 ribosomal proteins (r-proteins) and 2 rRNAs from DNA brushes and followed the dynamics of assembly coupled to synthesis in real time using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy. A systematic screen of the binding of each of the ribosomal proteins to the 23S rRNA revealed an assembly pattern indicative of early intermediates. The addition of genes coding for six rRNA assembly factors facilitated binding of late assembly ribosomal proteins, supporting formation of late-stage intermediates even in the absence of rRNA modifications. We established a scenario for the large subunit biogenesis via macromolecular colocalization that may aid in the identification and characterization of additional genes required for achieving complete functional ribosome self-regeneration in a minimal system.

title: Unilateral Functionalization of Covalent Organic Frameworks: Local Electronic Modulation and Morphology-Enabled Mass Transport for Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Peroxide Production
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving high selectivity and activity in the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR) pathway critically depends on the synergistic modulation of a catalyst’s electronic structure and mass diffusion channels. This work proposes an asymmetric modulation strategy via unilateral functionalization, in which −CH3, −CN, −SO3H, and −NO2 moieties are incorporated into a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs), systematically unraveling the multilevel regulatory mechanisms exerted by functional groups from molecular to macroscopic morphological scales. The research demonstrates that introducing strong electron-withdrawing −NO2 groups can effectively enhance charge transfer at adjacent carbon active sites, reduce the formation barrier of OOH* intermediates, and induce efficient 2e– ORR activity. Concurrently, the polarity and steric effects of functional groups induce structural evolution in COFs from spherical, rod-like to spiderweb-like architectures, wherein the interconnected network of COF-NO2 substantially enhances the diffusion efficiency of reactants and products. This synergy between electronic structure and macroscopic morphology enables COF-NO2 to achieve 94% H2O2 selectivity and a high production rate of 10.5 mol gcat–1 h–1 with sustained stability. This work not only provides outstanding catalysts for efficient electrochemical H2O2 synthesis but also clarifies functional group-induced electronic and morphological modulation, offering a novel paradigm for the rational design of porous catalytic materials.

title: Excited-State Engineering of Viologen Photocatalysts via Synergistic Through-Space and Through-Bond Electronic Coupling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise manipulation of excited-state charge dynamics represents a fundamental challenge in the molecular design of organic photocatalysts. Herein, we introduce a synergistic electronic coupling strategy for engineering long-lived charge separation states by integrating through-space and through-bond electronic coupling in viologen-based photocatalysts. A family of through-space-conjugated viologens (TSCVs) featuring a dumbbell-shaped donor–acceptor architecture was constructed by integrating extended π-conjugated scaffolds with TSCV units. This unique architecture establishes an electronically cooperative framework that accelerates photoinduced charge separation, promotes charge delocalization, and suppresses charge recombination. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and theoretical investigations reveal that the synergistic coupling pathway enables persistent charge-separated excited states with enhanced charge-carrier utilization. Consequently, TSCV-T-c functions as a highly efficient metal-free photocatalyst for tandem C(sp3)-H functionalization/annulation of N,N-dimethylanilines with maleimides, affording tetrahydroquinoline products in yields up to 98%. Beyond demonstrating an effective photocatalytic system, this work establishes electronic coupling engineering as a molecular strategy for controlling excited-state dynamics and unlocking enhanced photocatalytic reactivity in organic semiconducting molecules.

title: Asymmetric Alkylation of α-Cyanoketimines with Alkyl Bromides Catalyzed by Bis-Cinchonium Salts
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The SN2 reaction constitutes one of the most fundamental bond-forming transformations in organic chemistry, finding numerous synthetic applications across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials science. However, the development of new catalysts for asymmetric SN2 reactions with nucleophiles beyond enolate derivatives remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the development of a new class of bis-cinchonium catalysts for an unprecedented enantioselective SN2 alkylation of cyanoketimines with alkyl bromides. This reaction features a broad substrate scope with respect to both reaction partners, thereby providing a useful approach to enantioenriched α,α-dialkyl aminonitriles. Computational studies revealed that the bis-cinchonium catalyst, through a network of weak bonding interactions, activated both cyanoketimines and alkyl bromides and preorganized them along the trajectory toward the transition state of an SN2 reaction.

title: A Standalone Flavoprotein Monooxygenase Directs Divergent Tropolone Skeletal Editing through Baeyer–Villiger-Triggered Rearrangement
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Late-stage oxidative remodeling of tropolone cores underpins the remarkable scaffold diversity in fungal meroterpenoid biosynthesis. However, the mechanistic basis by which a single enzymatic catalyst diverts a common substrate toward carbon-excising ring contraction versus carbon-retentive skeletal rearrangement remains elusive. Here, via comparative transcriptomics and targeted gene deletion, we identified a standalone host-encoded class A flavoprotein monooxygenase, ANIA_01821 (AN1821), as indispensable for tropolone ring remodeling in Aspergillus nidulans. A functionally homologous enzyme, AO090103000276 (AO276), from Aspergillus oryzae was further characterized as a tractable biocatalyst for in vitro studies. Reconstitution assays using purified AO276 revealed that this single flavoprotein monooxygenase alone converts the bistropolone meroterpenoid eupenifeldin into both ring-contracted phenolic products and carbon-retentive bridged polycycles, establishing a unified enzymatic origin for two structurally distinct natural-product scaffolds. Structure-guided mutagenesis uncovered a precisely organized electrostatic network that is critical for flavin-dependent oxygenation. Complementary well-tempered metadynamics simulations and quantum-chemical calculations support a Baeyer–Villiger branching mechanism, wherein the AO276 active site may preferentially stabilize alternative migration-competent conformations of a putative Criegee intermediate. Each conformation aligns a distinct C–C bond in an antiperiplanar geometry relative to the O–O bond; restricted conformational interconversion within the active site could preserve the initial reactive geometry and bias divergent carbon migration. Collectively, our findings identify conformational preorganization as a plausible contributor to regiodivergent enzymatic Baeyer–Villiger catalysis, offering a rational strategy for steering oxidative skeletal remodeling in complex natural product molecules.

title: High-Resolution 6Li Solid-State Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Reveals Hidden Lithium Dynamics in All-Solid-State Cathodes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The decisive chemistry of iron-based halide cathodes─where lithium resides, how it evolves, and how disorder governs multielectron redox─has remained largely inaccessible, limiting the rational design of catholyte-free composite cathodes in all-solid-state lithium batteries. Here we make the lithium sublattice directly visible in paramagnetic LiFeCl3 using a 6Li solid-state NMR strategy combining high isotopic enrichment, optimized acquisition, and variable-temperature control. This method resolves and quantifies three Li+ environments, revealing that local Li/Fe disorder drives in-place Fe2+ reduction as the root cause of highly reversible intercalation-conversion chemistry. It further uncovers trace irreversible Fe0 species invisible to conventional spectroscopic and imaging techniques. Guided by this hidden degradation signature, optimization of the voltage window enables 85.9% capacity retention after 500 cycles with a 16.3% energy-density penalty, whereas full-depth cycling retains 68.6% after 100 cycles. Our work establishes lithium-resolved NMR as a platform linking disorder, hidden redox, and reversibility in paramagnetic cathodes.

title: Construction of Divergent Enantioenriched 3D-Fluoro Scaffolds via Ni(0) π-Lewis Base-Mediated Umpolung of Fluorodienes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Enantioenriched three-dimensional (3D) fluorinated scaffolds are pivotal in drug discovery, whereas the asymmetric synthesis directly from readily available 2D fluoroalkenes represents a desirable yet challenging synthetic objective. The α-carbon of gem-difluoroalkenes is inherently electrophilic, which typically precludes their utility in nucleophilic assemblies. Herein, we report an umpolung strategy that utilizes low-valent Ni(0) as a π-Lewis base activator for gem-difluorodienes and leverages d → π* backdonation to effectively reverse their intrinsic electrophilicity, thereby enabling the addition to aldehydes and imines stereoselectively. Two distinct transformative pathways for the resultant difluoro π-allylnickel(II) species are developed: exclusively (Z)-defined defluorination and reductive coupling, finally furnishing chiral fluoroalkenyl and gem-difluoro homoallylic derivatives, respectively. In addition, stereodivergent control over vicinal fluorine-containing stereocenters is achievable under the identical catalysis, by simply using geometric isomers of 1-fluorodienes. The current Ni(0)-based umpolung paradigm of fluorodienes establishes a powerful framework for constructing structurally diverse and enantioenriched fluorinated compounds with pharmaceutical significance.

title: Interfacial Quantum States in ZrO2 Quantum Dots as a Strategy to Activate Photocatalytic Efficiency
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ultrasmall quantum dots (QDs) exhibit electronic behavior inaccessible to bulk counterparts, yet the role of structurally disordered interfaces remains unresolved, particularly in wide-band gap oxides. Herein, using the flame spray pyrolysis (FSP) technology, we engineered ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs comprising tetragonal ZrO2 QDs (2–5 nm) tightly interfaced with a semiamorphous, subnanometric ZrO2–x layer. Rather than forming a conventional heterojunction, electronic coupling between a {surface distorted hydroxylated ZrO2–x}, and the {quantum-confined crystalline core} generates shallow interfacial quantum states (IQS). This single-metal-oxide architecture elucidates the synergistic contributions of quantum confinement and interfacial states to photocatalytic H2 evolution. The ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs exhibit an unprecedented H2 production rate of 32,943 μmol g–1 h–1 and an apparent quantum yield of 3.49% at 252 nm, outperforming bulk-like ZrO2. Experimental results indicate that IQS activate otherwise photoinactive ZrO2, while density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate their origin and electronic character. Photoelectrochemical measurements reveal a negative shift in flat-band potential and enhanced interfacial charge conductivity. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy identifies a highly reduced, hydroxylated surface environment in the ZrO2 QDs, whereas electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) reveals that {ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs} form photoactive Zr3+ centers. Additionally, reversible photoinduced (g < 2) and (g > 2) signals consistent with electron and hole trapping, respectively. These findings establish IQS engineering as a novel interphase concept, beyond the quantum-dot limit, to promote charge separation and H2 evolution even in wide-band gap metal oxides. More broadly, coupling metal-oxide QDs with subnanometric, oxygen-deficient layers of the same metal offer a simple chemical route to activate otherwise inefficient oxide photocatalysts.

title: Solar Biorefinery: Stoichiometric Coproduction of Gluconic and Glucaric Acids and Impurity-Free Hydrogen from Lignocellulosic Biomass and Water
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Solar biorefinery serves as a game changer in the sustainable production of transportation fuels and value-added chemicals by capitalizing on sunlight, lignocellulosic biomass, and water. Central to this endeavor is the modulation of highly reactive, nonselective hydroxyl radicals to prevent undesired side reactions. Here, surface-hydroxylated nickel oxyphosphide works synergistically with one-dimensional gallium nitride, enabling the selective reforming of lignocellulose in water toward glucose-derived organic acids (GOAs: gluconic and glucaric acids) and H2 at a nearly stoichiometric ratio: (C6H12O6)n+ H2O + sunlight → GOAs + H2. The GaN@NiOP–OH system achieves an H2 evolution rate of 2.55 mol g–1 h–1 with 100% gas-phase selectivity under simulated concentrated sunlight at 3.5 W cm–2. GOAs are simultaneously produced at a total rate of 2.23 mol g–1 h–1, corresponding to a near-stoichiometric GOAs/H2 ratio of 0.97 with nearly 100% atom utilization efficiency. This platform is broadly applicable to sunlight-driven reforming of cellulose, straw, and camphorwood. In situ spectroscopy, isotope labeling, and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that NiOP–OH cooperates with GaN to modulate in situ-generated hydroxyl radical species originating from water oxidation by photogenerated holes. These radicals are confined on the catalytic surface with their nonselective reactivity finely tuned, enabling selective conversion of glucose with H2O into GOAs and H2 via a dynamic hydroxyl exchange mechanism while suppressing side and mineralization reactions. Outdoor testing and techno-economic analysis confirm the practical viability of this proof-of-concept solar biorefinery for coproducing high-value chemicals and green H2 using only sunlight, lignocellulose, and water.

title: Nearly half of reef-building corals face elevated relative risk of extinction
abstract: Coral reefs are diverse marine ecosystems that provide ecological functions and economic and social benefits across over 100 tropical countries. Warming driven by climate change is a primary threat to coral reefs and is increasing the frequency of global coral bleaching events. Here we reassessed the IUCN Red List status of 892 reef-building coral species, first assessed in 2008 1. Because species-level population trends are unavailable for most reef-building corals, population reductions were inferred using proxies based on global coral cover trends and projected annual severe bleaching under SSP2-4.5, both over three decades, adjusted using trait-based estimates of species vulnerability. Of the 774 species with sufficient data to be assessed, 340 (44%) were classified as threatened under IUCN Red List criteria. Thirty-three species were assessed as Critically Endangered, 251 as Endangered, and 56 as Vulnerable, most due to risk of population reduction associated with projected thermal stress. These findings predate the three hottest years on record and the fourth global coral bleaching event (2023-2025), and the first exceedance for an annual mean of the 1.5oC global warming threshold. The findings reinforce the importance of limiting further warming to maintain coral biodiversity and reef ecosystem function. The Red List assesses the relative extinction risk of species, whereby species are placed in categories of increasing risk by comparing their population size, decline and geographic range against standardised thresholds. The Red List does not predict whether or when a species may go extinct. As the ranges of coral species remain under-surveyed, future assessments would be strengthened by species-level population data and thermal-stress and recovery metrics that better capture range-representative dynamics.

title: Beyond nature: charting the roadmap to intelligent biomanufacturing for sustainable biohydrogen
abstract: Hydrogen has been recognized as a key pillar of future energy systems in the global pursuit of carbon neutrality. However, hydrogen production processes still highly rely on fossil fuels. Biohydrogen production is a microbial-based process that converts biomass, organic waste, and solar energy into hydrogen via dark fermentation, photo-fermentation, or photolytic water-splitting pathways. It is a promising pathway to sustainable energy, with the potential for carbon-negative emissions under favorable feedstock and system-boundary conditions. Yet, the limitations of natural biological systems, such as poor energy conversion efficiency, huge carbon diversion, and poor operational robustness, have prevented its transition from laboratory research to industrial application. To resolve these bottlenecks, this review proposes a strategic shift from traditional biological conversion toward intelligent biomanufacturing via three enabling technologies: (1) synthetic biology to design microbial cell factories with a tailored hydrogen-centric metabolism; (2) nanomaterials engineering to create smart biotic-abiotic interfaces for overcoming the physical limitations of electron and mass transfer; and (3) artificial intelligence to enable autonomous bioprocessing through predictive digital twins and self-optimizing reactor systems. These three pillars can bridge molecular-scale engineering to system-level intelligence. A scalable roadmap starting from modular bioreactor design, waste-derived feedstock integration, and rigorous techno-economic and life-cycle assessment has been outlined to position biohydrogen within circular economy and potentially carbon-negative ecosystems. This review suggests a pathway to make biohydrogen an important, efficient, cost-effective, and reliable building block of the future hydrogen economy.

title: Two clusters of brain regions with distinct age-related profiles of functional connectivity in autism spectrum disorder
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Brain functional connectivity changes throughout development, and individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may follow trajectories that differ from those of typically developing controls. Using large multisite resting-state fMRI cross-sectional datasets, we examined how functional connectivity differences between ASD and typically developing controls change across a broad age range of 5 to 64 y. A data-driven analysis identified two spatially distributed clusters of cortical regions showing distinct age-related profiles of ASD–TD connectivity differences. Cluster 1 was marked by consistent hypoconnectivity across ages, suggesting a stable neural signature of ASD. Cluster 2 was characterized by hypoconnectivity in childhood that gradually diminished with age, suggesting a temporary delay profile. These clusters were systematically organized along the sensory–association axis. Cluster 1 mainly involved lower-rank sensory and sensorimotor cortices, while Cluster 2 mainly involved higher-rank association cortices. Brain–behavior analyses revealed greater and broader ASD symptom associations across ages in the consistent hypoconnectivity profile than the delay profile. Further subtype analyses suggested that social-affect symptoms were associated with greater hypoconnectivity than repetitive behavior symptoms in both clusters. Spatial correlation analyses with neurotransmitter maps revealed associations of Cluster 1 with mGluR5 and of Cluster 2 with GABA A α5, providing insight into the neurobiological basis of the two clusters. In a cross-disorder validation analysis, applying the same analytic framework to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder did not reveal comparable results. Together, these findings suggest that ASD-related functional connectivity alterations are developmentally heterogeneous and organized along the cortical hierarchy, providing a developmental perspective for understanding the neurobiology of ASD.

title: Rotation‐Coupled Guest Anions Stabilize Polymer Solid‐State Sodium‐Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries are constrained by sluggish Na + migration and unstable sodium–metal interfaces, both of which are closely associated with poorly regulated solvation chemistry. Here we report a rotation‐coupled guest‐anion strategy in a poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene)‐based solid‐state electrolyte (PHSE) using Mg(OTf) 2 . Mg 2+ preferentially coordinates DMF and TFSI − , weakening Na + –TFSI − association and limiting solvent‐derived reactions at the sodium metal anode. OTf − enters the Na + solvation shell as a mobile guest anion. Its C─S rotational axis and equivalent oxygen coordination sites allow conformational rotation to synchronize with Na + hopping along polymer chains. This anchor–rotator chemistry reorganizes Na + coordination, lowers the migration barrier, and promotes an inorganic‐rich, Mg─O‐containing interphase. The optimized electrolyte enables Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 ||Na cells to retain 94.2% capacity after 1100 cycles at 2C and supports a 94 mAh pouch cell with stable cycling. It also enables high‐voltage Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 O 2 F||Na cells to retain 93.6% capacity after 1000 cycles at 0.5C over 2.5–4.2 V. Comparative evaluation across a total of 20 polymer electrolyte systems with varied polymer matrices and anion structures identifies anion symmetry, rotational periodicity, and finite rotational barriers as molecular criteria for designing stable polymer solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries.

title: Efficient Bipolar Hydrogen Peroxide Production Through Photoelectrochemistry
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is a crucial environmentally benign oxidant. Photoanodes in bias‐free photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems suffer from poor H 2 O 2 selectivity at low potentials, limiting the efficiency of bipolar H 2 O 2 production. Herein, we report a rare‐earth ytterbium oxide (YbO x ) modified BiVO 4 /WO 3 photoanode for efficient PEC water oxidation to H 2 O 2 . The optimized photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 4.83 mA cm −2 at 1.23 V RHE , an H 2 O 2 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of over 80% across the potential range of 0.6–1.8 V RHE , and a peak FE of 90.4% at 1.6 V RHE . Yb 3+ Lewis acid sites suppress the competitive four‐electron oxygen evolution reaction by forming Yb‐hydroxyl complexes, while YbO x enhances charge transfer and reduces interfacial resistance. Importantly, when coupled with a FeZnWMnYb high‐entropy amorphous oxide cathode for the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction, the bias‐free tandem cell achieves ∼160% bipolar H 2 O 2 FE. Scaling the photoelectrode to 20 cm 2 under 0.7 suns illumination yields an H 2 O 2 production rate of 3.03 mmol L −1 h −1 . This work demonstrates a viable strategy for large‐scale solar‐driven H 2 O 2 synthesis for environmental applications.

title: Radical‐Mediated Surface Reconstruction of SnO 2 Nanocrystals Enables Efficient and Durable Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
abstract: ABSTRACT Charge‐transport layers fundamentally dictate interfacial recombination, carrier extraction, and operational stability in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet scalable routes to simultaneously regulate their colloidal stability and defect chemistry remain elusive. Here, we report a radical‐mediated surface reconstruction strategy for ligand‐free SnO 2 nanocrystals that enables concurrent gains in device efficiency, scalability, and durability. Sonochemical activation generates hydroxyl radicals that selectively passivate oxygen‐deficient Sn sites while inducing electrostatically stabilized dispersions with exceptional shelf stability, allowing the SnO 2 colloids to be stored for over 2 years without aggregation or performance degradation. This stabilization enables the formation of uniform electron transport layers with reduced trap density and enhanced electron mobility. These improvements promote buried‐interface perovskite crystallization and accelerate charge extraction, yielding PSCs with an efficiency of 26.47% (certified 26.12%). Importantly, the strategy is inherently scalable, enabling a perovskite module (∼110 cm 2 ) with an efficiency of 21.45%. Devices exhibit enhanced operational stability, retaining 92% efficiency after 1000 h thermal aging (ISOS‐D‐2), maintaining 88% efficiency under maximum power point tracking (ISOS‐L‐1), and showing negligible degradation over 500 thermal cycles (ISOS‐T‐3). These results establish radical‐mediated engineering of SnO 2 nanocrystals as a general pathway in perovskite photovoltaics, bridging high efficiency, large‐area manufacturability, and long‐term operational stability.

title: Chiralizing Covalent Organic Frameworks to Boost H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven H 2 O 2 photosynthesis offers a sustainable route to on‐site oxidant production, yet the selective reduction of triplet O 2 to spin‐paired H 2 O 2 remains kinetically challenging. Covalent organic framework (COF) photocatalysts have largely focused on charge separation and active‐site reactivity, while overlooking the spin character of electrons transferred to O 2 . Here we discover that chiralization renders COFs significantly enhanced production of H 2 O 2 , and report a chiralization strategy for spin‐regulated H 2 O 2 photosynthesis in β‐ketoenamine‐linked COFs. The chiral frameworks enable spin‐selective electron transport, favor the O–O‐bond‐preserving reduction pathway and lower the apparent kinetic barrier for H 2 O 2 formation. Chiralization enhances H 2 O 2 production by 38.7%–252.1% relative to achiral counterparts. A bipyridine‐containing chiral COF reaches 22.8 mmol g −1 h −1 using solely water and oxygen, with an apparent quantum yield of 10.3% at 420 nm, placing it at the forefront of sacrificial‐agent‐free COF systems. Membrane‐integrated chiral COFs enable continuous‐flow H 2 O 2 production. These findings establish chirality as a design parameter coupling spin‐selective electron transport with O 2 reduction pathway control, opening new directions for COF photocatalysis.

title: Synthesis of gem ‐Phosphorylsilylalkenes Bearing Si/Si,P‐Stereogenic Centers by Regio‐ and Enantio‐Selective Pd‐Catalyzed Hydrosilylation
abstract: ABSTRACT The catalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral molecules containing both silicon‐ and phosphorus‐stereogenic centers represents a highly attractive yet underexplored domain in synthetic chemistry, largely due to the considerable challenge associated with the simultaneous control of two distinct stereogenic elements. Herein, we disclose a palladium‐catalyzed enantioselective hydrosilylation that enables the construction of a C(sp 2 )─Si bond, affording a regioselective route to gem ‐phosphorylsilylalkenes bearing contiguous Si‐ and P‐stereocenters. This transformation operates through a synergistic combination of desymmetrization of dihydrosilanes and diastereomeric resolution (DR) of unsymmetrical and racemic alkynylphosphoryl substrates, in which a diverse array of silicon‐stereogenic gem ‐phosphorylsilylalkenes and their structural analogues bearing additional P‐stereogenic centers in good yields and high enantioselectivities (up to 98:2 er). Furthermore, the synthetic utility of this methodology is underscored by the concise preparation of structurally diverse organosilicon frameworks. Mechanistic investigations, supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, have been performed to delineate the reaction pathway and rationalize the observed regio‐ and enantioselectivity.

title: “Direct Injection” Bubble Growth Mediated by Nano‐Interfaced Electrodes for Efficient Chlorine Production
abstract: ABSTRACT The chlor‐alkali industry, with the chlorine evolution reaction (CER) as its core anodic process, accounts for nearly 4% of global electricity consumption. The development of energy‐efficient and stable CER system is therefore urgently needed. Nano‐interfaced electrodes exhibit superior catalytic performance, yet their mechanism for energy saving and system stability remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine a high‐speed camera and confocal laser scanning microscope Platform to visualize and digitalize the bubble evolution and the bubble‐induced overpotential ( ƞ bub ). We provide direct visual evidence that the bubble‐induced concentration gradients and fluid flow field disturbances are key regulators of overpotential, and that the nano‐interfaced electrode exhibits an ƞ bub of only approximately 49% of that of the flat‐interfaced electrode. Specifically, the nano interface not only generates a stronger interfacial electric field and enhanced bubble‐induced interfacial turbulence—which promote the Cl − migration to the electrode surface—but also induces a “direct‐injection” mode of bubble growth that mitigates the accumulation of reaction products near the electrode. Moreover, the Cl − enrichment capacity of the nano interface endows the near‐interface solution with ionic buffering capability, effectively suppressing potential fluctuations. This work demonstrates that regulating bubble dynamics is key to constructing energy‐saving and stable gas‐evolving electrochemical systems.

title: Crystallography‐Dependent Plating/Stripping Kinetics and Interfacial Morphologies in Zn Metal Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Crystallographic orientation governs Zn deposition, dissolution, and cycling stability, but its influence on interfacial charge‐transfer kinetics remains difficult to quantify. Here, scanning electrochemical cell microscopy coupled with fast scan cyclic voltammetry (FSCV) is used to resolve Zn plating and stripping on single‐crystal (002), (100), and (101) surfaces. Meniscus‐confined measurements reveal facet‐dependent branch‐specific apparent zero‐current potentials and apparent exchange current densities, j 0 , with the kinetic ordering j 0 (100) > j 0 (101) > j 0 (002) for both plating and stripping. This ordering is reproduced across independently prepared electrodes and retained over different scan rates and aqueous electrolytes. Beyond charge transfer, Zn removal and regrowth are strongly crystallographically encoded: dissolution footprints preserve the symmetry of the parent facets, while potentiostatically deposited Zn adopts substrate‐dependent growth geometries. These coupled kinetic and morphological differences translate directly to battery performance. Despite its slower apparent kinetics, the close‐packed, low‐energy (002) facet exhibits the longest cycling life in Zn/Zn symmetric cells and substantially improved capacity retention in both polyaniline/Zn and Na 0.33 V 2 O 5 /Zn full cells, whereas the faster (100) and (101) interfaces fail earlier. These findings establish a facet‐dependent kinetics–stability trade‐off and show that durable Zn anodes require coordinated control of charge transfer, dissolution topology, and crystallographic reconstruction.

title: Redirecting Excited‐State Energy Flow Through Programmed Supramolecular Confinement in Twisted Photosensitizers
abstract: ABSTRACT Programmed supramolecular confinement is introduced as a physical strategy to investigate aggregation‐enhanced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation in twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT)‐active twisted photosensitizers without changing the conjugated photosensitizing unit. In this design, TICT functions as a confinement‐sensitive regulator of excited‐state energy dissipation, while cell membranes (CM) serve as supramolecular platforms that confine photosensitizers within their compact phospholipid bilayer architectures. Through alkyl‐chain engineering, the obtained photosensitizers exhibit similar photophysical properties but tunable interactions with phospholipids, resulting in programmed confinement states within CMs. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that supramolecular confinement suppresses TICT‐mediated non‐radiative relaxation by reducing excitation‐induced donor‐acceptor torsional change and restricting intramolecular rotation, thereby redirecting excited‐state energy flow toward radiative emission and intersystem crossing‐mediated ROS generation. Accordingly, stronger confinement induces higher enhancements in fluorescence and ROS generation, establishing a supramolecular confinement‐dependent correlation among TICT restriction, fluorescence, and ROS generation. Finally, the optimized CM‐photosensitizer assemblies are applied as photodynamic systems and display effective performance in cancer immunotherapy. By coupling TICT restriction with ROS generation, this work establishes supramolecular confinement as a physical strategy for redirecting excited‐state energy flow and provides direct insight into how aggregation enhances ROS generation in twisted photosensitizers.

title: Metal‐Center‐Controlled Fenton‐Like Reactivity of Biomimetic First‐Row Transition Metal Complexes in Aqueous Anticancer Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Catalytic oxidative cancer therapy exploits elevated hydrogen peroxide levels within tumor microenvironments to induce selective oxidative damage in malignant cells. However, many ROS‐generating therapeutic systems rely on heavy metals or structurally complex inorganic architectures, limiting their biological compatibility and catalytic selectivity. Inspired by nonheme iron‐mediated redox catalysis, we report a series of water‐soluble biomimetic first‐row transition metal complexes supported by a picolylamine‐derived nonheme ligand scaffold bearing a pendant hydroxyl group. Systematic variation of the metal center (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn) generated divergent electrochemical behavior and distinct peroxide‐activation reactivity, yet only the iron complex, [Fe(N 2 Py 3 OH)] 2+ ( 1‐Fe ), promoted hydroxyl radical formation via Fenton‐like hydrogen peroxide activation in water. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and crystallographic analyses revealed a biomimetic coordination environment that stabilizes a quasi‐reversible Fe(II)/Fe(III) redox couple suited to catalytic peroxide activation. In gastric cancer cells, 1‐Fe induced intracellular oxidative stress, mitochondrial depolarization, lipid peroxidation, and concomitant apoptosis and ferroptosis, while exhibiting negligible toxicity toward normal fibroblasts. In combination with paclitaxel, 1‐Fe produced synergistic antiproliferative activity in vitro and suppressed peritoneal tumor dissemination in vivo without overt systemic toxicity. Collectively, these results establish biomimetic iron complexes as molecular platforms for Fenton‐like oxidative catalysis in redox‐based cancer therapy.

title: Integrated Antigen–DNA Co‐Detection Using Digital Microfluidics for Improving Diagnostic Accuracy in POCT Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Simultaneous detection of protein and nucleic acid (NA) provides complementary information essential for accurate analysis of complex samples. Conventional approaches for the analysis of protein and NA typically rely on separate workflows and instruments, limiting the reliability of point‐of‐care testing. Here, we present a digital microfluidics‐based dual‐mode molecular assay for simultaneous detection of both protein and NA from the same microscale sample. The protein is captured by a gold nanoparticle–antibody conjugate, while NA is enriched by magnetic beads. Magnetic manipulation separates the protein‐containing fraction from NA, enabling separate analysis of the two molecular classes within an automated workflow. By integrating the analysis of protein and NA, the platform enables more accurate analysis than either modality alone. In 56 clinical samples, the combined analysis of hepatitis B surface antigen and DNA reduces the false‐negative rate to 1.79%, compared with 12.5% for HBsAg alone. In food safety assays, simultaneous detection of Staphylococcus aureus ‐associated toxins and PMA‐treated bacterial NA provides information not only on protein‐based toxins, but also the presence and viability of bacteria within milk. This automated DMF‐based dual‐mode molecular assay provides a highly integrated strategy for multimodal POCT and public health risk assessment.

title: Mechanophotochemistry : Lighting up EDA Complexes in the Solid State
abstract: ABSTRACT Solvent arguably constitutes the single largest waste stream in synthesis. Mechanophotocatalysis , a synergistic union of mechanochemistry and photocatalysis, offers a solution to significantly reduce solvent use in photochemistry. Here, we show how photochemical reactions in the solid state can be driven by visible light using in situ formed electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes in air, obviating the need for an external photocatalyst. Under the optimized conditions, only 2–4 equiv. of solvent is used as a liquid‐assisted grinding (LAG) agent, thus significantly reducing solvent use. We demonstrate EDA mechanophotochemistry across five reactions: a Giese reaction; a C─S cross‐coupling reaction; a phosphorylation reaction; a sulfonylation reaction; and a Povarov reaction. While the first four proceeded readily and competitively with the solution‐state EDA photochemical reaction, the latter one, requiring O 2 as a terminal oxidant, does not. In investigating the sulfonylation reaction we further identify the first example of a photomechanoredox reaction in which the stainless‐steel milling ball directly participates in the reaction, revealing the milling medium as a previously unrecognized reactivity parameter. Together, these results establish visible light‐promoted mechanophotochemistry as a solvent‐minimized and viable alternative to solution‐state photochemical reactions.
